section.title: Okuma evi 3
section.description: YÖKDİL alan okuması: fen, sağlık ve sosyal bilimlerde 64 özgün metin, terim yoğun uzun cümleler ve paragraf soruları; arada yarım denemeler 6–8

units.title: Terim yoğun metinde ana fikir
units.description: Fen metinleri: bilinmeyen terimleri geç, yazarın iddiasını bul
units.guide:
## Strateji
Terim yoğun bir fen metninde (perovskit, nötron yıldızı, metalik cam…) her terimi bilmek zorunda değilsin. Ana fikir sorusu terimin tanımını değil, yazarın o terim hakkında **ne iddia ettiğini** sorar. Bilinmeyen terimi bir harf gibi düşün (X); iddiayı cümlenin iskeleti ve değerlendirme sözcükleri taşır.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Bilmediğin terimi işaretle ve geç: *X is highly sensitive to moisture* → "X neme duyarlı".
2. Her paragrafın ilk ve son cümlesinden 2–3 kelimelik bir etiket çıkar.
3. Dönüş sözcüklerini işaretle: *however, that said, nevertheless, as such*. Bunlardan sonra çoğu zaman yazarın asıl yargısı gelir.
4. İddiayı "konu + yazarın yargısı" biçiminde tek cümleyle yaz.
5. Şıklarda üç tuzağı ele: tek bir ayrıntı (*dar*), metinde olmayan genelleme (*geniş*), terimleri doğru kullanıp yargıyı tersine çeviren cümle (*çarpıtma*).

## Örnek
*Ferrofluids are composed of microscopic iron oxide particles. They are exploited in loudspeakers and vacuum seals. Medical uses, however, remain experimental.*
- "ferrofluid" bilinmese de iddia açık: X birçok teknolojide kullanılıyor, tıpta henüz deneme aşamasında.
- "Ferrofluids are now routine in medicine" → çarpıtma.
- "The particles are microscopic" → dar.

## Sınav ipucu
YÖKDİL fen metinlerinde terim sayısı seni yavaşlatmasın. Ana fikir çoğunlukla terimlerin çevresindeki sıradan sözcüklerdedir: *remain, limit, promising, uncertain, valuable*. Önce bu yargı sözcüklerini bul, terimlere ancak soru isterse dön.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Perovskites have already replaced silicon as the main material in commercial solar panels.
The crystal structure of perovskites was first identified by a research group in Japan in 2009.
Perovskites have quickly matched silicon in efficiency, but their stability and lead content still limit their commercial use.
Silicon panels are cheaper to make than perovskite cells because they are processed at lower temperatures.
Lead-free perovskites have proved more efficient than any other material used in solar cells.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Perovskites have quickly matched silicon in efficiency, but their stability and lead content still limit their commercial use’: metin hızlı verim artışını anlatıp ‘That said’ ile dayanıklılık ve kurşun sorununa döner; iddia budur. ‘replaced’ yanlış, silisyum pazara hâlâ hâkim. ‘Japan’ seçeneği karıştırıyor: yapı Rusya’da bulunan bir mineralden adını alır, 2009 yalnızca ilk güneş pilidir. ‘cheaper’ seçeneği tersini söylüyor: düşük sıcaklıkta işlenen perovskittir. ‘Lead-free’ türlerin en verimli olduğu metinde yok.
exercises.passage:
Over the past fifteen years, few materials have attracted as much scrutiny from energy researchers as the perovskites. This family of compounds takes its name from a mineral found in Russia in the nineteenth century, whose crystalline structure it shares. The name refers to a particular arrangement of atoms rather than to a single chemical recipe, which means that many different elements can be combined within the same basic lattice. In 2009, a group in Japan reported that a lead-based perovskite could act as the light-absorbing layer of a solar cell, although the device converted only about four per cent of sunlight into electricity.

Since then, progress has been remarkably rapid. Laboratory cells made from these semiconductors now reach efficiencies of more than 25 per cent, a figure that is comparable to that of the silicon panels which dominate the photovoltaic market today. Unlike silicon, which must be purified and processed at very high temperatures, perovskite layers can be spread from a liquid solution at relatively low temperatures, and this is expected to reduce manufacturing costs considerably. When a thin perovskite film is placed on top of a conventional silicon cell, the combined device can absorb a wider range of wavelengths, and such double-layer cells have exceeded 30 per cent in controlled experiments.

That said, the commercial future of the technology remains uncertain. Perovskites are highly sensitive to moisture, heat and even long exposure to light, so their performance can decline within months, whereas silicon panels are usually guaranteed for about 25 years. Questions of toxicity have also been raised, since most of the efficient versions contain small amounts of lead, which could escape into the soil if damaged panels were not properly collected. Many investigators therefore argue that the decisive measure is no longer peak efficiency but durability, and a considerable share of current work is devoted to protective coatings, such as thin oxide layers, and to lead-free alternatives that may prove more stable.

exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that perovskite panels would become far more attractive commercially if ----.
options: their peak efficiency rose slightly above 25 per cent
they were processed at the same high temperatures as silicon
more lead were added to protect them from moisture
they absorbed a narrower range of wavelengths
they could keep their performance for many years outside the laboratory
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘they could keep their performance for many years outside the laboratory’: yazar asıl ölçünün artık en yüksek verim değil dayanıklılık olduğunu söylüyor. ‘peak efficiency’ zaten 25’i aşmış ve belirleyici değil. ‘high temperatures’ maliyet avantajını ortadan kaldırır. ‘more lead’ zehirlilik sorununu büyütür. ‘narrower’ daha az ışık emmek demektir, avantaj değil.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Helium was first isolated in a laboratory and only later detected in the Sun.
Helium was identified from a line in the Sun's spectrum long before it was found on Earth, which shows the power of spectroscopy.
Sodium and helium produce exactly the same yellow line in a spectrum.
Helium is the most common element on Earth because it forms deep underground.
Janssen travelled to India in order to prove that the Moon produces its own light.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Helium was identified from a line in the Sun’s spectrum long before it was found on Earth, which shows the power of spectroscopy’: metin 1868’deki çizgiden 1895’teki doğrulamaya uzanır ve son cümlede spektroskopinin gücünü vurgular. ‘isolated’ seçeneği sırayı tersine çeviriyor. ‘exactly’ yanlış; çizgi sodyumunkine yakın ama ölçülebilir biçimde farklıydı. ‘most common element on Earth’ yanlış; evrende ikinci en yaygın elementtir, Dünya’da ise kolayca kaçar. ‘Moon produces’ metinde yok.
exercises.passage:
In August 1868, the French astronomer Jules Janssen travelled to India to study the glowing gas at the edge of the Sun, which becomes visible only when the Moon covers the bright disc. Passing the light collected by his telescope through a prism, he recorded its spectrum, the band of colours in which every chemical element leaves its own pattern of narrow lines. Among the lines he saw was a bright yellow one. A few months later, the same line was observed in London by the English astronomer Norman Lockyer, who had developed a method of studying the Sun's edge on ordinary days.

The puzzle lay in the precise position of this line. It was close to, but measurably different from, the well-known pair of yellow lines produced by sodium, and no element that had been identified in the laboratory could account for it. Lockyer, working partly with the chemist Edward Frankland, therefore proposed that the Sun contained an element unknown on Earth, which he named helium after the Greek word for the Sun. Many chemists treated the claim with considerable scrutiny, since an element that had never been isolated seemed little more than a presumption based on a single line.

Confirmation came only in 1895, when the Scottish chemist William Ramsay released a gas from a uranium mineral and found that its spectrum showed exactly the same yellow line. It is known today that helium is the second most common element in the universe, and that on Earth it forms mainly from the particles released during radioactive decay deep underground. Because it is so light and chemically inert, it escapes easily into space once it reaches the atmosphere, which explains why it had been so hard to detect. As such, the story illustrates how spectroscopy allowed scientists to identify an element in a distant star decades before they could hold it in their hands.

exercises.question: According to the passage, Lockyer concluded that the yellow line came from a new element because ----.
options: it could be seen only when the Moon covered the Sun
it did not match the lines of any element identified in the laboratory
it was exactly the same as the pair of lines produced by sodium
Ramsay had already released the gas from a uranium mineral
it was much brighter than every other line in the spectrum
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘it did not match the lines of any element identified in the laboratory’: ‘no element that had been identified in the laboratory could account for it’ cümlesi nedeni verir. ‘only when the Moon’ yanlış; Lockyer çizgiyi sıradan günlerde gözlemleyebiliyordu. ‘exactly the same’ metne ters. ‘Ramsay’ yanlış; onun deneyi 1895’te, yani sonra yapıldı. ‘brighter’ parlaklık karşılaştırması metinde yok.

nodes.title: Fen: Metalik cam ve piezoelektrik
nodes.description: Metin 1: Kristalsiz metaller. Metin 2: Sıkıştırılınca elektrik üreten kristaller. ys9 kelimeleri: experimentation, investigator, magnetism, crystalline, brittle, malleable, corrosion, lattice ve 14 kelime daha; ys7 kelimeleri: core, confine, defect, elastic, rough ve 16 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Metallic glass is weaker than ordinary steel because its atoms are arranged in a regular lattice.
Crystal boundaries make metals perfect, so engineers try to create as many of them as possible.
Metallic glass is now widely used to build large structures such as bridges and buildings.
The first metallic glass was produced by slowly cooling pure gold over several days.
Because metallic glass lacks a crystal structure, it has unusual strengths, but its size and brittleness still restrict its use.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Because metallic glass lacks a crystal structure, it has unusual strengths, but its size and brittleness still restrict its use’: metin önce kristalsiz yapının getirdiği üstünlükleri, sonra boyut ve kırılganlık sınırlarını anlatır. ‘weaker’ yanlış; bazı türleri çelikten iki kat güçlü ve düzenli kafes yoktur. ‘perfect’ yanlış; sınırlar çatlamanın başladığı yerlerdir. ‘bridges’ metne ters; kullanım küçük parçalarla sınırlı. ‘slowly’ yanlış; saniyede yaklaşık bir milyon derece hızla soğutulmuştur.
exercises.passage:
Most metals are crystalline: as they cool from a molten state, their atoms settle into a regular, repeating lattice, much like oranges stacked neatly on a market stall. This orderly structure is never perfect, however, and the boundaries between small crystals, together with the defects inside them, are the points at which a malleable metal usually begins to bend permanently or to crack. In 1960, investigators in California found, somewhat unexpectedly, that if certain alloys of gold and silicon were cooled extremely quickly, at roughly a million degrees per second, the atoms had no time to arrange themselves. Instead, they remained frozen in the random pattern of a liquid, and the solid that resulted had no crystal structure at all.

This material, which became known as metallic glass, combines properties that are rarely found together. Because it has no crystal boundaries, some versions can be about twice as strong as conventional steel while remaining remarkably elastic, so that they spring back to their original shape after considerable stress. It also offers good resistance to corrosion, and its unusually soft magnetism makes it useful in the cores of electrical transformers, where it reduces the energy that is wasted as heat. Some sports equipment manufacturers have used it in golf clubs, claiming that more of the energy of a swing is transferred to the ball.

The main obstacle has been size. The early samples were ribbons thinner than a human hair, since only a thin layer can lose heat fast enough to avoid crystallisation. Through years of experimentation with mixtures of five or more elements, chemists have developed alloys that remain glassy in pieces thick enough to hold in the hand, but these often contain expensive metals such as palladium. Moreover, metallic glasses can be surprisingly brittle under tensile stress, failing suddenly because a single narrow band of deformation can spread through the material without being stopped by crystal boundaries. For this reason, their use remains largely confined to small, specialised components, although the search for cheaper and tougher compositions continues.

exercises.question: According to the passage, early samples of metallic glass were extremely thin because ----.
options: palladium was too expensive to be used in thicker pieces
thicker pieces became magnetic and wasted energy as heat
only a thin layer could lose heat quickly enough to prevent crystals from forming
golf club makers required very light materials
thin ribbons were less likely to suffer from corrosion
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘only a thin layer could lose heat quickly enough to prevent crystals from forming’: ‘since only a thin layer can lose heat fast enough to avoid crystallisation’ cümlesi nedeni verir. ‘palladium’ sonraki kalın alaşımlarla ilgilidir. ‘wasted’ enerji kaybı transformatörlerle ilgili ve tersini söylüyor. ‘golf’ sopaları sonraki bir kullanım örneğidir. ‘corrosion’ direnci ince örneklerin nedeni olarak verilmez.

exercises.passage:
Most metals are crystalline: as they cool from a molten state, their atoms settle into a regular, repeating lattice, much like oranges stacked neatly on a market stall. This orderly structure is never perfect, however, and the boundaries between small crystals, together with the defects inside them, are the points at which a malleable metal usually begins to bend permanently or to crack. In 1960, investigators in California found, somewhat unexpectedly, that if certain alloys of gold and silicon were cooled extremely quickly, at roughly a million degrees per second, the atoms had no time to arrange themselves. Instead, they remained frozen in the random pattern of a liquid, and the solid that resulted had no crystal structure at all.

This material, which became known as metallic glass, combines properties that are rarely found together. Because it has no crystal boundaries, some versions can be about twice as strong as conventional steel while remaining remarkably elastic, so that they spring back to their original shape after considerable stress. It also offers good resistance to corrosion, and its unusually soft magnetism makes it useful in the cores of electrical transformers, where it reduces the energy that is wasted as heat. Some sports equipment manufacturers have used it in golf clubs, claiming that more of the energy of a swing is transferred to the ball.

The main obstacle has been size. The early samples were ribbons thinner than a human hair, since only a thin layer can lose heat fast enough to avoid crystallisation. Through years of experimentation with mixtures of five or more elements, chemists have developed alloys that remain glassy in pieces thick enough to hold in the hand, but these often contain expensive metals such as palladium. Moreover, metallic glasses can be surprisingly brittle under tensile stress, failing suddenly because a single narrow band of deformation can spread through the material without being stopped by crystal boundaries. For this reason, their use remains largely confined to small, specialised components, although the search for cheaper and tougher compositions continues.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Piezoelectricity: From Laboratory Curiosity to Everyday Converter’: metin keşiften gündelik cihazlara ve dönüştürücü rolüne uzanır. ‘Radioactivity’ metinde geçmez. ‘Footstep’ başlığı yazarın kuşkusuyla çelişir. ‘Stopped’ başlığı yanlış; kuvars saatler zamanı ölçmeye devam eder. ‘Warfare’ yalnızca ilk uygulamadaki dar bir ayrıntıdır.
exercises.passage:
In 1880 the brothers Pierre and Jacques Curie demonstrated that certain crystals, including quartz, produce a small electrical voltage when they are squeezed or bent. This effect, which was later named piezoelectricity after the Greek word for 'press', arises because the positive and negative charges inside such crystals are not arranged symmetrically, so any compression shifts their centres slightly apart. A year later the reverse effect was predicted on theoretical grounds and quickly confirmed: when a voltage is applied through electrodes, the same crystal changes its shape by a tiny but measurable amount.

For several decades the discovery was regarded as little more than a laboratory curiosity. Its first major application came during the First World War, when piezoelectric crystals were used to send and receive ultrasonic signals underwater in early attempts to detect submarines. Today the effect is found in a remarkable range of everyday devices. The quartz in a typical wristwatch is cut so that it vibrates exactly 32,768 times per second when an electrical current passes through it, and a simple circuit counts these vibrations to measure time. The click of many gas lighters is produced by a small hammer striking a crystal, which generates a spark of several thousand volts, while medical ultrasound scanners rely on ceramic crystals that convert electrical pulses into sound and turn the returning echoes back into signals.

In recent years, engineers have explored whether the effect could be used to collect energy from footsteps, traffic or the vibration of machines. Pilot floors that generate electricity as people walk across them have attracted considerable publicity. The amount of power that is produced, however, is generally very small, often enough to light a few lamps or run wireless sensors rather than to supply a building. As such, piezoelectric materials are likely to remain most valuable not as a source of energy but as precise converters between mechanical and electrical signals.

exercises.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: why NASA's rockets still depend on magnetic fuel to reach space
how loudspeakers were invented by engineers working in space research

why liquids cannot be stored in tanks under any conditions

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how a magnetic liquid first designed for a problem in space came to be used in various technologies on Earth’: metin NASA’daki sorundan başlayıp hoparlör, conta ve tıbbi araştırmalara uzanır. ‘depend’ yanlış; fikir roketlerde hiç benimsenmedi. ‘invented’ yanlış; hoparlörler ferroakışkanı yalnızca kullanır. ‘dangers’ metinde tehlike yok, uygulama deneme aşamasında. ‘any conditions’ yanlış; sorun yalnızca ağırlıksız ortamdadır.
exercises.passage:
In the early 1960s, engineers working for NASA faced an unusual problem. In the weightless conditions of space, liquid fuel does not settle at the bottom of a tank, so it cannot easily be drawn into an engine. One proposed solution, developed by the engineer Steve Papell, was to make the fuel itself magnetic so that it could be pulled towards the outlet by a magnetic field. The idea was never adopted for rocket propulsion, but the material that resulted, now called a ferrofluid, has since found a remarkably wide range of other uses.

A ferrofluid is composed of microscopic particles of an iron oxide, typically about ten nanometres across, which are suspended in a carrier liquid such as a light oil or water. The particles are insoluble in this liquid, and each one is coated with a thin layer of a substance whose molecules prevent the particles from sticking together, so that they remain evenly distributed instead of forming a solid lump. Because the particles are so small, their random thermal motion keeps them from sinking. As a result, the liquid behaves as a single magnetic material whose viscosity rises when a magnet is near. When a strong magnet is brought close, the surface forms a striking pattern of sharp spikes, which reflect a balance between magnetic forces, gravity and surface tension.

These properties are exploited in several technologies that are rarely noticed by users. In many loudspeakers, a small amount of ferrofluid is held in the gap around the coil, where its high thermal conductivity helps to carry heat away and it also reduces unwanted vibration. Ferrofluid seals, which are held in place by permanent magnets, allow rotating parts to pass into vacuum chambers or computer hard drives without letting dust or gas through. Researchers have also investigated whether similar particles could be guided by external magnets to deliver drugs to a specific part of the body, although such applications are still largely at the experimental stage.

options: each of them is covered with a thin layer of a special substance

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘each of them is covered with a thin layer of a special substance’: kaplamanın molekülleri parçacıkların yapışmasını engeller. ‘permanent magnet’ contaları yerinde tutar, yapışmayı önlemez. ‘dissolve’ yanlış; parçacıklar sıvıda çözünmez (insoluble). ‘viscous’ mıknatısın etkisidir, yapışmayla ilgisi yok. ‘too large’ yanlış; parçacıklar yaklaşık on nanometredir.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Most stars, including the Sun, will end their lives in a violent explosion.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘White dwarfs, the dense remains of most stars, help astronomers to estimate ages and to measure the expansion of the universe’: metin beyaz cücenin ne olduğunu, neden çökmediğini ve iki bilimsel kullanımını anlatır. ‘violent’ ilk cümleyle çelişir. ‘rejected’ yanlış; sonradan kabul gördü ve Nobel getirdi. ‘nuclear’ yanlış; tepkimeler durmuştur. ‘observing the Sun’ yanlış; uzak gökadalardaki patlamalar gözlendi.
exercises.passage:
When a star like the Sun has used up the hydrogen in its core, its life does not end in a violent explosion. Instead, after swelling into a red giant and gently pushing its outer layers into space, it leaves behind a small, extremely dense and largely inert remnant known as a white dwarf. Such an object typically contains about half the mass of the Sun packed into a sphere roughly the size of the Earth. As a result, a single teaspoon of its material would weigh several tonnes on our planet. Astronomers estimate that about 97 per cent of the stars in our galaxy, including the Sun in roughly five billion years, will end their lives in this form.

What prevents a white dwarf from collapsing further under its own gravitational pull is not the heat of nuclear reactions, which have stopped, but a quantum effect: electrons that are squeezed very closely together resist further compression. In the 1930s the young Indian physicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar calculated that this resistance has a limit, and that a white dwarf heavier than about 1.4 times the mass of the Sun cannot support itself. His conclusion was initially received with considerable scepticism by leading astronomers, but it gradually gained credence and earned him a Nobel Prize in 1983.

White dwarfs are of interest for at least two reasons. First, because they cool slowly and predictably over billions of years, the coolest ones in a group of stars can be used to estimate the age of that group and to reconstruct the chronology of our galaxy. In a similar way, the temperature of a cooling object can indicate how long ago it was heated. Second, when a white dwarf in a close pair gains enough matter from its partner to approach the limit, it may be destroyed in a particular type of explosion whose peak brightness shows remarkable uniformity. Observations of such explosions in distant galaxies, made with powerful telescopes, provided the evidence, in 1998, that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences, if added to the passage's second paragraph, would be irrelevant?

exercises.passage:
When a star like the Sun has used up the hydrogen in its core, its life does not end in a violent explosion. Instead, after swelling into a red giant and gently pushing its outer layers into space, it leaves behind a small, extremely dense and largely inert remnant known as a white dwarf. Such an object typically contains about half the mass of the Sun packed into a sphere roughly the size of the Earth. As a result, a single teaspoon of its material would weigh several tonnes on our planet. Astronomers estimate that about 97 per cent of the stars in our galaxy, including the Sun in roughly five billion years, will end their lives in this form.

What prevents a white dwarf from collapsing further under its own gravitational pull is not the heat of nuclear reactions, which have stopped, but a quantum effect: electrons that are squeezed very closely together resist further compression. In the 1930s the young Indian physicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar calculated that this resistance has a limit, and that a white dwarf heavier than about 1.4 times the mass of the Sun cannot support itself. His conclusion was initially received with considerable scepticism by leading astronomers, but it gradually gained credence and earned him a Nobel Prize in 1983.

In a similar way, the temperature of a cooling object can indicate how long ago it was heated. Second, when a white dwarf in a close pair gains enough matter from its partner to approach the limit, it may be destroyed in a particular type of explosion whose peak brightness shows remarkable uniformity. Observations of such explosions in distant galaxies, made with powerful telescopes, provided the evidence, in 1998, that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.

to show that the Sun is already cooling quickly
to explain why white dwarfs explode when they reach the limit
to argue that astronomers cannot estimate the age of stars
to illustrate how the temperature of white dwarfs can reveal the age of a group of stars

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘The ceramic crystal used in a medical scanner, which converts electrical pulses into sound, is also designed to turn the returning echoes back into signals.’
options: used
converts
is also designed

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘is also designed’. İskelet: The ceramic crystal (özne) + is also designed (ana fiil, edilgen) + to turn… ‘used’ özneyi niteleyen geçmiş ortaçtır (kullanılan). ‘converts’ which ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘returning’ echoes sözcüğünü niteleyen -ing sıfatıdır. ‘to turn’ amaç bildiren mastardır.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘The English astronomer who had developed a method of studying the Sun's edge on ordinary days observed the same yellow line a few months later, proposing that it came from an unknown element.’

was later recognised
studying
heated

Helyum atmosfere ulaştığında kolayca uzaya kaçar, bu da saptanmasının neden bu kadar zor olduğunu açıklar.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Metallic glasses can be surprisingly brittle under tensile stress, because a narrow band of deformation is not stopped by crystal boundaries.’

Metalik camlar çekme gerilimi altında her zaman kırılgandır, çünkü kristal sınırları tarafından durdurulurlar.

exercises.passage:
In 1821 the German physicist Thomas Seebeck joined two different metals in a closed loop and heated one of the junctions where they met. Unexpectedly, a compass needle placed nearby turned, which he took as a sign of magnetism, although it was later recognised that a small electric current was flowing through the loop. This direct conversion of a temperature difference into electricity, without any moving parts, became known as the Seebeck effect. Thirteen years later, the French physicist Jean Peltier observed the reverse: when a current is passed through such a junction, heat is either absorbed or released, depending on the direction of the current.

For most of the following century these effects were valued mainly for measurement. A thermocouple, which consists of two wires of different metals joined at one end, produces a voltage that rises with temperature, and devices of this kind are still widely used to monitor the temperature of furnaces and engines with considerable precision. Generating useful amounts of power was another matter. The efficiency of the process depends on a material that combines high electrical conductivity with poor heat conduction, a combination that is rarely found in nature, since in most metals the same electrons carry both.

The development of semiconductors such as bismuth telluride in the 1950s improved matters considerably, yet even modern devices, which are also limited by the laws of thermodynamics, typically convert only about five to eight per cent of the heat that passes through them. As such, thermoelectric generators are used mainly where reliability and durability matter more than efficiency. The two Voyager probes, launched in 1977, are still powered by generators that turn the heat from radioactive decay into electricity, and small Peltier units cool camping boxes and sensitive instruments. Investigators are now testing new compounds and nanostructured materials, in the hope that waste heat from car exhausts and factories could one day be recovered on a large scale.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘trace how a puzzling observation about a compound became the basis of a widely used display technology’: metin 1888’deki iki erime noktasından ekranlara uzanan süreci anlatır. ‘disappear’ yanlış; LCD’ler hâlâ en yaygın cihazlar arasında. ‘career’ Lehmann’ın hayatı anlatılmaz. ‘carrots’ yalnızca maddenin kaynağıdır. ‘calculators’ ile televizyonların güç karşılaştırması yapılmaz.
exercises.passage:
In 1888 the Austrian scientist Friedrich Reinitzer, whose main interest was botany, was studying a compound extracted from carrots when he noticed something anomalous that seemed to contradict a basic rule of chemistry. Instead of melting sharply at one temperature, the substance first turned into a cloudy liquid at about 145 degrees Celsius and became clear only at about 179 degrees, as if it had more than one melting point. Reinitzer sent samples to the German physicist Otto Lehmann, who studied them with a microscope. From these microscopic observations he concluded that the cloudy phase was a new state of matter, which he called a liquid crystal.

The explanation lies in the shape of the molecules involved. In many such substances the molecules are long and rod-like, so although they can flow past one another as in an ordinary liquid, they tend to point in roughly the same direction, as in a crystalline solid. This partial order means that the refraction of light passing through the material depends on direction, and it also means that the orientation of the molecules can be changed by a weak electric field. For decades, however, liquid crystals were regarded mainly as an academic curiosity with no obvious practical value.

units.title: Deney raporu
units.description: Fen metinleri: hipotez, yöntem, sonuç ve sınırlılığı ayır
units.guide:
## Strateji
Deney anlatan bir fen metni sabit bir iskelet izler: **hipotez** (ne bekleniyordu?), **yöntem** (ne değiştirildi, neyle karşılaştırıldı?), **sonuç** (ne bulundu?), **sınırlılık** (sonuç nereye kadar genellenebilir?). Sorular da bu dört parçaya yönelir. Parçaların yerini bilirsen cevabı metnin tamamında aramazsın, doğrudan o bölüme gidersin.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Hipotezi bul: *hypothesis, to test whether, predicted, expected*.
2. Yöntemde bağımsız değişkeni (değiştirilen şey), bağımlı değişkeni (ölçülen şey) ve karşılaştırma grubunu (*control group, baseline*) işaretle.
3. Sonuçta *observed, found, fell, rose* fiillerini ve sayıları ayır; sonucu hipotezle karşılaştır.
4. Sınırlılık çoğunlukla *however, nevertheless, acknowledged, only one site* ile gelir. Çıkarım sorularının çoğu buradan sorulur.
5. Yöntemi sonuçla karıştıran ya da sınırlı bir sonucu genelleyen (*always, all, proved*) şıkları ele.

## Örnek
*Researchers predicted that ants count their steps. They lengthened some ants' legs; a control group was left unchanged. Ants with longer legs walked past the nest. However, the study did not show how the counting happens.*
- Hipotez: adım sayma. Yöntem: bacak boyu (bağımsız) → yürünen mesafe (bağımlı), kontrol grubu.
- Sonuç: uzun bacaklılar yuvayı geçti. Sınırlılık: mekanizma bilinmiyor.
- "The study revealed how ants count" → sınırlılıkla çelişir, yanlış.

## Sınav ipucu
"It can be inferred…" sorusunda önce sınırlılık cümlesine bak. Yazarın çekincesi (*may, probably, only*) doğru şıkkın tonunu belirler: kesin konuşan şık genellikle yanlıştır.

exercises.question: The Lake 226 experiment was mainly designed to test whether ----.
options: plastic curtains could stop algae from spreading between lakes
nitrogen alone could make a lake turn green within a few months
phosphorus, rather than carbon, was responsible for the growth of algae in lakes
detergents without phosphates could clean clothes more effectively
aerial photographs could be used to measure the depth of lakes
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘phosphorus, rather than carbon, was responsible for the growth of algae in lakes’: metin fosfor ile karbon arasındaki tartışmayı çözmek için deneyin yapıldığını söylüyor. ‘curtains’ perde yalnızca yöntemin aracıdır. ‘nitrogen alone’ test edilmedi; azot iki yarıya da eklendi. ‘clothes’ deterjanların temizleme gücü konu dışı. ‘depth’ hava fotoğrafı sonucu gösterdi, derinlik ölçmedi.
exercises.passage:
By the late 1960s, many lakes in North America and Europe were turning green with dense growths of algae, and there was fierce debate about the cause. Some scientists argued that phosphorus from sewage and washing powders was mainly responsible, whereas parts of the detergent industry suggested that carbon was the limiting nutrient, which would have made restrictions on phosphates pointless. To settle the question, a team led by the Canadian scientist David Schindler carried out a large-scale controlled experiment in north-western Ontario, where a number of small lakes had been set aside for research.

Lake 226, which consists of two basins joined by a narrow channel, was divided in 1973 by a heavy plastic curtain. One basin received regular additions of carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus, while the other received the same amounts of carbon and nitrogen but no phosphorus, so that it served as a baseline for comparison. Because phosphorus was the only independent variable that differed between the two halves, the design allowed firm conclusions about cause and effect. Within a few months, the basin that had received phosphorus was covered by a thick layer of algae, whereas the other remained clear, and the mismatch was easily observable from the air.

Unsurprisingly, the result had considerable influence on policy, and several governments subsequently restricted the use of phosphates in detergents. Nevertheless, the experiment had limitations that its authors acknowledged. It was conducted on a single small lake on ancient rock in Canada, so any extrapolation to large or very different lakes required further evidence. Later studies have also cast some doubt on the presumption that phosphorus is always the key factor, suggesting that, in some waters, nitrogen plays a larger role than was once assumed and that controlling phosphorus alone may not be sufficient.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the basin that received no phosphorus ----.
options: was treated with extra carbon to stop algae from growing
was later covered by a thick layer of algae
was joined to a different lake by a narrow channel
received no additions of any kind during the experiment
acted as a baseline against which the other basin could be compared
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘acted as a baseline against which the other basin could be compared’: ‘so that it served as a baseline for comparison’ ifadesi bunu söyler. ‘extra carbon’ yanlış; iki yarıya da aynı miktarda karbon verildi. ‘thick layer’ fosfor alan yarıda oldu; bu yarı berrak kaldı. ‘different lake’ yanlış; kanal aynı gölün iki yarısını birleştiriyordu. ‘no additions’ yanlış; karbon ve azot eklendi.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the experiment described in the passage?
options: Gull chicks were trained over several weeks to peck only at realistic models of their parents.

Herring gull chicks obtain food by pecking at the tip of a parent's bill, and the adult responds by bringing up partly digested food for its offspring. The adult's yellow bill carries a conspicuous red spot near the tip of its lower half. In the late 1940s, the Dutch biologist Niko Tinbergen and his student Albert Perdeck asked which features of the parent actually trigger this pecking. Their hypothesis was that the chicks do not respond to the whole bird but to a few simple sensory signals, which act as keys that release a hereditary pattern of behaviour, in other words an instinct.

To test this, the investigators made a series of cardboard models that simulated gull heads. Each model differed from a standard one in only one feature, such as the colour of the spot, the colour of the bill or the shape of the head. The feature being changed was thus the independent variable, while the number of pecks served as the dependent variable. The models were shown to young chicks, most of which had little or no experience of being fed, and a tally of pecks at each model was kept for a fixed period. Because chicks lose interest quickly, the protocol avoided sequential effects by varying the order of presentation.

The results were remarkably clear, and later studies found them broadly replicable. The shape and colour of the head had little effect, and even a bill shown without any head received a similar number of pecks; removing the red spot, however, sharply reduced the response. Unexpectedly, a thin red stick marked with three white bands received more pecks than a realistic model of a gull's head. Later research on parent recognition showed that chicks soon learn to identify their own parents, so these results describe only the observable starting point of behaviour that experience later shapes.

Metin 2: Bacakları uzatılan çöl karıncaları. ys9 kelimeleri: baseline, methodical, control group, investigator, plankton, mammalian, invertebrate, predatory ve 11 kelime daha; ys7 kelimeleri: generalisation, dominant, cumulative, gradual, ecological ve 6 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Paine's hypothesis predicted that, once the sea stars were removed, ----.
options: the number of species would rise because fewer animals were being eaten
barnacles would disappear from the rocks within a few days
the sea stars would quickly return from deeper water
the weather would affect the shore more than predation did
a single prey species would take over and the variety of species would fall
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a single prey species would take over and the variety of species would fall’: hipotez, tepedeki avcının tek bir av türünün baskın olmasını engelleyerek çeşitliliği koruduğudur. ‘rise’ hipotezin tersidir. ‘barnacles’ hipotezde yer almaz; üstelik önce yayıldılar. ‘return’ deniz yıldızlarının geri dönmesi beklenen bir sonuç değildi. ‘weather’ yalnızca kontrol alanıyla ayrıştırılan bir etkendi.
exercises.passage:
In 1963 the American ecologist Robert Paine began a simple but unusually patient experiment on a rocky shore in Washington State. He wanted to test the hypothesis that predatory species at the top of a food chain can maintain the variety of life below them by preventing any single prey species from becoming dominant. On this shore, the purple sea star feeds mainly on mussels, which filter plankton from the water and compete with barnacles, seaweeds and other invertebrates for the limited space on the rocks.

Paine selected a stretch of shore about eight metres long and two metres high and recorded baseline counts of the species living there. Over several years, he then followed a methodical routine, removing every sea star he found by hand and throwing it back into deeper water. A neighbouring stretch, where the sea stars were left undisturbed, served in effect as a control group, so that changes caused by weather or season could be distinguished from the cumulative effect of the removal. The investigator then recorded the number of species in both areas at regular intervals.

Within months, small barnacles spread across the cleared area, and they were soon replaced by mussels, which gradually crowded out most other organisms once predation had stopped. According to his 1966 report, the number of species in the experimental area fell from fifteen to eight, while the neighbouring stretch changed relatively little. A few years later, Paine introduced the term 'keystone species' for a predator whose influence on its ecological community is far greater than its abundance would suggest. The idea has since been applied to mammalian predators such as sea otters and wolves. As it turns out, however, removing a top predator does not always cause such dramatic changes. Because Paine studied only one site and one predator, any generalisation from his results must therefore be made with care.

exercises.question: The neighbouring stretch of shore was important to the experiment because ----.
options: it was where Paine threw the sea stars after removing them
it contained more mussels than the experimental area at the start
it showed which changes were caused by weather or season rather than by the removal
it was cleared of sea stars twice as often
it was the only place where barnacles could grow
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘it showed which changes were caused by weather or season rather than by the removal’: komşu alan kontrol grubu işlevi gördü. ‘threw’ yanlış; deniz yıldızları daha derin suya atıldı. ‘more mussels’ metinde yok. ‘twice as often’ yanlış; komşu alana dokunulmadı. ‘only place’ metinde böyle bir bilgi yok.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the result of the experiment?
options: Ants with longer legs found the nest more quickly than the control group.
The ants found their way mainly by using landmarks on the salt plains.
All the altered ants walked exactly the right distance back to the nest.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Changing the length of the ants’ legs changed the distance they walked, which supports the idea that they count steps’: uzun bacaklılar yuvayı geçti, kısa bacaklılar erken durdu. ‘more quickly’ hız ölçülmedi; uzun bacaklılar yuvayı aştı. ‘landmarks’ yanlış; tuz düzlüklerinde neredeyse yer işareti yok. ‘exactly’ yalnızca kontrol grubu için doğrudur. ‘revealed’ sınırlılıkla çelişir; sinirsel süreç bilinmiyor.
exercises.passage:
Desert ants of the genus Cataglyphis search for food alone on the hot, flat salt plains of North Africa, where there are few landmarks to guide them. After wandering along a winding path for a hundred metres or more, an ant can return to its nest in an almost straight line, which implies that it keeps track of both direction and distance. Direction was already known to be estimated from the pattern of light in the sky, but how the insects measured distance remained unclear. In 2006, researchers from Germany and Switzerland tested a falsifiable hypothesis: that the ants count their steps, functioning in effect as living step counters.

The ants were first trained to walk through a straight channel from their nest to a feeding station ten metres away. Once they had reached the food, some of them were caught and given an anatomical change: in one group, tiny extensions made from pig hairs were glued to the legs, while in another group the legs were shortened. The ants were then released in a parallel test channel and allowed to search for the nest. The predictive logic was simple, the investigators reasoned: ants with longer legs, and thus longer strides, should walk past the nest, whereas those with shorter legs should stop too early.

This is exactly what was observed, with remarkable precision. The median search position of the ants with extended legs lay several metres beyond the nest, the ants with shortened legs fell short, and a control group of unmodified ants searched at roughly the correct distance. When the altered ants later made a full journey from the nest, they estimated the distance correctly, which suggests that the error arose only because stride length had changed after the outward trip. The authors noted, however, that the result was not conclusive about other cues, and that the neuronal process behind the counting remained unknown.

find out whether longer legs help ants to carry more food
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘change the length of their strides without changing the distance to the nest’: adım sayısı aynı kalırken adım boyu değişirse ölçülen mesafe değişir; mantık budur. ‘faster’ hız deneyin konusu değil. ‘light in the sky’ yönle ilgilidir, değiştirilmedi. ‘heat’ korunma amaçlanmadı. ‘carry more food’ metinde yok.

Metin 2: Bulutlu havada mıknatıs taşıyan güvercinler. ys9 kelimeleri: baseline, measurable, precision, investigator, deciduous, foliage, regeneration, nitrate ve 13 kelime daha; ys7 kelimeleri: volume, rough, calcium, mineral, drain ve 11 kelime daha.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: argue that all commercial logging should be banned immediately
describe the history of New Hampshire's forest industry
explain how drinking water standards are set
compare the trees growing in different valleys
report a forest-clearing experiment, its results and the limits on how they can be applied
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘report a forest-clearing experiment, its results and the limits on how they can be applied’: metin hipotez, yöntem, sonuç ve sınırlılık sırasıyla bir deney raporudur. ‘banned’ yazar bir yasak önermez; tersine sonuçların ticari ormancılığa doğrudan uygulanamayacağını söyler. ‘history’ eyaletin orman tarihi anlatılmaz. ‘standards’ içme suyu sınırları yalnızca karşılaştırma için anılır. ‘compare the trees’ ağaç türleri karşılaştırılmaz.
exercises.passage:
Forests strongly influence the water and chemicals that leave a landscape, but in the early 1960s this influence was difficult to measure, because most streams receive water from many different sources. Two American investigators, Gene Likens and Herbert Bormann, saw an opportunity in the Hubbard Brook forest of New Hampshire. There, a number of small deciduous valleys are each drained by a single stream and lie on solid rock that lets very little water escape underground, so the water leaving through the stream can be measured with precision.

At the outset, their hypothesis was that removing the vegetation would increase the flow of water and the loss of nutrients from the soil. During the winter of 1965 to 1966, all the trees in one valley of about sixteen hectares were cut down and left where they fell, and chemicals were sprayed for the next three summers to prevent any regeneration. A neighbouring valley, which was left untouched, provided a baseline, and the volume and chemistry of both streams were recorded every week.

The differences were large. In the first year, the flow of water from the cleared valley rose by roughly 40 per cent, mainly because there was no foliage left to pass moisture back into the air by evaporation from its leaves. More strikingly, the concentration of nitrate in the stream increased many times over, at times exceeding the limits that were then recommended for drinking water, and calcium and other minerals were also lost at a much higher rate. The authors acknowledged that their treatment was far more extreme than ordinary logging, in which new plants are allowed to grow back, so the figures could not be applied directly to commercial forestry. The study nevertheless established the small valley as a measurable basic unit of ecosystem research.

exercises.question: The valleys at Hubbard Brook were especially suitable for the study because ----.
options: almost all the water leaving each valley flowed out through a single stream
they received no rain or snow during the winter
they had already been cleared of trees by farmers
their streams were fed by water from many different sources
they contained no nutrients in their soil
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘almost all the water leaving each valley flowed out through a single stream’: kaya suyu yeraltına kaçırmadığı için çıkan su dereden hassasça ölçülebiliyordu. ‘no rain’ metinde yok. ‘farmers’ yanlış; ağaçları araştırmacılar kesti. ‘many different sources’ birinci cümledeki genel sorundur, Hubbard Brook’un avantajı değil. ‘no nutrients’ yanlış; deney besin kaybını ölçüyordu.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the flow of water from the cleared valley increased mainly because ----.

the cut trees blocked the stream
more snow fell on the cleared valley
no leaves were left to return moisture to the air
new plants used less water than the old trees

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences would best be inserted after the sentence ending ‘…recorded every week’?
options: As a result, the trees in the neighbouring valley were cut down as well.
Any change in the cleared valley could therefore be judged against the natural changes in its neighbour.
For example, nitrate is a common ingredient in garden fertilisers.
However, the streams were measured only once, at the end of the study.
Similarly, logging companies always allow new plants to grow back.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Any change in the cleared valley could therefore be judged against the natural changes in its neighbour’: kontrol vadisinin neden önemli olduğunu açıklar ve sonraki ‘The differences were large’ cümlesine zemin hazırlar. ‘cut down as well’ komşu vadinin dokunulmadan bırakıldığı bilgisiyle çelişir. ‘fertilisers’ odağı kaydırır. ‘only once’ haftalık ölçümle çelişir. ‘Similarly’ sınırlılık paragrafına erken ve yanlış bağlaçla atlar.

exercises.question: Keeton's hypothesis was that pigeons ----.
options: find their way home mainly by following familiar landmarks
can use a magnetic sense to find their direction when the Sun is hidden
cannot fly in the right direction on sunny days
are confused by brass bars as much as by magnets
use the Sun as a compass only when the sky is cloudy
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘can use a magnetic sense to find their direction when the Sun is hidden’: hipotez, güvercinlerin Güneş görünmediğinde başvurdukları ikinci, manyetik bir pusula taşıdığıdır. ‘landmarks’ yalnızca sonraki çalışmalarda anılan ek bir ipucudur. ‘sunny days’ yanlış; güneşli günlerde yönlerini buldular. ‘brass bars’ etkisiz olsun diye seçildi. ‘only when the sky is cloudy’ mantığı ters çeviriyor.
exercises.passage:
Homing pigeons released hundreds of kilometres from their loft usually set off in roughly the right direction within minutes, even over unfamiliar ground. By the late 1960s, experiments had shown that the birds can use the position of the Sun as a compass, but this could not explain how they also returned successfully on days when thick cloud covered the sky. In 1971 the American biologist William Keeton tested a falsifiable hypothesis: that pigeons carry a second, magnetic compass, on which they rely mainly when the Sun is hidden.

Keeton glued small bar magnets to the backs of one group of pigeons, while birds in a control group carried brass bars of the same size and weight, which have no magnetic effect. Because the magnet was the only independent variable, any difference in behaviour could reasonably be attributed to it. The birds were released one at a time at sites far from home, both on sunny days and under total cloud, and observers watched each bird until it was no longer observable. The direction in which it vanished from view, which served as the dependent variable, was then recorded.

The results matched the prediction remarkably well. On sunny days, birds in both groups vanished in roughly the direction of home, which suggests that the magnets made little difference when the Sun was visible. Under overcast skies, however, the control birds still headed home, whereas the directions taken by the birds carrying magnets were scattered almost at random. Keeton was careful to point out that the experiment did not show how pigeons actually sense the magnetic field. Moreover, later attempts to obtain replicable results produced some inconsistency, partly because of methodological differences and partly because pigeons also seem to use smell and familiar landmarks.

exercises.question: The brass bars were attached to the control birds in order to ----.
options: help the observers follow the birds more easily
increase the strength of the magnetic field around the birds
make the control birds lighter than the others
make sure that the two groups differed only in the presence of a magnet
stop the control birds from seeing the Sun
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘make sure that the two groups differed only in the presence of a magnet’: aynı boyut ve ağırlıktaki pirinç çubuk, mıknatısı tek bağımsız değişken yapar. ‘observers’ gözlemi kolaylaştırmak amaçlanmadı. ‘increase’ yanlış; pirincin manyetik etkisi yoktur. ‘lighter’ yanlış; ağırlık aynıydı. ‘seeing the Sun’ çubukların görüşle ilgisi yok.

exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that on sunny days the pigeons carrying magnets ----.
options: were probably able to rely on the Sun instead of their magnetic sense
flew in random directions like the birds under cloud
returned home faster than the control birds
removed the magnets before they took off
could not be watched by the observers
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘were probably able to rely on the Sun instead of their magnetic sense’: güneşli havada iki grup da eve yöneldi; mıknatısın bozucu etkisi ancak Güneş görünmediğinde ortaya çıktı. ‘random’ yalnızca bulutlu havadaki mıknatıslı kuşlar içindir. ‘faster’ hız ölçülmedi. ‘removed’ metinde yok. ‘watched’ gözlemcilerin kuşları izleyemediği söylenmez.

nodes.title: Cümle çözümleme
nodes.description: Deney raporlarından uzun cümleler: ana fiili bul, whose neyi niteliyor, en uygun çeviri

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘The basin receiving phosphorus, which had been separated from the other by a plastic curtain, was soon covered by spreading algae that turned the water bright green.’
options: receiving
had been separated
was soon covered
spreading
turned
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘was soon covered’. İskelet: The basin (özne) + was soon covered (ana fiil, edilgen) + by spreading algae. ‘receiving’ özneyi niteleyen -ing yapısıdır. ‘had been separated’ which ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘spreading’ algae sözcüğünü niteleyen sıfattır. ‘turned’ that ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Ants whose legs had been lengthened, unlike those used as controls, walked past the nest, searching several metres beyond the point where it was located.’
options: walked
had been lengthened
used
searching
was located
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘walked’. İskelet: Ants (özne) + walked (ana fiil) + past the nest. ‘had been lengthened’ whose ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘used’ those sözcüğünü niteleyen geçmiş ortaçtır. ‘searching’ zarf görevli -ing yapısıdır. ‘was located’ where ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Removing the red spot from the cardboard model, which otherwise closely resembled a real parent, sharply reduced the number of pecks that were recorded by the watching investigators.’
options: Removing
resembled
reduced
were recorded
watching
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘reduced’. İskelet: Removing the red spot (-ing ile kurulan isim öbeği, özne) + sharply reduced (ana fiil) + the number of pecks (nesne). ‘Removing’ öznenin kendisidir, ana fiil değildir. ‘resembled’ which ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘were recorded’ that ile başlayan yan cümlenin edilgen fiilidir. ‘watching’ investigators sözcüğünü niteleyen sıfattır.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘whose’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘The soils, which had been made very rich in organic matter, contained microbial populations whose respiration consumed oxygen.’
options: the soils
organic matter
oxygen
respiration
microbial populations
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘microbial populations’: whose iyelik bildirir ve hemen önündeki ada bağlanır; solunum mikrop topluluklarına aittir. ‘the soils’ which ile nitelenen öznedir. ‘organic matter’ which cümlesinin içindedir. ‘oxygen’ whose cümlesinin nesnesidir. ‘respiration’ whose’dan sonra gelen ve sahip olunan şeydir, nitelenen değil.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Within about a year, most of the islands had regained roughly the number of species that they had contained before the treatment.’
options: Yaklaşık bir yıl içinde adaların tümü, işlemden önceki türlerin aynısına kavuşmuştu.
Yaklaşık bir yıl içinde adaların çoğu, işlemden önce barındırdıkları tür sayısına aşağı yukarı yeniden ulaşmıştı.
Yaklaşık on yıl içinde adaların çoğu, işlemden önce barındırdıkları tür sayısını kaybetmişti.
Yaklaşık bir yıl içinde adaların çoğu, işlemden önceki tür sayısına yeniden ulaşacaktır.
Yaklaşık bir yıl içinde adaların hiçbiri, işlemden önceki tür sayısına yeniden ulaşamamıştı.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…adaların çoğu, işlemden önce barındırdıkları tür sayısına aşağı yukarı yeniden ulaşmıştı’. İskelet: most of the islands (özne) + had regained (ana fiil, miş’li geçmiş) + roughly the number of species (nesne). ‘tümü’ niceleyiciyi, ‘aynısına’ ise anlamı değiştiriyor; türler çoğu zaman farklıydı. ‘kaybetmişti’ ve ‘on yıl’ anlamı ve süreyi bozuyor. ‘ulaşacaktır’ zamanı geleceğe çeviriyor. ‘hiçbiri’ olumsuzluk katıyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Later studies have suggested that controlling phosphorus alone may not be sufficient in some waters.’
options: Sonraki çalışmalar, bütün sularda yalnızca fosforu denetlemenin yeterli olduğunu kanıtlamıştır.
Sonraki çalışmalar, bazı sularda fosforu denetlemenin kesinlikle gereksiz olduğunu göstermiştir.
Önceki çalışmalar, bazı sularda yalnızca fosforu denetlemenin yeterli olabileceğini ileri sürmüştü.
Sonraki çalışmalar, bazı sularda yalnızca fosforu denetlemenin yeterli olmayabileceğini ileri sürmüştür.
Sonraki çalışmalar, bazı sularda yalnızca azotu denetlemenin yeterli olmayabileceğini ileri sürecektir.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…bazı sularda yalnızca fosforu denetlemenin yeterli olmayabileceğini ileri sürmüştür’. İskelet: Later studies (özne) + have suggested (ana fiil) + that… may not be (olumsuz olasılık). ‘bütün’ ve ‘kanıtlamıştır’ niceleyiciyi ve çekinceyi değiştiriyor. ‘gereksiz’ anlamı bozup ‘kesinlikle’ ile kesinlik katıyor. ‘Önceki’ özneyi, ‘olabileceğini’ ise olumsuzluğu değiştiriyor. ‘azotu’ ve ‘sürecektir’ öğeyi ve zamanı değiştiriyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘The birds carrying magnets were not able to keep a course towards home when the Sun was hidden by cloud.’
options: Güneş bulutlarla örtüldüğünde mıknatıs taşıyan kuşlar eve doğru bir rota izlemeyi sürdürdü.
Mıknatıs taşıyan kuşlar Güneş’i bulutlarla örttüğünde eve doğru bir rota izleyemedi.
Güneş bulutlarla örtüldüğünde mıknatıs taşıyan kuşlar eve doğru bir rota izleyemedi.
Güneş bulutlarla örtülürse mıknatıs taşıyan kuşların bazıları eve doğru bir rota izleyemeyebilir.
Güneş bulutlarla örtüldüğünde mıknatıs taşıyan kuşlar eve daha hızlı döndü.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Güneş bulutlarla örtüldüğünde mıknatıs taşıyan kuşlar eve doğru bir rota izleyemedi’. İskelet: The birds (özne) + were not able to keep (olumsuz yeterlilik, geçmiş); carrying magnets (özneyi niteleyen -ing); when the Sun was hidden (edilgen zaman cümlesi). ‘sürdürdü’ olumsuzluğu kaldırıyor. ‘örttüğünde’ edilgeni etkene çevirip işi kuşlara veriyor. ‘bazıları’ ve ‘izleyemeyebilir’ niceleyici ve olasılık ekliyor. ‘hızlı’ metinde olmayan bir anlam katıyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Ağaçlar kesildikten sonra deredeki nitrat derişimi birçok kat arttı.’
options: Before the trees were cut down, the concentration of nitrate in the stream fell sharply.
After the trees were cut down, the concentration of nitrate in the stream may increase slightly.
After the stream was cut down, the trees increased the concentration of nitrate many times over.
After the trees were cut down, the concentration of nitrate in the stream did not change.
After the trees were cut down, the concentration of nitrate in the stream increased many times over.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘After the trees were cut down, the concentration of nitrate in the stream increased many times over’: “kesildikten sonra” edilgen ve geçmiş (were cut down), “birçok kat arttı” = increased many times over. ‘Before’ ve ‘fell’ zamanı ve yönü tersine çeviriyor. ‘may’ ve ‘slightly’ olasılık ve miktarı değiştiriyor. ‘stream was cut down’ özneleri karıştırıyor. ‘did not change’ olumsuzluk ekliyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Deneyin yalnızca tek bir göl üzerinde yapılması, sonuçlarının genellenmesini sınırladı.’
options: The fact that the experiment was carried out on only one lake limited the generalisation of its results.
Because the experiment was carried out on many lakes, its results could be generalised easily.
The experiment was carried out on only one lake, but this did not limit its results in any way.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the findings of the experiment?
options: The islands remained empty of animals for many years after the treatment.
Exactly the same species returned to every island in the same numbers.
The most distant island recovered more quickly than the nearest one.
After their animals were removed, the islands regained roughly their former number of species, though not always the same species.
The gas used in the treatment destroyed the mangrove trees on most islands.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘After their animals were removed, the islands regained roughly their former number of species, though not always the same species’: üçüncü paragraf tam olarak bunu söyler. ‘empty’ yanlış; yaklaşık bir yılda tür sayısı geri geldi. ‘Exactly the same’ yanlış; türler çoğu zaman farklıydı. ‘most distant’ tersidir; en yakın ada en hızlı toparlandı. ‘destroyed’ yanlış; ağaçlar büyük ölçüde zarar görmedi.
exercises.passage:
In the 1960s, the American ecologists Robert MacArthur and Edward Wilson proposed that the number of species on an island reflects a balance between the arrival of new species and the disappearance of existing ones. If this theory, which had considerable predictive power, was correct, an island that had lost its animals should gradually return to roughly its original number of species, although not necessarily the same ones. Testing such a falsifiable prediction on a real island seemed almost impossible. In 1966, however, Wilson and his student Daniel Simberloff, who was then a young investigator, designed an experiment in the Florida Keys.

The researchers chose several tiny islands, each consisting of a few mangrove trees standing in shallow water and measuring only about eleven to eighteen metres across. During careful fieldwork, they first recorded a baseline tally of every species of insect, spider and other small invertebrate living on each island, with help from experts in taxonomy. A professional pest-control company then covered the islands with large tents and filled them with a gas that killed the animals but left the trees largely undamaged. Over the following two years, the islands were visited regularly, and the colonisation of each one by new arrivals was recorded.

Within about a year, most of the islands had regained roughly the number of species that they had contained before the treatment, although the particular species were often different, and the pattern proved reproducible across the islands. The island that lay closest to the mainland recovered most quickly, while the most distant one remained poorer in species, as the theory predicted. The study, which is now regarded as a classic, nevertheless had clear limitations. It was confined to small animals on very small islands, and it was difficult to be sure that every creature hidden inside the wood had been removed.

have a baseline with which later counts could be compared
show that the gas had no effect on insects
find out how far each island lay from the mainland
make sure that the mangrove trees were healthy
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘have a baseline with which later counts could be compared’: işlem öncesi sayım, sonradan geri gelen tür sayısının karşılaştırılacağı başlangıç değeridir. ‘returned’ yanlış; türler kendiliğinden geldi. ‘no effect’ gazın amacı tam tersine hayvanları öldürmekti. ‘how far’ uzaklık sayımla ölçülmez. ‘healthy’ ağaçların sağlığı sayımın amacı değil.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: describe what went wrong in Biosphere 2 and what its problems revealed
encourage people to build sealed homes in the desert
prove that humans can live in a closed system for many years
explain how rainforests produce most of the oxygen on Earth
describe the daily lives of the eight crew members
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘describe what went wrong in Biosphere 2 and what its problems revealed’: metin oksijen düşüşünü, nedenlerini ve projenin bilimsel sınırlarını anlatır. ‘encourage’ yazar kimseyi böyle evler kurmaya çağırmaz. ‘prove’ yanlış; sistem kapalı kalamadı. ‘rainforests’ yalnızca yapının bir bölümüdür. ‘daily lives’ ekibin günlük yaşamı anlatılmaz.
exercises.passage:
In September 1991, eight people entered Biosphere 2, a sealed structure of glass and steel covering about one hectare in the desert of Arizona, and planned to remain inside for two years. The building contained small versions of several natural environments, including a rainforest, a desert and a miniature ocean, together with a farm on which the crew were expected to grow almost all of their own food. The project was intended to test the feasibility of maintaining human life inside a closed artificial ecosystem that recycled its own air, water and nutrients.

From the outset, the level of oxygen inside the structure fell steadily. Within about sixteen months it had dropped from roughly 21 per cent, the normal value at sea level, to about 14 per cent, a level at which several crew members reported tiredness and difficulty in breathing. In January 1993 the managers decided to pump in pure oxygen from outside, which meant that the system was no longer fully closed. The investigators then faced an anomalous pattern: the oxygen had disappeared, but the carbon dioxide that its consumption should have produced had not risen as expected.

Later studies suggested an answer to both puzzles. The soils, which had been made very rich in organic matter to support farming, contained huge microbial populations whose respiration consumed oxygen faster than the plants could replace it through photosynthesis. Much of the resulting gas was then absorbed by the exposed concrete inside the building, where it reacted to form calcium carbonate. Critics pointed out that Biosphere 2 had never been a controlled experiment, since many factors changed at the same time and there was no replication. Nevertheless, its failures demonstrated how difficult it is to reproduce the hidden processes that keep the atmosphere of the Earth in balance.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the carbon dioxide inside Biosphere 2 did not rise as expected because ----.
options: the plants turned all of it back into oxygen
the managers pumped it out of the building
the microbes in the soil consumed it
the crew members breathed less as oxygen fell
much of it was absorbed by exposed concrete
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘much of it was absorbed by exposed concrete’: gaz açıkta kalan betonla tepkimeye girip kalsiyum karbonat oluşturdu. ‘plants’ bitkiler oksijeni yeterince yerine koyamadı. ‘pumped it out’ yanlış; dışarıdan oksijen pompalandı. ‘microbes’ karbondioksidi tüketmedi, tersine üretti. ‘breathed less’ metinde böyle bir açıklama yok.

units.title: Klinik çalışma özeti
units.description: Katılımcı, müdahale, sonuç ve çekinceyi ayırarak klinik çalışma özetlerini oku
units.guide:
## Strateji

Klinik çalışma özetleri YÖKDİL sağlık metinlerinin en sık türüdür ve hep aynı iskeleti izler: **katılımcılar** (kim, kaç kişi), **müdahale** (ne verildi, neyle karşılaştırıldı), **sonuç** (ne ölçüldü, ne bulundu) ve **çekince** (sonuç kime uymaz, neden temkinli olmalı). Sorular çoğu zaman bu dört kutudan birini sorar; çeldiriciler de bir kutudaki bilgiyi ötekine taşır.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Okurken kenara dört harf yaz: K, M, S, Ç.

2. K: sayı ve özellik (*about 420 adults, aged 70 to 84, in remission*).

3. M: müdahale ve karşılaştırma grubu (*placebo, sham procedure, usual care, control group*). *randomly assigned* ve *blinded* ifadelerini işaretle.

4. S: ana sonuç ve süre (*death within 28 days, after twelve months*).

5. Ç: *however, nevertheless, caution, not conclusive, applies only to, subgroup* ile gelen sınırlama.

## Örnek

Çeldiriciler çoğu zaman bir alt grubun sonucunu bütün katılımcılara genelleştirir ya da *may, suggest* gibi temkinli fiilleri *prove* düzeyine çıkarır. Şıktaki iddianın hangi gruba ve hangi süreye ait olduğunu metinde kontrol et.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
For many years, keyhole surgery on the knee was among the most frequently performed outpatient operations in middle-aged adults. Many of these patients had developed symptomatic pain after small, gradual tears in the soft tissue that cushions the joint. Surgeons trimmed away the damaged tissue through a tiny incision, and most patients reported that they felt considerably better afterwards. In the absence of a proper control group, however, it was impossible to tell whether the improvement was caused by the procedure itself or by other factors, such as rest, rehabilitation and the natural tendency of pain to fade over time.

To answer this question, investigators in Finland designed a clinical trial with an unusual feature. About 150 patients aged between 35 and 65, who had knee pain and a slowly developing tear but no serious joint disease, gave informed consent and were randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group received the standard operation, whereas the other underwent a sham procedure in which the surgeon made the same incisions and imitated the sounds of real surgery without removing any tissue. Neither the patients nor the staff who compared their pain scores with baseline values were told which treatment had been given, a feature which added considerable methodological rigour.

After twelve months, both groups showed a similar and substantial reduction in pain, and the difference between them was too small to be clinically meaningful. Later trials with comparable designs reached broadly consistent conclusions about the limited efficacy of the operation, and some guidelines now advise against routine surgery for this condition. Nevertheless, the findings are not conclusive for every patient, since they apply only to slowly developing tears in middle-aged adults and not to sudden injuries in young athletes, for whom surgery may still be the appropriate choice. Interestingly, the study also illustrates how strongly expectations can shape the outcome of an operation.

Young athletes with sudden knee injuries should never be offered surgery.

Rehabilitation has been shown to work better than surgery for all kinds of knee injury.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Appendicitis, an inflammation of the small pouch attached to the large intestine, has been treated by surgical removal of the appendix for more than a century. The operation is still regarded as one of the most routine procedures in emergency medicine, although it requires hospitalisation and carries the usual risks of surgery. Over the past two decades, more than one clinical trial has therefore examined whether a regimen of antibiotics might be a reasonable alternative for patients whose condition is uncomplicated, meaning that the appendix has not burst. In a typical design, symptomatic adults whose diagnosis had been confirmed by a scan gave informed consent and were randomly assigned either to surgery or to antibiotics, which were given intravenously to inpatients at first and then by mouth at home.

The results have been broadly consistent. In a Finnish trial of about 500 adults, roughly seven in ten patients in the antibiotic group did not need an operation within the first year, and the proportion who had avoided surgery was still above half after five years. Patients who eventually required an operation did not appear to suffer more serious complications as a result of the delay, and no major adverse effect of the antibiotics was reported. A later trial in the United States, which included about 1,500 participants, found that antibiotics were no worse than surgery in terms of general health after thirty days.

These findings support the efficacy of antibiotics, but they do not mean that the operation has become outdated. Recurrence remains common, and a small hard deposit inside the appendix was found to be a useful predictor of later surgery. Many clinicians therefore regard antibiotics as one therapeutic option to be discussed with the patient rather than a replacement for surgery. The decision is increasingly shaped by individual preferences, such as the wish to avoid an operation or, conversely, the wish to avoid the risk of the problem returning.
options: Why Appendix Surgery Should Be Abandoned Completely
The History of Emergency Surgery in Finland
How a Burst Appendix Is Treated in Hospital
The Dangers of Delaying Every Kind of Operation
Antibiotics as an Alternative to Surgery for Uncomplicated Appendicitis
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Antibiotics as an Alternative to Surgery for Uncomplicated Appendicitis’: metin antibiyotik ile ameliyatı karşılaştıran denemeleri ve sınırlarını özetler. ‘Abandoned’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, metin ameliyatın modası geçmediğini söyler; ‘History’ geçen başlık metnin konusu değildir; ‘Burst’ geçen başlık yanlış hasta grubundan söz eder, denemeler patlamamış apandisi inceler; ‘Dangers’ geçen başlık metne ters düşer, gecikme ciddi komplikasyon yaratmadı.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
exercises.passage:
When the COVID-19 pandemic began in early 2020, doctors had no treatment that had been shown to reduce deaths, and many drugs were given to patients on the basis of laboratory studies or small, uncontrolled reports. In the United Kingdom, investigators responded by setting up a large clinical trial which was designed to be simple enough for busy hospitals to join. Inpatients with the infection were randomly assigned to usual care alone or to usual care plus one of several drugs. The main outcome, death within 28 days, was recorded from routine hospital documentation with minimal extra work for the staff, which greatly improved the feasibility of the study.

One of the drugs tested was dexamethasone, an inexpensive steroid which reduces inflammation and had been available for decades. About 2,100 patients received it in a regimen of up to ten days, and their outcomes were compared with those of about 4,300 patients who received usual care. Among patients in intensive care who needed a machine to help them breathe, deaths were reduced by about one third, and among those who needed extra oxygen alone, the reduction was about one fifth. However, no efficacy was found in the subgroup of patients who did not require oxygen, and the results even suggested a possibility of harm in this group.

The findings were announced in June 2020 and quickly changed practice around the world, since the drug was cheap and widely available. Experts noted that the trial was not blinded, which might normally raise concern, but because death is an objective outcome, this limitation was considered less serious. The large sample size also made the results unusually conclusive. The study is often cited as evidence that simple trials can produce reliable answers in a short time, even in the middle of a crisis.
options: the laboratory studies on which most early treatments for COVID-19 were based
the reasons why blinded trials are always more reliable than open ones
the harmful effects of steroids on every patient admitted to hospital
the way in which the pandemic first spread to the United Kingdom
a large, simple trial which showed that a cheap drug reduced deaths in some patients with COVID-19
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a large, simple trial which showed that a cheap drug reduced deaths in some patients with COVID-19’: metin büyük ve basit bir denemede deksametazonun bazı hasta gruplarında ölümleri azalttığını anlatır. ‘laboratory’ geçen şık yalnızca giriş cümlesindeki bir ayrıntıdır; ‘blinded’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, kör olmamanın burada ciddi bir sorun sayılmadığı söylenir; ‘harmful’ geçen şık olası zararı yalnızca oksijen almayan gruba ait bir ihtimalden bütün hastalara genelleştirir; ‘spread’ geçen şık metnin konusu değildir.
