exercises.question: Which of the following sentences would best follow the last sentence of the passage?
exercises.passage:
When the COVID-19 pandemic began in early 2020, doctors had no treatment that had been shown to reduce deaths, and many drugs were given to patients on the basis of laboratory studies or small, uncontrolled reports. In the United Kingdom, investigators responded by setting up a large clinical trial which was designed to be simple enough for busy hospitals to join. Inpatients with the infection were randomly assigned to usual care alone or to usual care plus one of several drugs. The main outcome, death within 28 days, was recorded from routine hospital documentation with minimal extra work for the staff, which greatly improved the feasibility of the study.

One of the drugs tested was dexamethasone, an inexpensive steroid which reduces inflammation and had been available for decades. About 2,100 patients received it in a regimen of up to ten days, and their outcomes were compared with those of about 4,300 patients who received usual care. Among patients in intensive care who needed a machine to help them breathe, deaths were reduced by about one third, and among those who needed extra oxygen alone, the reduction was about one fifth. However, no efficacy was found in the subgroup of patients who did not require oxygen, and the results even suggested a possibility of harm in this group.

The findings were announced in June 2020 and quickly changed practice around the world, since the drug was cheap and widely available. Experts noted that the trial was not blinded, which might normally raise concern, but because death is an objective outcome, this limitation was considered less serious. The large sample size also made the results unusually conclusive. The study is often cited as evidence that simple trials can produce reliable answers in a short time, even in the middle of a crisis.
options: However, the trial took more than ten years to produce any useful results.
Steroids are also widely misused by some athletes who wish to build muscle.
For this reason, dexamethasone is now given to every patient with a mild cough.
In contrast, small uncontrolled reports have always produced the most reliable answers.
Its design has since been recommended as a model for testing treatments quickly in future outbreaks.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Its design has since been recommended as a model for testing treatments quickly in future outbreaks’: son cümle basit ve büyük denemelerin kriz anında bile hızlı cevap verebildiğini söyler; bu cümle o fikri geleceğe taşır. ‘years’ geçen şık ‘However’ ile metindeki hız vurgusuyla çelişir; ‘athletes’ geçen şık odağı başka bir konuya kaydırır; ‘cough’ geçen şık metindeki bulguya ters düşer, ilaç oksijen gerektirmeyenlere yarar sağlamadı; ‘uncontrolled’ geçen şık ‘In contrast’ ile metnin görüşünü tersine çevirir.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Bleeding is one of the leading causes of death after serious injuries, such as those suffered in road crashes, falls and violence, and many of these deaths occur within hours of the injury. Tranexamic acid is an inexpensive drug which helps blood to clot by slowing down the natural breakdown of clots, and it had long been used to reduce blood loss during planned surgery. Whether it could also save the lives of injured patients, however, remained uncertain until a large international clinical trial was carried out.

The trial enrolled about 20,000 adult trauma patients in 40 countries whose vital signs suggested heavy bleeding or who were thought to be at risk of it. Within eight hours of the injury, each patient was randomly assigned to receive either the drug or a placebo through an intravenous drip in a simple regimen, and neither the patients nor the clinicians knew which had been given. The main outcome was death in hospital within four weeks. Deaths from any cause fell from about 16 per cent in the placebo group to about 14.5 per cent in the treatment group, and the reduction in deaths due to bleeding was proportionally larger. No increase in any serious adverse effect, such as a heart attack or a stroke, was detected, despite the very large sample size.

A later exploratory analysis revealed an important limitation regarding timing. The efficacy of the drug was greatest when it was given within one hour of the injury and was still evident up to three hours, but treatment started after three hours appeared to increase the risk of death from bleeding. For this reason, guidelines in many countries now recommend that the drug should be given as early as possible, ideally during triage. In some regions, paramedics even administer it before the patient reaches hospital.
options: How Tranexamic Acid Was Discovered in the Laboratory
Why Road Crashes Are the Leading Cause of Death Worldwide
Timing Matters: A Cheap Drug That Reduces Deaths From Bleeding After Injury
A Dangerous Drug That Causes Heart Attacks and Strokes
Planned Surgery Without Any Loss of Blood
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Timing Matters: A Cheap Drug That Reduces Deaths From Bleeding After Injury’: metin ilacın kanamadan ölümleri azalttığını ve etkinin zamanlamaya bağlı olduğunu anlatır. ‘Discovered’ geçen başlık metinde geçmeyen bir konudur; ‘Crashes’ geçen başlık yalnızca giriş cümlesindeki bir örneği konu yapar; ‘Dangerous’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, pıhtı kaynaklı olaylarda artış görülmedi; ‘Planned’ geçen başlık ilacın eski kullanım alanını ana konu sayar.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
Babies who are born too early or too small are at high risk of dying in their first weeks of life, particularly in low-income countries, where incubators and other equipment are often in short supply. Kangaroo mother care, in which the baby is held in continuous skin-to-skin contact on the mother's chest and supported by breastfeeding, was developed by physicians in Colombia in the late 1970s as a low-cost way of keeping such infants warm. Traditionally, however, it was started only after the baby had become stable, which often took several days after childbirth.

A clinical trial coordinated by the World Health Organization examined whether starting this care immediately would further reduce infant mortality. The study enrolled about 3,200 infants weighing between one and 1.8 kilograms in hospitals in five countries in Africa and Asia. In the intervention group, babies were kept on the mother's chest in a special maternity unit where mothers and infants stayed together. In the control group, by comparison, babies were cared for in a conventional intensive care unit and were placed with their mothers only once they were stable. The main outcome was death within 28 days of birth.

Mortality was about 12 per cent in the intervention group and about 16 per cent in the control group, which amounts to a reduction of roughly one quarter. Because the efficacy of the approach was so clear, the trial was stopped earlier than planned on the recommendation of an independent committee. The investigators noted, however, that the hospitals involved had to change their protocols and be reorganised so that mothers could remain with their babies day and night, and that the feasibility of doing this elsewhere may depend on considerable investment in space and staff. Even so, the results have led to a revision of international guidance.
options: Incubators have proved more effective than skin-to-skin care for keeping small babies warm.
Starting skin-to-skin care straight after birth reduced deaths among small babies, although it requires changes in hospitals.
Kangaroo mother care was invented by the World Health Organization in the 1970s.
Hospitals in rich countries no longer need intensive care units for small babies.
The trial failed because it had to be stopped earlier than planned.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Starting skin-to-skin care straight after birth reduced deaths among small babies, although it requires changes in hospitals’: metin hem ölümlerdeki azalmayı hem de hastanelerin yeniden düzenlenmesi çekincesini verir. ‘Incubators’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘invented’ geçen şık yöntemi yanlış kuruma bağlar, yöntem Kolombiya’da geliştirildi; ‘rich’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir genellemedir; ‘failed’ geçen şık nedeni ters çevirir, deneme yarar açık olduğu için erken durduruldu.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Depression often returns after a person has recovered, and the risk of recurrence increases with every previous episode. For this reason, people who have experienced recurrent episodes are commonly advised to continue taking antidepressant medication for long periods, sometimes for years. Many patients, however, would prefer to stop, either because of adverse effects or because they do not wish to depend on medication, and this has prompted interest in psychotherapy as an alternative.

Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy is a group programme, usually delivered in eight weekly sessions, which combines meditation practice with techniques from cognitive therapy. Participants are taught to notice early warning signs, such as negative thoughts, and to respond to them without being carried away. In one large British clinical trial, about 420 adults who had experienced at least three episodes of depression and were currently in remission were randomly assigned either to continue their medication or to attend the programme. Those in the therapy group were also supported by their clinicians to reduce and stop their medication. Over two years, relapse occurred in about 44 per cent of the therapy group and about 47 per cent of the medication group, a difference which was not statistically significant.

These results suggest that the therapeutic benefit of the programme may be comparable to that of continued medication, rather than superior to it. A combined analysis of several trials reached a similar conclusion and also indicated that the efficacy might be greater in the subgroup of people with more severe symptoms at baseline. Some caution is needed, though, since participants in such trials are volunteers who are willing to attend group sessions and to practise at home, and the results may therefore not apply to all patients. Moreover, the programme requires trained instructors, who are not available in every region.
options: explain in detail how antidepressant drugs act on the brain
persuade all patients with depression to stop taking their medication
describe the history of meditation practice in Britain
criticise volunteers who fail to practise the exercises at home
summarise evidence on whether a group therapy can replace long-term medication in preventing depression from returning
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘summarise evidence on whether a group therapy can replace long-term medication in preventing depression from returning’: metin bir denemeyi ve birleşik analizi özetleyip çekincelerini verir. ‘brain’ geçen şık metinde hiç işlenmez; ‘persuade’ geçen şık yazarın temkinli tutumuyla çelişir; ‘history’ geçen şık metnin konusu değildir; ‘criticise’ geçen şık gönüllülerle ilgili çekinceyi bir eleştiriye çevirir.

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences, if added to the passage's second paragraph, would be irrelevant?
exercises.passage:
Depression often returns after a person has recovered, and the risk of recurrence increases with every previous episode. For this reason, people who have experienced recurrent episodes are commonly advised to continue taking antidepressant medication for long periods, sometimes for years. Many patients, however, would prefer to stop, either because of adverse effects or because they do not wish to depend on medication, and this has prompted interest in psychotherapy as an alternative.

Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy is a group programme, usually delivered in eight weekly sessions, which combines meditation practice with techniques from cognitive therapy. Participants are taught to notice early warning signs, such as negative thoughts, and to respond to them without being carried away. In one large British clinical trial, about 420 adults who had experienced at least three episodes of depression and were currently in remission were randomly assigned either to continue their medication or to attend the programme. Those in the therapy group were also supported by their clinicians to reduce and stop their medication. Over two years, relapse occurred in about 44 per cent of the therapy group and about 47 per cent of the medication group, a difference which was not statistically significant.

These results suggest that the therapeutic benefit of the programme may be comparable to that of continued medication, rather than superior to it. A combined analysis of several trials reached a similar conclusion and also indicated that the efficacy might be greater in the subgroup of people with more severe symptoms at baseline. Some caution is needed, though, since participants in such trials are volunteers who are willing to attend group sessions and to practise at home, and the results may therefore not apply to all patients. Moreover, the programme requires trained instructors, who are not available in every region.

Depression is diagnosed more often in women than in men in many countries.
Participants learn to see unpleasant thoughts as passing mental events rather than as facts.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Fish oil supplements, which contain omega-3 fatty acids, are among the most widely used dietary supplements in the world, largely because observational studies once suggested that people who eat a lot of oily fish suffer fewer cardiac problems. Such studies, however, cannot establish causality, since people who eat fish may also differ in their income, exercise and other habits, and the associations they reveal may therefore be misleading. In order to test the supplements directly, several large clinical trials have been carried out over the past fifteen years.

In one of the largest, about 26,000 healthy adults in the United States, none of whom had a history of heart disease, were randomly assigned to take a daily capsule of fish oil or a placebo for about five years. No significant reduction was found in the combined rate of heart attacks, strokes and deaths from cardiovascular causes. A trial of about 15,000 diabetic adults, which was conducted in the United Kingdom, produced a similar result over more than seven years. A combined analysis of earlier trials had already reached a comparable conclusion for patients at high risk.

The picture is not entirely uniform, however. One trial which used a high dose of a purified form of omega-3 in patients with raised blood fats reported a reduction of about a quarter in cardiovascular events. Critics have pointed out that the placebo in that study was a mineral oil, which may itself have had harmful effects on the control group and thus exaggerated the efficacy of the drug. Moreover, some trials have linked high doses to a slightly increased risk of an irregular heartbeat, an adverse effect which deserves attention. Overall, most experts now conclude that ordinary fish oil capsules offer little preventive benefit for the general population, although eating fish as part of a balanced diet is still recommended.
options: Observational studies have proved that fish oil capsules prevent heart attacks.
Eating oily fish should be avoided because of its adverse effects on the heart.
Large trials have found that ordinary fish oil supplements offer little protection against heart disease for most people.
Mineral oil has turned out to be a more effective supplement than fish oil.
Diabetic adults benefit far more from daily fish oil capsules than healthy adults.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Large trials have found that ordinary fish oil supplements offer little protection against heart disease for most people’: metin büyük denemelerin genel olarak anlamlı bir koruma bulmadığını anlatır. ‘proved’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, gözlemsel çalışmalar nedensellik kuramaz; ‘avoided’ geçen şık metnin sonundaki öneriye ters düşer; ‘Mineral’ geçen şık plasebo tartışmasını yanlış yorumlar; ‘Diabetic’ geçen şık yanlıştır, diyabetli yetişkinlerde de benzer, olumsuz bir sonuç bulundu.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Hearing loss is very common in later life, and observational studies have repeatedly found that older adults with poor hearing are more likely to develop dementia than those whose hearing is normal. Some neurologists have therefore suggested that hearing loss may contribute to cognitive decline, perhaps because the brain must work harder to understand speech or because people who struggle to hear tend to withdraw from social life. If this were true, treating hearing loss could be one of the simplest ways of protecting the ageing brain, which would be of great relevance to public health.

To test this possibility, investigators in the United States recruited about 980 adults aged 70 to 84 who had untreated hearing loss but no significant cognitive problems at baseline. Participants were randomly assigned either to a hearing intervention, which included properly fitted hearing aids and regular sessions with a hearing specialist, or to a control programme on healthy ageing. Their thinking skills were then measured with a set of standard tests over three years, and attrition during this period was relatively low.

Overall, no significant difference was found in the rate of cognitive decline between the two groups. However, the trial included two different groups of participants. Some had been recruited from a long-running cardiovascular study, which meant that they were older and had more risk factors for dementia, while others were healthy volunteers from the local community. Among the first subgroup, the decline was slowed by almost half, whereas no benefit was seen among the volunteers. The investigators acknowledged that this finding is not conclusive and must be confirmed by further research, since analyses of subgroups can produce spurious results. Nevertheless, hearing aids clearly improved communication and wellbeing, which are valuable outcomes in themselves.
options: Hearing Aids Prevent Dementia in All Older Adults
Why Older People Withdraw From Social Life
The Long History of an American Heart Study
How Loud Noise Causes Hearing Loss in Later Life
Do Hearing Aids Slow Cognitive Decline? Mixed Results From a Trial

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘cautious’: araştırmacılar bulgunun kesin olmadığını, tesadüfi olabileceğini ve yeni araştırmayla doğrulanması gerektiğini kabul eder. ‘dismissive’ yanlıştır, bulguyu reddetmezler; ‘enthusiastic’ yanlıştır, kesin bir başarı ilan etmezler; ‘indifferent’ ve ‘hostile’ metinde hiçbir dayanağı olmayan tutumlardır.

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences, if added to the passage's second paragraph, would be irrelevant?
exercises.passage:
Hearing loss is very common in later life, and observational studies have repeatedly found that older adults with poor hearing are more likely to develop dementia than those whose hearing is normal. Some neurologists have therefore suggested that hearing loss may contribute to cognitive decline, perhaps because the brain must work harder to understand speech or because people who struggle to hear tend to withdraw from social life. If this were true, treating hearing loss could be one of the simplest ways of protecting the ageing brain, which would be of great relevance to public health.

To test this possibility, investigators in the United States recruited about 980 adults aged 70 to 84 who had untreated hearing loss but no significant cognitive problems at baseline. Participants were randomly assigned either to a hearing intervention, which included properly fitted hearing aids and regular sessions with a hearing specialist, or to a control programme on healthy ageing. Their thinking skills were then measured with a set of standard tests over three years, and attrition during this period was relatively low.

Overall, no significant difference was found in the rate of cognitive decline between the two groups. However, the trial included two different groups of participants. Some had been recruited from a long-running cardiovascular study, which meant that they were older and had more risk factors for dementia, while others were healthy volunteers from the local community. Among the first subgroup, the decline was slowed by almost half, whereas no benefit was seen among the volunteers. The investigators acknowledged that this finding is not conclusive and must be confirmed by further research, since analyses of subgroups can produce spurious results. Nevertheless, hearing aids clearly improved communication and wellbeing, which are valuable outcomes in themselves.
options: All participants underwent hearing tests and cognitive assessments before the intervention began.
The control programme involved sessions with a health educator on topics such as exercise and nutrition.
Modern hearing aids are much smaller than earlier models and can often be connected to mobile phones.
The tests covered several skills, including memory, attention and language.
Participants in both groups were seen by the study staff at similar intervals.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Modern hearing aids are much smaller than earlier models and can often be connected to mobile phones’: ikinci paragraf denemenin yöntemini anlatır; bu cümle işitme cihazlarından söz etse de cihazların teknolojisine geçerek odağı kaydırır. ‘underwent’ geçen cümle başlangıç ölçümlerini, ‘educator’ geçen cümle kontrol programını, ‘memory’ geçen cümle testleri, ‘intervals’ geçen cümle ise izlemi anlatarak paragrafa uyar.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘No significant reduction was found in the combined rate of heart attacks, strokes and deaths from cardiovascular causes.’
options: Kalp krizleri, inmeler ve kalp-damar kaynaklı ölümlerin toplam oranında anlamlı bir artış bulundu.
Yalnızca kalp krizlerinin oranında anlamlı bir azalma bulundu.
Kalp krizleri, inmeler ve kalp-damar kaynaklı ölümlerin toplam oranında anlamlı bir azalma bulunacağı düşünülmektedir.
Kalp krizleri, inmeler ve kalp-damar kaynaklı ölümlerin toplam oranında anlamlı bir azalma bulunmadı.
Kalp krizleri, inmeler ve kalp-damar kaynaklı ölümlerin toplam oranında anlamlı bir azalma bulundu.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Kalp krizleri, inmeler ve kalp-damar kaynaklı ölümlerin toplam oranında anlamlı bir azalma bulunmadı’. İskelet: özne ‘No significant reduction’ + edilgen fiil ‘was found’ + ‘in the combined rate of …’; ‘No’ olumsuzluğu fiile taşınır. ‘artış’ geçen şık anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘Yalnızca’ geçen şık kapsamı daraltır ve olumsuzluğu kaldırır; ‘düşünülmektedir’ geçen şık zamanı ve kesinliği değiştirir; ‘bulundu’ ile biten şık olumsuzluğu atar.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Participants were randomly assigned either to a hearing intervention or to a control programme on healthy ageing.’
options: Katılımcılar rastgele olarak ya bir işitme müdahalesine ya da sağlıklı yaşlanma üzerine bir kontrol programına atandı.
Katılımcılar işitme müdahalesine mi yoksa kontrol programına mı katılacaklarını kendileri seçti.
Katılımcılar rastgele olarak hem bir işitme müdahalesine hem de sağlıklı yaşlanma üzerine bir kontrol programına atandı.
Katılımcılar rastgele olarak ya bir işitme müdahalesine ya da bir kontrol programına atanacak.
Sağlıklı yaşlanma programındaki katılımcılara rastgele olarak işitme cihazı verildi.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Katılımcılar rastgele olarak ya bir işitme müdahalesine ya da sağlıklı yaşlanma üzerine bir kontrol programına atandı’. İskelet: özne ‘Participants’ + edilgen fiil ‘were randomly assigned’ + ‘either to … or to …’. ‘seçti’ geçen şık rastgele atamayı kaldırır; ‘hem … hem de’ geçen şık ‘either … or’ yapısını bozar; ‘atanacak’ geçen şık zamanı değiştirir; ‘cihazı’ geçen şık özneyi ve anlamı değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Gözlemsel çalışmalar nedenselliği kanıtlayamaz, çünkü balık yiyen kişiler başka alışkanlıklarda da farklılık gösterebilir.’
options: Observational studies can easily establish causality, since people who eat fish may also differ in other habits.
Observational studies cannot establish causality, although people who eat fish never differ in other habits.
Clinical trials cannot establish causality, since people who eat fish may also differ in other habits.
Observational studies could not establish causality because people stopped eating fish.
Observational studies cannot establish causality, since people who eat fish may also differ in other habits.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Observational studies cannot establish causality, since people who eat fish may also differ in other habits’. İskelet: özne ‘Observational studies’ + ‘cannot establish’ + ‘causality’ + neden cümlesi ‘since …’. ‘easily’ geçen şık olumsuzluğu kaldırır; ‘never’ geçen şık bağlacı ve kipi bozar; ‘Clinical trials’ geçen şık özneyi değiştirir; ‘stopped’ geçen şık zamanı ve nedeni değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Alt gruplar üzerine yapılan analizler tesadüfi sonuçlar üretebilir.’
options: Analyses of subgroups always produce reliable results.
Analyses of subgroups can produce chance results.
Analyses of subgroups could not produce any results.
Chance results can be avoided by analysing subgroups.
Analyses of the whole sample must produce chance results.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Analyses of subgroups can produce chance results’. İskelet: özne ‘Analyses of subgroups’ + ‘can produce’ + nesne ‘chance results’; ‘-ebilir’ = ‘can’. ‘always’ geçen şık olasılığı kesinliğe çevirip anlamı tersine döndürür; ‘could not’ geçen şık olumsuzluk ekler; ‘avoided’ geçen şık anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘whole sample’ geçen şık özneyi ve kipi değiştirir.

exercises.question: Although keyhole surgery on the knee was once very common, ----.
options: most patients reported that they felt considerably better afterwards
because surgeons trimmed away the damaged tissue
which was performed through a tiny incision
so it was immediately banned in every country
a trial with a sham procedure found that it offered little real benefit for slowly developing tears
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a trial with a sham procedure found that it offered little real benefit for slowly developing tears’: ‘Although’ beklenmeyen bir sonuç ister; ameliyat yaygındı ama gerçek yararı az bulundu. ‘considerably’ geçen şık zıtlık kurmaz; ‘because’ ile başlayan şık ana cümle olamaz; ‘which’ ile başlayan şık yüklemsiz kalır; ‘so’ ile başlayan şık hem bağlacı bozar hem dayanaksızdır.

exercises.question: ----, the trial was stopped earlier than planned.
options: Because the benefit of immediate skin-to-skin care was so clear
Although no difference in deaths could be found
Unless mothers are allowed to stay with their babies
Which was coordinated by the World Health Organization
So that more babies could be placed in incubators
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Because the benefit of immediate skin-to-skin care was so clear’: deneme yarar açık olduğu için erken durduruldu. ‘Although’ ile başlayan şık mantıksız bir zıtlık kurar; ‘Unless’ ile başlayan şık geçmiş zamanlı ana cümleyle uyuşmayan bir koşuldur; ‘Which’ ile başlayan şık bağlanacak isim bulamaz; ‘incubators’ geçen şık mantıksız bir amaç bildirir.

exercises.question: Guidelines recommend that the drug should be given as early as possible, ----.
options: although it works best within the first hour
since its benefit is greatest within the first hour after an injury
which paramedics who reach the hospital
unless the patient is bleeding heavily
so that treatment can begin after three hours
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘since its benefit is greatest within the first hour after an injury’: öneri, yararın ilk saatte en büyük olmasıyla açıklanır. ‘although’ ile başlayan şık neden yerine zıtlık kurar; ‘which paramedics’ geçen şık yüklemi olmayan eksik bir yapıdır; ‘unless’ ile başlayan şık mantıksız bir koşul koyar; ‘three hours’ geçen şık metindeki uyarıyla çelişir.

exercises.question: Tidal power stations are often described as more ---- than wind farms, because the times of high and low water can be calculated years in advance.
options: fragile
reluctant
predictable
ambiguous
hostile
exercises.explanation: Gelgit saatleri yıllar önceden hesaplanabildiği için bu santrallerin üretimi ‘predictable’ (öngörülebilir) olur; cümlenin ikinci yarısı tam bu anlamı gerekçelendirir. ‘fragile’ (kırılgan) hesaplanabilirlikle ilgili değildir; ‘reluctant’ (isteksiz) yalnızca canlılar için kullanılır; ‘ambiguous’ (belirsiz) anlamca terstir; ‘hostile’ (düşmanca) ise bir enerji santralini nitelemez.

exercises.question: Because a new pair of light and dark layers is ---- on the bottom of certain glacial lakes every year, geologists can count these layers much like tree rings to date past events.
options: deposited
rewarded
accelerated
translated
forbidden
exercises.explanation: Göl tabanında her yıl yeni bir açık-koyu katman çiftinin ‘deposited’ (biriktirilmek, çökeltilmek) olması, bu katmanların ağaç halkaları gibi sayılmasını mümkün kılar. ‘rewarded’ (ödüllendirilmek) ve ‘translated’ (çevrilmek) tortu için anlam taşımaz; ‘accelerated’ (hızlandırılmak) katmanın oluşumunu değil hızını anlatır; ‘forbidden’ (yasaklanmak) ise doğal bir süreçle bağdaşmaz.

exercises.question: Plant breeders often cross modern wheat varieties with their wild relatives, which tend to be more ---- to drought and disease because they have survived for thousands of years without human help.
options: eligible
transparent
punctual
generous
resistant
exercises.explanation: Yabani akrabalar insan yardımı olmadan binlerce yıl hayatta kaldığı için kuraklığa ve hastalığa daha ‘resistant’ (dayanıklı) olur; ‘resistant to’ kalıbı cümleye tam uyar. ‘eligible’ (uygun, hak sahibi) bir bitki özelliği değildir; ‘transparent’ (saydam) ve ‘punctual’ (dakik) kuraklıkla ilişki kurmaz; ‘generous’ (cömert) ise insanlar için kullanılır.

exercises.question: Tempered glass, which is heated to more than 600°C and then cooled rapidly with jets of air, ---- into small, blunt pieces rather than long, sharp fragments when it is damaged.
options: breaking
breaks
to break
having broken
which breaks
exercises.explanation: Cümlenin öznesi ‘Tempered glass’ tır; virgüller arasındaki ‘which is heated …’ onu niteleyen bir ara yan cümledir, bu yüzden boşluğa çekimli bir ana fiil gerekir: ‘breaks’. ‘breaking’ ve ‘having broken’ çekimsiz fiilimsilerdir; ‘to break’ tek başına yüklem olamaz; ‘which breaks’ ise ikinci bir yan cümle kurarak cümleyi ana fiilsiz bırakır.

exercises.question: ---- the Forth Bridge in Scotland was completed in 1890, cantilever designs had rarely been used for railway crossings of such length.
options: Unless
Whereas
Since
Until
So that
exercises.explanation: Ana cümledeki ‘had rarely been used’ (geçmiş zamanın öncesi) köprünün tamamlandığı 1890’dan önceki dönemi anlatır; bu zaman sınırını ‘Until’ (-e kadar) kurar. ‘Unless’ (-mezse) koşul bildirir ve geçmişteki bir olguya uymaz; ‘Whereas’ iki durumu karşılaştırır ama burada karşıtlık yoktur; ‘Since’ zaman anlamında geçmiş zamanın öncesiyle kullanılmaz; ‘So that’ ise amaç bildirir.

exercises.question: Rammed-earth walls are made by compressing damp soil between wooden frames, and provided that they are protected from heavy rain, they ---- for several centuries.
options: can last
must have lasted
had lasted
would have lasted
were lasting
exercises.explanation: Cümle geniş zamanda genel bir bilgi verir (‘are made’, ‘provided that they are protected’); koşul gerçekleşirse duvarların yüzyıllarca dayanabileceğini ‘can last’ anlatır. ‘must have lasted’ geçmişe yönelik bir çıkarımdır; ‘had lasted’ ve ‘were lasting’ geçmiş zaman bildirir ve geniş zamanlı koşulla uyuşmaz; ‘would have lasted’ ise gerçekleşmemiş geçmiş bir koşul gerektirir.

exercises.question: Drumlins, ---- long axes generally point in the direction in which the ice once moved, allow geologists to reconstruct the flow of ancient glaciers.
options: which
that
whom
where
whose
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘long axes’ tepeciklere aittir (tepeciklerin uzun eksenleri), bu yüzden iyelik bildiren ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘which’ ve ‘that’ kendinden sonra sahipsiz bir isim almaz; ‘whom’ yalnızca insanlar için nesne olarak kullanılır; ‘where’ ise bir yer bildirir ve ‘long axes’ ile iyelik ilişkisi kurmaz.

exercises.question: Farmers who adopt no-till methods leave the remains of the previous crop on the field instead of ploughing them in, ---- reduces soil erosion and helps the ground hold moisture.
options: what
it
which
that
so
exercises.explanation: Boşluk, önceki cümlenin tamamını (bitki artıklarının tarlada bırakılmasını) niteleyen bir yan cümle başlatır; virgülden sonra bu işi ‘which’ yapar. ‘what’ önceki bir öğeye gönderme yapamaz; ‘it’ iki bağımsız cümleyi bağlaçsız birleştirir; ‘that’ virgülden sonra ilgi zamiri olarak kullanılmaz; ‘so’ ise öznesiz bir yüklem bırakır.

exercises.passage: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically throws a column of boiling water and steam into the air. Fewer than a thousand are thought to exist worldwide, and roughly half of them (1)---- in Yellowstone National Park in the United States. Geysers need three conditions: a supply of groundwater, an intense source of heat such as a body of magma close to the surface, and a narrow system of underground channels. Water at the bottom of these channels is under great pressure from the water above it, which allows it to become much hotter than 100°C (2)---- boiling. When some of it finally turns to steam, the expanding bubbles push water out of the top of the channel, and the sudden (3)---- in pressure causes the remaining water to boil almost instantly. (4)----, a powerful eruption follows. Because the channels are so delicate, geysers can stop erupting altogether (5)---- earthquakes or careless drilling for geothermal energy change the flow of water underground.
exercises.question: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: reflect
consist
dominate
are located
belong
exercises.explanation: Gayzerlerin yaklaşık yarısının Yellowstone’da bulunduğu anlatılır; ‘are located in’ (-de yer almak) bu anlamı verir. ‘reflect’ (yansıtmak) nesne ister ve anlam kurmaz; ‘consist’ (oluşmak) ‘of’ ile kullanılır; ‘dominate’ (hâkim olmak) nesne ister ve ‘in’ ile yer bildirmez; ‘belong’ (ait olmak) ise ‘to’ ister.

When some of it finally turns to steam, the expanding bubbles push water out of the top of the channel, and the sudden (3)---- in pressure causes the remaining water to boil almost instantly. (4)----, a powerful eruption follows. Because the channels are so delicate, geysers can stop erupting altogether (5)---- earthquakes or careless drilling for geothermal energy change the flow of water underground.
exercises.question: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: despite
without
unlike
through
beyond
exercises.explanation: Üstteki suyun basıncı sayesinde dipteki su 100°C’nin çok üstüne çıkar ama kaynamaz; ‘without boiling’ (kaynamadan) bu anlamı verir. ‘despite boiling’ suyun kaynadığını varsayar ve anlamı bozar; ‘unlike’ (-den farklı olarak) bir karşılaştırma kurar; ‘through’ (aracılığıyla) ve ‘beyond’ (ötesinde) ise ısınmayla kaynama arasındaki ilişkiyi anlatmaz.

Fewer than a thousand are thought to exist worldwide, and roughly half of them (1)---- in Yellowstone National Park in the United States. When some of it finally turns to steam, the expanding bubbles push water out of the top of the channel, and the sudden (3)---- in pressure causes the remaining water to boil almost instantly. (4)----, a powerful eruption follows. Because the channels are so delicate, geysers can stop erupting altogether (5)---- earthquakes or careless drilling for geothermal energy change the flow of water underground.
exercises.question: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: rise
balance
pattern
source
drop
exercises.explanation: Kanalın üstündeki su dışarı itilince alttaki suya binen ağırlık azalır; basınçtaki ani ‘drop’ (düşüş) suyun hemen kaynamasına yol açar. ‘rise’ (artış) anlamı tersine çevirir, çünkü basınç artarsa su kaynamaz; ‘balance’ (denge) ve ‘pattern’ (örüntü) ani bir değişimi anlatmaz; ‘source’ (kaynak) ise ‘in pressure’ ile anlamlı bir öbek kurmaz.

Fewer than a thousand are thought to exist worldwide, and roughly half of them (1)---- in Yellowstone National Park in the United States. Because the channels are so delicate, geysers can stop erupting altogether (5)---- earthquakes or careless drilling for geothermal energy change the flow of water underground.
exercises.question: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: As a result
In contrast
Otherwise
For instance
Nevertheless
exercises.explanation: Suyun bir anda kaynaması güçlü bir püskürmeye yol açar; neden-sonuç ilişkisini ‘As a result’ (sonuç olarak) kurar. ‘In contrast’ ve ‘Nevertheless’ karşıtlık bildirir, oysa püskürme beklenen sonuçtur; ‘Otherwise’ (aksi hâlde) koşulun gerçekleşmediği durumu anlatır; ‘For instance’ ise bir örnek getirir.

Fewer than a thousand are thought to exist worldwide, and roughly half of them (1)---- in Yellowstone National Park in the United States. exercises.question: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: unless
so that
if
as though
in case
exercises.explanation: Kanallar hassas olduğundan, depremler ya da sondaj yeraltındaki su akışını değiştirirse gayzerler tamamen susabilir; bu koşulu ‘if’ (eğer) kurar. ‘unless’ (-mezse) anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘so that’ (-sin diye) amaç bildirir; ‘as though’ (sanki) bir benzetme yapar; ‘in case’ (ihtimaline karşı) ise önlem anlamı taşır.

exercises.question: Because obsidian breaks into pieces with extremely sharp edges, ----.
options: it was widely used for knives and arrowheads by prehistoric communities
although it forms when lava cools too quickly for crystals to grow
whether it could be found far from any volcano remained unclear
unless the volcanic glass was polished by hand before use
which explains why it is mostly black or dark green in colour
exercises.explanation: ‘Because’ ile verilen neden (çok keskin kenarlarla kırılması) bir sonuç bekler: tarih öncesi topluluklar onu bıçak ve ok ucu için kullanmıştır (‘it was widely used for knives and arrowheads …’). ‘although’ ve ‘unless’ ile başlayan seçenekler ana cümle değildir; ‘whether … remained unclear’ keskinlikle neden-sonuç ilişkisi kurmaz; ‘black or dark green’ ise rengi keskinliğe bağlayarak mantığı bozar.

exercises.question: ----, it forms rounded shapes known as pillows, because its outer surface cools and hardens almost immediately on contact with cold water.
options: Since lava on land usually flows for many kilometres
Although lava is far hotter than the surrounding air
When lava erupts on the ocean floor
Unless lava contains a large amount of dissolved gas
As lava from most volcanoes is rich in iron
exercises.explanation: Cümlenin ikinci yarısı ‘soğuk su ile temas’tan söz eder; bu nedenle lavın okyanus tabanında püskürdüğü durumu anlatan ‘When lava erupts on the ocean floor’ gerekir. Karadaki lavın kilometrelerce akması (‘land’) suyla teması açıklamaz; havadan sıcak olması (‘surrounding air’) suyla ilgili değildir; çözünmüş gaz (‘dissolved gas’) ve demir zenginliği (‘iron’) ise yastık biçimini açıklayan soğuk su koşulunu vermez.

exercises.question: Until welding became common in shipyards during the 1940s, ----.
options: engineers will rely on robots to join the steel plates of a hull
welded joints have proved stronger than many experts expected
the hull of a modern vessel is inspected every year for corrosion
the steel plates of most ships were joined with thousands of hot metal rivets
whether riveted ships were safer is still debated by historians
exercises.explanation: ‘Until … became common in the 1940s’ geçmişte bir dönemin sonunu bildirir; ana cümle de o döneme ait bir durumu geçmiş zamanla anlatmalıdır: çelik levhalar perçinlerle birleştiriliyordu (‘… were joined with thousands of hot metal rivets’). ‘will rely on robots’ gelecek zamandır; ‘have proved stronger’ ve ‘is inspected every year’ bugüne ait bilgiler verir; ‘still debated’ ise tartışmayı anlatır ve ‘Until’ ile zaman ilişkisi kurmaz.

exercises.question: In hydroponic systems, crops are grown without any soil, ----.
options: although their roots are rarely given any nutrients at all
and their roots are placed instead in water containing carefully measured amounts of nutrients
so that the soil must be tested regularly for harmful insects
because farmers had always preferred traditional open fields

exercises.passage: During a strong earthquake, the ground beneath a building does not always behave like a solid. In loose, sandy soils that are saturated with groundwater, the repeated shaking pushes the sand grains closer together, but because the water between them cannot escape quickly enough, the pressure of that water rises sharply. When the water pressure becomes nearly equal to the weight of the soil above, the grains lose contact with one another and the soil briefly flows like a thick liquid. This process, which is known as liquefaction, was brought to international attention in 1964, when earthquakes in Niigata, Japan, and in Alaska caused serious damage. In Niigata, several apartment buildings that had suffered relatively little structural damage tilted sharply or even fell onto their sides, simply because the ground that supported them had lost its strength. Since then, engineers have developed a range of methods to reduce the risk. One approach is to make the soil denser before construction, for example by dropping heavy weights onto the site or by vibrating long steel probes into the ground. Another is to install columns of gravel, which allow the excess water to drain away during shaking so that the pressure cannot build up. Where improving the soil is too expensive, the foundations themselves can be extended downwards through the weak layer until they rest on firmer material. Yet none of these techniques is cheap, and they are far easier to apply to new projects than to existing neighbourhoods. As a result, many older districts that were built on reclaimed land or former riverbeds remain vulnerable, and in such areas the best protection may simply be accurate mapping that shows residents and planners where the danger is greatest.

exercises.passage: For maize farmers in East Africa, two of the most serious threats are stemborers, moth larvae that tunnel inside the stems, and Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches itself to the roots of the crop and draws away its water and nutrients. Since the 1990s, researchers in Kenya, who have worked closely with partners in Britain, have developed a method known as 'push-pull', which deals with both problems without relying on expensive chemicals. In this system, maize is planted together with a legume called desmodium, whose smell repels the adult moths and pushes them away from the crop. At the same time, a border of napier grass is planted around the field; this grass is even more attractive to the moths than maize, so it pulls them towards it, and many of the larvae that hatch there fail to survive. Desmodium was later found to have an unexpected benefit as well. Chemicals released by its roots appear to prevent the seeds of Striga from developing properly, and, like other legumes, it adds nitrogen to the soil. Both plants can also be cut and fed to cattle, which gives farmers an additional source of income from milk. According to its developers, the method has been adopted on more than 200,000 small farms, and several field studies have reported considerably higher maize yields than in fields planted with maize alone. Nevertheless, its spread has been slower than its supporters had hoped. The establishment of the companion plants requires labour and seeds that are not always easy to obtain, and the benefits may take more than one season to appear. Researchers have since adapted the design to drier climates and tested it against newer pests such as the fall armyworm, with encouraging but still preliminary results.
exercises.question: Which of the following would be the most suitable title for the passage?

Mısırın ekonomik tarihi (‘Economic History’) anlatılmaz; ilaçların hiçbir yerde gerekmediği (‘Anywhere’) iddiası metnin temkinli diliyle bağdaşmaz; süt geliri (‘Dairy’) yalnızca yan bir yarardır; fil otu ise zararlı bir ot (‘Dangerous Weed’) değil, güveleri çeken bir tuzak bitkisidir.

units.title: Risk ve oran ifadeleri
units.description: Göreli ve mutlak riski, kat ve oran ifadelerini doğru yorumla
units.guide:
## Strateji

Sağlık metinleri riski iki yolla verir: **göreli risk** (*twice as likely, raises the risk by 18 per cent, cuts the risk by a quarter*) ve **mutlak risk** (*1 in 7,000, 6 in 100, per 1,000 people*). Göreli rakam değişimin büyüklüğünü, mutlak rakam ise kaç kişinin etkilendiğini söyler. YÖKDİL soruları bu ikisini karıştıran şıklarla tuzak kurar.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Her risk ifadesinin yanına G (göreli) ya da M (mutlak) yaz.

2. Göreli bir ifade gördüğünde başlangıç riskini ara: *baseline risk, to begin with*.

3. Oranları aynı paydaya çevir: *1 in 100 = 10 per 1,000*.

4. Kalıpları tanı: *twice as likely* = iki kat; *half as likely* = yarı yarıya; *a 25 per cent reduction* ile *25 percentage points* aynı şey değildir.

5. Hangi grubun hangi grupla karşılaştırıldığını işaretle (*compared with non-smokers*).

## Örnek

*A newer pill doubled the risk of a clot, from about 1 to about 2 cases per 7,000 women a year.*

G: iki kat. M: 7.000 kadında yılda 1 ek vaka. “Riskin iki katına çıkması kadınların çoğunu etkiledi” diyen bir şık mutlak rakamı göz ardı eder.

## Sınav ipucu

*Per cent* ile *percentage point*, *times as likely* ile *per cent more likely* farkına dikkat et: *15 times* ile *15 per cent* çok farklıdır. Şıktaki rakamın göreli mi mutlak mı olduğunu ve hangi gruba ait olduğunu metindeki cümleyle karşılaştır.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
In October 1995, the authorities responsible for medicines in the United Kingdom issued a warning to doctors that a newer type of contraceptive pill doubled the risk of a dangerous blood clot in the veins compared with older pills. The warning was based on several studies which had not yet been published or subjected to peer review, and it was quickly reported in the press, often with alarmist headlines. Many women stopped taking the pill immediately, sometimes without consulting a clinician.

The statement that the risk had doubled was technically correct, but it described the change in relative terms only. In absolute terms, the older pills were associated with about one case of a clot per 7,000 women each year, whereas the newer ones were associated with about two cases. That is to say, the increase amounted to roughly one extra case for every 7,000 women who took the pill for a year. Moreover, pregnancy and childbirth themselves carry a considerably higher risk of such clots than either type of contraception, so the adverse effect of the pill was small by comparison.

The consequences of the warning are thought to have been serious. In the following year, there was a marked rise in unplanned pregnancies, and it is estimated that about 13,000 additional abortions were carried out in England and Wales, a figure which far exceeded the number of clots that a change of pill could have prevented. Ironically, a warning which was intended to protect public health may therefore have caused more harm than the risk it described. This episode is now widely used in medical education to illustrate why risks should be communicated in absolute as well as relative terms, ideally with numbers expressed per 1,000 or per 10,000 people.
options: argue that the newer contraceptive pills were completely free of risk
explain in detail how blood clots form in the veins
show how reporting a risk only in relative terms can lead to harmful decisions
criticise doctors for prescribing the older type of pill
describe the history of contraception in the United Kingdom
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘show how reporting a risk only in relative terms can lead to harmful decisions’: metin ‘iki kat’ uyarısının mutlak rakam verilmeden duyurulmasının istenmeyen gebelik ve kürtaj artışına yol açtığını anlatır. ‘free of risk’ geçen şık aşırıdır, risk küçük ama vardır; ‘veins’ geçen şık metinde işlenmeyen bir ayrıntıdır; ‘criticise’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir eleştiridir; ‘history’ geçen şık metnin amacı değildir.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
In October 2015, the International Agency for Research on Cancer classified processed meat, such as bacon, sausages and ham, as carcinogenic, meaning that it can cause bowel cancer. This placed it in the same category as tobacco smoke, a decision which produced sensational headlines suggesting that a sausage was as dangerous as a cigarette. However, the category describes how strong the evidence of causality is, not how large the risk is, and the two are frequently confused in public debate.

According to the agency, which reviewed hundreds of studies by epidemiologists, eating 50 grams of processed meat every day, roughly the amount in two slices of ham, increases the risk of bowel cancer by about 18 per cent. This sounds alarming, but it is a relative figure, and its meaning depends on the baseline risk. In a country such as the United Kingdom, about 6 in every 100 people who eat little processed meat are likely to develop bowel cancer in their lifetime. An 18 per cent increase raises this figure to about 7 in 100, which corresponds to roughly one additional case for every 100 people who eat that amount daily throughout their lives.

By comparison, smoking raises the risk of lung cancer many times over and is responsible for a far greater number of preventable deaths. None of this means that the link with processed meat should be dismissed, since bowel cancer is common and a small rise across a whole population still amounts to many extra cases. For this reason, most dietary guidelines recommend eating processed meat in moderation rather than avoiding it entirely. Nevertheless, readers who are told that a food raises their risk by a certain percentage should always ask what the risk was at the outset, that is, before the increase was applied.
options: Why a Sausage Is as Dangerous as a Cigarette
How Processed Meat Is Produced and Preserved
Bowel Cancer: A Disease That Only Affects Meat Eaters
The End of Meat in the British Diet
Strong Evidence, Small Risk: Making Sense of the Processed Meat Warning
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Strong Evidence, Small Risk: Making Sense of the Processed Meat Warning’: metin kanıtın güçlü, mutlak riskin ise küçük olduğunu açıklar. ‘Sausage’ geçen başlık metnin eleştirdiği manşeti tekrar eder; ‘Produced’ geçen başlık metinde işlenmeyen bir konudur; ‘Only’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, et yemeyenlerde de risk vardır; ‘End’ geçen başlık metindeki ölçülü tüketim önerisine ters düşer.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Passengers on long flights are often warned about deep vein thrombosis, a condition in which a blood clot forms in a deep vein, usually in the leg. If part of the clot breaks away and travels to the lungs, it can block a pulmonary artery, which may be fatal. Concern about the condition grew in the early 2000s after several cases were reported in the media, often under dramatic headlines, and a research project involving epidemiologists and coordinated by the World Health Organization was set up to measure the risk with greater precision.

The project found that the risk of developing such a clot roughly doubles after a journey of four hours or more, whether by air, car, bus or train, which suggests that a sedentary position, rather than flying itself, is the main cause. The risk was also found to rise with the length of the journey and with the number of flights taken within a short period. These findings sound worrying, but the absolute risk remains low. On average, about one clot was detected for every 6,000 passengers who took a flight of more than four hours, and many such clots cause no symptoms at all.

That said, the risk is not evenly distributed. It is considerably higher in people who already have other risk factors, such as recent surgery, cancer, pregnancy, obesity or a previous clot, and in women taking contraceptive pills. Obese travellers, for example, face a higher baseline risk before the journey even begins. For this reason, doctors generally advise all passengers to walk around during long journeys and to exercise their leg muscles while seated, whereas preventive medication is usually recommended only for travellers who are at high risk. In other words, the same relative increase has very different consequences depending on the starting point.
options: Flying has been shown to be far more dangerous than travelling by car, bus or train.
Every passenger on a long flight should take preventive medication.
A clot in a deep vein always travels to the lungs and causes death.
The World Health Organization found no link at all between travel and clots.
Long journeys roughly double the risk of a clot in a deep vein, but the absolute risk stays low for most travellers.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Long journeys roughly double the risk of a clot in a deep vein, but the absolute risk stays low for most travellers’: metin göreli artışla düşük mutlak riski birlikte verir. ‘Flying’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, risk her uzun yolculukta benzerdir; ‘Every passenger’ geçen şık yanlıştır, ilaç yalnızca yüksek riskliler için önerilir; ‘always’ geçen şık metindeki ‘may be fatal’ temkinini abartır; ‘no link’ geçen şık sonuçla çelişir.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
When a new treatment is described in the news, its benefit is usually expressed as a relative reduction in risk, such as a claim that a drug cuts the risk of cardiac events by a quarter. Such figures are commonly accurate, but on their own they reveal little about how many patients actually benefit. To provide a clearer picture, clinicians often use a metric called the number needed to treat, which indicates how many people must receive a treatment for one of them to avoid a particular outcome.

Consider a hypothetical example which is purely illustrative. Suppose that over five years, 4 in every 100 untreated patients have a heart attack, whereas only 3 in every 100 patients taking a preventive drug that lowers cholesterol do so. The relative reduction is 25 per cent, but the absolute reduction is just one percentage point. The calculation is straightforward: the number needed to treat is found by dividing 100 by this absolute difference, which gives a result of 100. It follows that 100 people must follow the regimen for five years to prevent one heart attack, while the other 99 receive no benefit from it, although some of them may still experience adverse effects.

The same relative reduction can therefore correspond to very different numbers needed to treat, depending on the baseline risk. If the drug were given to a group at much higher cardiovascular risk, in which 20 in every 100 untreated patients have a heart attack, a quarter of these events would be prevented, and the number needed to treat would fall to 20. This explains why doctors tend to prescribe preventive drugs more readily to patients with diabetes, high blood pressure or other comorbidities. It is worth noting that this is also why patients who are considering a treatment are encouraged to ask about its efficacy in absolute as well as relative terms.
options: warn patients against taking drugs that prevent heart attacks
prove that relative risk figures are always false
explain a measure that shows how many patients must be treated for one of them to benefit
describe how a new heart drug was developed and tested
compare the side effects of several different preventive drugs
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain a measure that shows how many patients must be treated for one of them to benefit’: metin ‘number needed to treat’ ölçütünü varsayımsal bir örnekle açıklar. ‘warn’ geçen şık metnin amacı değildir; ‘false’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, göreli rakamların doğru olduğu söylenir; ‘developed’ geçen şık yanlıştır, örnek tamamen varsayımsaldır; ‘compare’ geçen şık metinde işlenmez.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
It is widely known that the chance of having a baby with Down syndrome, a condition caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21, increases with the age of the mother. In most cases the condition is not hereditary, and maternal age is its strongest known predictor. For a woman of 20, the risk at childbirth is often given as about 1 in 1,500, whereas at 35 it is roughly 1 in 350 and at 40 it reaches approximately 1 in 100. Expressed in relative terms, a 40-year-old mother is therefore about fifteen times as likely as a 20-year-old to have a baby with the condition.

Remarkably, however, for many years most babies with Down syndrome were born to mothers under the age of 35, and in many countries a large proportion still are. This apparent contradiction is explained, as it turns out, by the number of births in each age group. Because far more babies are born to younger women, even a small risk applied to a very large group produces more cases in total than a much higher risk applied to a small group. A maternity clinic which offered prenatal screening only to older mothers would therefore miss many cases, which is one reason why many health systems now offer screening to all pregnant women regardless of age.

It follows that a high relative risk does not necessarily mean that an event is likely. Even at 40, about 99 in every 100 pregnancies are not affected by the condition. When the figures are presented to parents, counsellors are advised, unsurprisingly, to use whole numbers, such as cases per 1,000 births, rather than percentages or ratios alone, since research suggests that most people understand such frequencies with greater precision. Moreover, the risk at any age is an average, and individual risk may be higher or lower depending on the results of screening tests.
options: Down syndrome is usually inherited from parents who also have the condition.
Although older mothers face a much higher relative risk, many affected babies are born to younger mothers, who have far more babies.
Most mothers over the age of 40 have babies with Down syndrome.
Screening should be offered only to women over the age of 35.
The risk of having a baby with Down syndrome is the same at every age.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Although older mothers face a much higher relative risk, many affected babies are born to younger mothers, who have far more babies’: metnin ana fikri göreli risk ile vaka sayısı arasındaki farktır. ‘inherited’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, durum çoğunlukla kalıtsal değildir; ‘Most mothers’ geçen şık 40 yaşında bile 100 gebeliğin yaklaşık 99’unun etkilenmediğini söyleyen metinle çelişir; ‘only’ geçen şık metnin önerisini tersine çevirir; ‘same’ geçen şık riskin yaşla arttığı bilgisiyle çelişir.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the risk of having a baby with Down syndrome at the age of 35 is roughly ----.
exercises.passage:
It is widely known that the chance of having a baby with Down syndrome, a condition caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21, increases with the age of the mother. In most cases the condition is not hereditary, and maternal age is its strongest known predictor. For a woman of 20, the risk at childbirth is often given as about 1 in 1,500, whereas at 35 it is roughly 1 in 350 and at 40 it reaches approximately 1 in 100. Expressed in relative terms, a 40-year-old mother is therefore about fifteen times as likely as a 20-year-old to have a baby with the condition.

Remarkably, however, for many years most babies with Down syndrome were born to mothers under the age of 35, and in many countries a large proportion still are. This apparent contradiction is explained, as it turns out, by the number of births in each age group. Because far more babies are born to younger women, even a small risk applied to a very large group produces more cases in total than a much higher risk applied to a small group. A maternity clinic which offered prenatal screening only to older mothers would therefore miss many cases, which is one reason why many health systems now offer screening to all pregnant women regardless of age.

It follows that a high relative risk does not necessarily mean that an event is likely. Even at 40, about 99 in every 100 pregnancies are not affected by the condition. When the figures are presented to parents, counsellors are advised, unsurprisingly, to use whole numbers, such as cases per 1,000 births, rather than percentages or ratios alone, since research suggests that most people understand such frequencies with greater precision. Moreover, the risk at any age is an average, and individual risk may be higher or lower depending on the results of screening tests.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘1 in 350’: metin 35 yaş için bu oranı verir. ‘1 in 1,500’ 20 yaşa, ‘1 in 100’ 40 yaşa aittir; ‘15 in 100’ ‘fifteen times’ ifadesini yanlış yorumlar; ‘99 in 100’ 40 yaşta etkilenmeyen gebeliklerin oranıdır.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Imagine that a screening test for a certain disease is offered to all adults over 50 in a region, most of whom are asymptomatic. The disease affects about 1 in 100 people in this age group. This diagnostic test detects nine out of ten people who have the disease, but its specificity is imperfect, so it wrongly gives a positive result for about nine in every 100 people who do not. A patient who receives a positive result naturally wants to know how likely it is that he or she really has the disease. When questions of this kind were put to groups of clinicians in several studies, many of them greatly overestimated the chance, and a common answer was about 90 per cent.

The correct calculation gives a far lower answer, which becomes clear when the figures are expressed as natural frequencies, that is to say, as numbers of people rather than percentages. Out of 1,000 people who are tested, about 10 have the disease, and 9 of them will test positive. Of the remaining 990 healthy people, about 89 will also test positive. Altogether, therefore, about 98 people receive a positive result, but only 9 of them are actually ill, which means that the predictive value of a positive result is less than one in ten.

This illustrative example, which has been used widely in medical education, shows the importance of the base rate, the frequency of a disease in the population being tested. It should be noted that when a disease is rare, even a test of reasonable accuracy produces many false alarms, which can cause anxiety and lead to unnecessary procedures such as a biopsy before the disease can be ruled out with certainty. Studies suggest that both doctors and patients make fewer erroneous judgements when they are given natural frequencies, and some medical schools now teach this approach explicitly.
options: A New Test That Detects Every Case of Disease
Why Doctors Should Stop Screening Older Adults
How a Biopsy Is Carried Out
The Growth of Medical Schools in the Modern World
Why a Positive Test Result Is Often Less Alarming Than It Seems
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Why a Positive Test Result Is Often Less Alarming Than It Seems’: metin nadir hastalıkta pozitif sonucun çoğu zaman yanlış alarm olduğunu açıklar. ‘Every Case’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, test her on hastadan birini kaçırır; ‘Stop’ geçen başlık metinde olmayan bir öneridir; ‘Biopsy’ geçen başlık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır; ‘Schools’ geçen başlık metnin konusu değildir.

a flight
four hours

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Few findings in epidemiology are as conclusive and as well established as the link between smoking and lung cancer. Compared with people who have never smoked, smokers are estimated to be roughly 15 to 30 times as likely to develop the disease, and the risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked and the number of years spent smoking. A relative risk of this size is extremely unusual, and it is one reason why the causal link was accepted by most epidemiologists in the 1950s and 1960s, even before the biological mechanisms were fully understood. Smoking cessation, by comparison, gradually reduces the risk, although it rarely returns to the level of a lifelong non-smoker.

Secondhand smoke, which is inhaled by people who live or work with smokers, presents a very different picture. Studies of non-smokers whose partners smoked have generally found that their risk of lung cancer is raised by about 20 to 30 per cent. In relative terms, this increase is far smaller than the risk faced by smokers, and for an individual non-smoker the absolute risk remains low. For this reason, the link was debated for many years, and the tobacco industry repeatedly argued that such a modest association could be spurious, that is to say, caused by errors in the studies rather than by the smoke itself.

Nevertheless, most public health authorities eventually concluded that secondhand smoke is carcinogenic and also contributes to cardiovascular disease. Because millions of people were exposed to it at home and at work, even a modest relative increase was estimated to cause thousands of deaths every year in large countries. This argument was used to justify bans on smoking in workplaces, restaurants and bars, which have been introduced in many countries since the early 2000s. The example shows that a small relative risk can matter a great deal when exposure is widespread.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the causal link between smoking and lung cancer was accepted early partly because ----.
exercises.passage:
Few findings in epidemiology are as conclusive and as well established as the link between smoking and lung cancer. Compared with people who have never smoked, smokers are estimated to be roughly 15 to 30 times as likely to develop the disease, and the risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked and the number of years spent smoking. A relative risk of this size is extremely unusual, and it is one reason why the causal link was accepted by most epidemiologists in the 1950s and 1960s, even before the biological mechanisms were fully understood. Smoking cessation, by comparison, gradually reduces the risk, although it rarely returns to the level of a lifelong non-smoker.

Studies of non-smokers whose partners smoked have generally found that their risk of lung cancer is raised by about 20 to 30 per cent. In relative terms, this increase is far smaller than the risk faced by smokers, and for an individual non-smoker the absolute risk remains low. For this reason, the link was debated for many years, and the tobacco industry repeatedly argued that such a modest association could be spurious, that is to say, caused by errors in the studies rather than by the smoke itself.

Nevertheless, most public health authorities eventually concluded that secondhand smoke is carcinogenic and also contributes to cardiovascular disease. Because millions of people were exposed to it at home and at work, even a modest relative increase was estimated to cause thousands of deaths every year in large countries. This argument was used to justify bans on smoking in workplaces, restaurants and bars, which have been introduced in many countries since the early 2000s. The example shows that a small relative risk can matter a great deal when exposure is widespread.

the biological mechanisms had already been fully explained
the tobacco industry supported the research from the start
secondhand smoke had been studied before active smoking
smoking bans had already reduced the number of cases

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Five-year survival rates are often used to compare the success of cancer care between countries or over time. The metric indicates the proportion of patients who are still alive five years after their diagnosis, and to many patients and even some oncologists it seems natural to assume that a higher rate means that more lives are being saved. However, survival rates can rise sharply even when no one lives longer, a problem which is particularly important when the effects of screening asymptomatic people are being evaluated.

Consider a hypothetical and purely illustrative group of patients whose cancer would become symptomatic at the age of 67 and who would all die of it at 70. Without screening, their cancer is diagnosed at 67, and none of them survives for five years after diagnosis, so the five-year survival rate is zero. Suppose now that a screening programme detects the same malignant tumours at 60, but that treatment changes nothing and the patients still die at 70. Every one of them is now alive five years after diagnosis, and the survival rate rises to 100 per cent, even though not a single death has been prevented. This effect, which is known as lead-time bias, is caused simply by moving the date of diagnosis forward.

A further problem arises when screening detects slow-growing tumours that would never have caused harm, since adding these patients increases survival rates without affecting deaths. For these reasons, generally speaking, most experts in epidemiology argue that the benefit of screening should be judged by mortality rates, that is, the number of deaths from the disease per 100,000 people in the whole population. Ironically, research has shown that even many clinicians misunderstand this distinction and are more impressed by improvements in survival than by improvements in mortality. Such a mistake could easily lead to erroneous advice for patients.
options: Screening Has Doubled the Lifespan of Cancer Patients
How Doctors Treat Slow-Growing Tumours
The Best Countries in the World for Cancer Care
Why Mortality Rates Are Misleading
Why Rising Survival Rates Do Not Always Mean Longer Lives
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Why Rising Survival Rates Do Not Always Mean Longer Lives’: metin hayatta kalma oranlarının kimse daha uzun yaşamadan artabileceğini açıklar. ‘Doubled’ geçen başlık metinde olmayan bir iddiadır; ‘Treat’ geçen başlık metnin konusu değildir; ‘Countries’ geçen başlık giriş cümlesindeki bir ayrıntıyı abartır; ‘Mortality’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, yazar ölüm oranlarını daha güvenilir bulur.

units.title: Kuram karşılaştırma
units.description: İki kuramı karşılaştıran sosyal bilim metinlerinde görüşleri, ayrılık noktasını ve yazarın konumunu bul
units.guide:
## Strateji

YÖKDİL sosyal bilim metinleri sık sık iki kuramı karşılaştırır: A görüşü bir şey söyler, B görüşü ona karşı çıkar, yazar da sonunda bir tarafa yaslanır ya da ikisini birleştirir. Sorular üç şeyi sorar: iki görüş ne diyor, tam olarak nerede ayrılıyor ve **yazarın kendi konumu** ne. Metni bu üç kutuya ayırırsan çeldiricilerin çoğu kendiliğinden düşer.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Her görüşün sahibini ve özünü bir satırla not et: *Malthus: nüfus → kıtlık; Boserup: nüfus → yenilik*.

2. Karşıtlık işaretlerini bul: *by contrast, whereas, however, critics argue*.

3. Ayrılık noktasını yaz: olgular mı farklı, yoksa varsayımlar mı?

4. Yazarın sesini ara: *it could be argued, the most defensible position, on balance, that said*. Bu ifadeler çoğunlukla son paragraftadır.

5. Şıkta *always, entirely, proved* gibi kesin sözcükler varsa temkinli yazarla karşılaştır.

## Örnek

*Hardin argued that shared resources are inevitably destroyed. Ostrom, by contrast, documented communities that managed them for centuries. The upshot is not that Hardin was simply wrong.* İki görüş: kaçınılmaz çöküş ve yerel kurallarla başarı. Ayrılık: kanıtın türü. Yazarın konumu: *not simply wrong*, yani dengeli ama Hardin’in genellemesine eleştirel.

## Sınav ipucu

Tutum sorusunda bir görüşü aktaran cümleyi yazarın görüşü sanma. *Critics claim…* eleştirmenlerin sözüdür; yazar çoğu zaman *that said* ya da *on balance* ile kendi sesine geçer.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, the idea that the language people speak shapes the way they think was associated with the linguist Benjamin Lee Whorf, whose writings on Native American languages attracted both admiration and scepticism. In its strong form, often called linguistic determinism, the proposition holds that thought is entirely bound by the categories of one's mother tongue, so that native speakers of different languages effectively live in different mental worlds. A weaker version, which most researchers today find more plausible, claims only that language makes certain distinctions easier to notice and to remember, without preventing anyone from forming ideas for which no word exists.

The strong view was largely abandoned after the 1960s, partly because its central claims were judged not to be falsifiable and partly because successful translation between languages seemed to contradict it. If speakers were truly imprisoned by their lexicon, it was argued, a concept expressed in one language could never be conveyed in another, yet translators manage to do this every day, albeit with some loss of detail. Critics also pointed out that infants and animals appear capable of reasoning before they have any language at all.

The weak version, by comparison, has received considerable corroboration from experimental and anthropological work. A frequently cited example concerns languages that describe space with compass directions rather than with words such as 'left' and 'right'. Speakers of such languages, who must keep track of north and south in ordinary conversation, have been reported to stay oriented remarkably well in unfamiliar places. Even so, the crux of the debate is the size of these effects, which are often modest and sometimes disappear when the task is changed slightly.

It could be argued that the most defensible position lies between the two extremes. Language does not imprison thought or fix a whole worldview, but it acts as a kind of habit, quietly directing attention towards some features of experience rather than others.
options: Language may guide what speakers notice, but it does not set strict limits on what they can think.
Translation between languages is impossible because each lexicon creates a separate mental world.
Speakers of languages with compass directions are generally more intelligent than other speakers.
Whorf's writings on Native American languages have been fully confirmed by modern experiments.
Infants and animals reason more effectively than adults because they have no language.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1798 the English clergyman Thomas Malthus published an essay which argued that population, when left unchecked, tends to grow faster than the food supply. The work is often described as a founding text of demography. According to his reasoning, the number of people could double within a generation, whereas agricultural output could increase only gradually, because new land was scarce and each additional field was less productive than the last. It follows that periods of prosperity must eventually give way to starvation, disease or falling birth rates, which bring the populace back to a level of bare subsistence.

More than a century and a half later, the Danish economist Ester Boserup proposed a theory that reversed this chain of causation. In a book published in 1965, she argued that population growth is not merely a burden on agriculture but a determinant of how it is organised. When land becomes scarce, farmers are pushed to adopt more intensive methods, such as shorter rest periods for the soil, irrigation and the use of animal manure, which raise the yield of each field. From this perspective, a rising population is a stimulus to innovation rather than a sentence of decline.

The two views differ less in their description of the facts than in their assumptions about human behaviour. For Malthus, technology was largely fixed and the crux of the problem was arithmetic; for Boserup, technology was a response to pressure and therefore could not be predicted from numbers alone. Historical evidence lends support to both positions, since some agrarian societies did suffer famine after rapid growth, while others intensified production and grew more populous without any loss of livelihood.

It seems reasonable to conclude that neither theory should be treated as a universal law. Boserup's account offers a less pessimistic and, arguably, more accurate description of the last two centuries, but the speed with which farming systems adapt clearly depends on institutions, markets and access to knowledge, which received little attention in Malthus's original essay.
options: Why Famine Is Unavoidable in Agrarian Societies
Ester Boserup and the History of Irrigation
How Malthus Invented Modern Agriculture
The Decline of Birth Rates in the Twentieth Century
Population and Food: Two Opposing Accounts of Cause and Effect
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Population and Food: Two Opposing Accounts of Cause and Effect’: metin nüfus ile gıda arasındaki nedenselliği ters yönde kuran iki kuramı karşılaştırır. ‘Famine’ geçen başlık yalnızca Malthus’un görüşünü kesin doğru sayar. ‘Irrigation’ geçen başlık bir örneği başlığa taşır. ‘Invented’ geçen başlık metinde olmayan bir iddiadır. ‘Birth Rates’ geçen başlık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır.
