Metin 2: Hardin’in ortak kaynaklar trajedisi ve Ostrom’un saha kanıtları. ys9 kelimeleri: sequential, presumption, scrutiny, adolescence, interpersonal, conversational, reductive, that said ve 12 kelime daha. ys7 kelimeleri: characterise, influential, rough, partner, joint ve 15 kelime daha.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
exercises.passage:
Two of the most influential theories of how children learn were developed at roughly the same time by thinkers who never worked together: the Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget and the Soviet psychologist Lev Vygotsky. Both rejected the older presumption that a child is an empty container to be filled with facts, and both described learning as an active process. Where they differ is in the question of what drives cognitive development forward, and this difference has had lasting consequences for classroom practice.

For Piaget, development is primarily an individual achievement. Children are seen as small scientists who construct knowledge by acting on objects, and their thinking passes through a sequential series of stages from infancy to adolescence, each of which is characterised by its own logic. A corollary of this view is that teaching cannot hurry a child past a stage for which he or she is not yet ready; the role of the teacher is mainly to provide suitable materials and to wait.

Vygotsky, by contrast, placed interpersonal activity at the centre of his account. In his view, higher mental functions first appear between people, in conversational exchanges and joint tasks, and only later become part of the individual's own thinking. His best-known concept, the zone of proximal, or nearest, development, refers to the gap between what a learner can do alone and what he or she can achieve with guidance from a more capable partner. It follows that well-timed instruction does not simply wait for development but actively leads it.

It would be reductive to present the two theories as entirely opposed, since both emphasise activity and both have been refined under the scrutiny of later research. That said, Vygotsky's emphasis on language and cooperation seems better suited to explaining why children learn so much from peers and adults, and much contemporary educational research, it could be argued, has moved closer to his position than to Piaget's.
options: showing that Piaget's stages have been disproved by recent research
describing the personal rivalry between Piaget and Vygotsky
explaining why teachers should avoid providing materials to children
comparing two accounts of how children's thinking develops and judging their relative strengths
arguing that children learn only through conversation with adults
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘comparing two accounts of how children’s thinking develops and judging their relative strengths’: metin iki kuramı tanıtır, ayrıldıkları noktayı gösterir ve sonunda yazar bir tarafa yaslanır. ‘disproved’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; yazar kuramların geliştirildiğini söyler. ‘rivalry’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; iki düşünür birlikte çalışmamıştır ama kişisel bir çekişme anlatılmaz. ‘avoid’ geçen şık Piaget’nin görüşünü çarpıtır. ‘only’ geçen şık Vygotsky’yi bile abartır.

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences would best be inserted after the sentence ending 'the role of the teacher is mainly to provide suitable materials and to wait'?
exercises.passage:
Two of the most influential theories of how children learn were developed at roughly the same time by thinkers who never worked together: the Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget and the Soviet psychologist Lev Vygotsky. Both rejected the older presumption that a child is an empty container to be filled with facts, and both described learning as an active process. Where they differ is in the question of what drives cognitive development forward, and this difference has had lasting consequences for classroom practice.

For Piaget, development is primarily an individual achievement. Children are seen as small scientists who construct knowledge by acting on objects, and their thinking passes through a sequential series of stages from infancy to adolescence, each of which is characterised by its own logic. A corollary of this view is that teaching cannot hurry a child past a stage for which he or she is not yet ready; the role of the teacher is mainly to provide suitable materials and to wait.

Vygotsky, by contrast, placed interpersonal activity at the centre of his account. In his view, higher mental functions first appear between people, in conversational exchanges and joint tasks, and only later become part of the individual's own thinking. His best-known concept, the zone of proximal, or nearest, development, refers to the gap between what a learner can do alone and what he or she can achieve with guidance from a more capable partner. It follows that well-timed instruction does not simply wait for development but actively leads it.

It would be reductive to present the two theories as entirely opposed, since both emphasise activity and both have been refined under the scrutiny of later research. That said, Vygotsky's emphasis on language and cooperation seems better suited to explaining why children learn so much from peers and adults, and much contemporary educational research, it could be argued, has moved closer to his position than to Piaget's.
options: As a result, Piaget insisted that teachers should push children through the stages as quickly as possible.
However, Soviet schools adopted his ideas long before they reached Switzerland.
Errors made by children are therefore treated not as failures but as useful signs of the stage they have reached.
In the same way, children who learn with peers acquire knowledge first in conversation.
Nevertheless, an empty container is an ideal image of the mind of a young child.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1968 the ecologist Garrett Hardin published a short article that became one of the most frequently cited texts in the social sciences. He asked readers to imagine a pasture which is open to all, where each herder gains the full benefit of adding one more animal but bears only a fraction of the cost of overgrazing. Because every individual reasons in the same way, Hardin argued, the shared resource is inevitably destroyed, and he called this outcome the tragedy of the commons. His proposed remedies were either privatisation, in which the land is divided among owners, or strict regulation imposed by a centralised authority.

The political scientist Elinor Ostrom challenged this conclusion on empirical rather than theoretical grounds. Through extensive fieldwork and comparisons of cases from many countries, she documented grassroots communities that had managed forests, fisheries and irrigation systems for generations without either private ownership or state control, which suggests that solidarity among users can replace outside enforcement. Swiss mountain villages, for instance, had regulated the use of shared summer pastures through locally agreed rules for several centuries, and the livelihoods of their members were protected in this way.

Ostrom did not deny that resources are sometimes overused; her contention was that collapse is not inevitable. She identified a set of conditions under which collective management tends to succeed, including clear boundaries, rules that suit local circumstances, monitoring by the users themselves and graduated penalties for those who break the rules. In 2009 she became the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Prize in economics, a recognition which reflected how far her work had changed the field.

The upshot of this debate is not that Hardin was simply wrong. His model describes accurately what happens when users cannot communicate or trust one another, a situation akin to that of many open-ocean fisheries. Ostrom's achievement was to show that this situation is a special case rather than the general rule, and that policies based on Hardin's sweeping pessimism may destroy local institutions which already work.

Why Shared Resources Must Always Be Privatised
Swiss Villages and the History of Summer Pastures
How Ocean Fisheries Were Saved by Central Regulation
The First Woman to Win a Nobel Prize

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
Most people assume that emotions come first and bodily reactions follow: we see a bear, feel afraid and then start to run. In the 1880s the American philosopher William James and, independently, the Danish physician Carl Lange proposed exactly the opposite sequence. According to what became known as the James-Lange theory, the perception of a threatening event directly triggers physiological changes, such as a faster heartbeat, hormonal activity and tense muscles, and the emotion is nothing more than our awareness of these changes. In a famous formulation of the idea, we do not run because we are afraid; we are afraid because we run.

This account was strongly criticised in the 1920s by Walter Cannon, a specialist in physiology, and his student Philip Bard. They pointed out that very different emotions, such as fear and anger, are accompanied by almost identical bodily responses, which could hardly allow a person to tell them apart. They also observed that internal organs react too slowly to explain how quickly emotions are felt. In their alternative model, a cerebral process produces the emotional experience and the bodily response simultaneously, and neither is regarded as the cause of the other.

Later research in psychology and neuroscience has produced findings that cannot be fully explained by either position. Studies of patients with spinal injuries, who receive less feedback from the body, have yielded results marked by inconsistency, and some experiments suggest that facial expressions can slightly intensify the feelings they display. Such evidence lends partial support to James, while the speed and specificity of emotional responses still favour aspects of Cannon's critique, so neither side can claim a conclusive victory.

Most contemporary psychologists therefore regard the original dispute as somewhat misguided. Rather than asking whether body or brain comes first, current theories tend to describe emotion as the product of a continual interplay between physiological signals, the brain's interpretation of them and the context in which they occur.
options: Cannon and Bard proved that emotions are produced entirely by the heart.
William James showed that people run before they notice any threat.
Two early theories disagreed about whether bodily changes cause emotions, and later research suggests that both were partly right.
Facial expressions are the main cause of all human emotions.
Patients with spinal injuries cannot experience any emotions.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Two early theories disagreed… both were partly right’: metin James-Lange ile Cannon-Bard kuramlarını karşılaştırır ve sonraki araştırmaların ikisine de kısmen destek verdiğini söyler. ‘heart’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; Cannon beyni öne çıkarır. ‘notice’ geçen şık James’in görüşünü çarpıtır; algı tepkiden öncedir. ‘Facial’ geçen şık küçük bir bulguyu abartır. ‘spinal’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; sonuçlar yalnızca tutarsızdır.

exercises.question: The passage mainly discusses ----.
exercises.passage:
How children acquire their mother tongue with such speed has been one of the central questions of modern linguistics. From the late 1950s onwards, Noam Chomsky argued that the input children receive is too limited and too messy to explain the complex syntactic knowledge that every native speaker eventually possesses. He concluded that humans must be born with an innate capacity for language, later described as universal grammar, which contains the basic principles shared by all human languages. On this view, exposure to speech merely sets a number of switches, and language acquisition resembles the growth of a bodily organ more than a process of learning.

Usage-based theories, associated in particular with the psychologist Michael Tomasello, reject the need for such a specialised mental device. They hold that children build their grammar gradually from the specific expressions they hear in everyday conversational exchanges, whether they grow up with one language or several, relying on general cognitive abilities such as pattern recognition and the capacity to understand what other people intend. Early utterances are seen not as applications of abstract rules but as fixed phrases, which are only later broken down and generalised.

The two positions differ most clearly on the question of evidence. Chomsky's argument is largely deductive: if a structure cannot be learned from the input, it must be innate. Usage-based researchers, by comparison, rely on detailed transcripts of children's speech, which suggest that early grammar is much less abstract than the innate view predicts. Critics of Chomsky also note that the proposed universal principles have been revised so often that they are hardly falsifiable, since it is difficult to say what evidence could disprove them.

On balance, the usage-based account appears to rest on more solid empirical ground, although it has not yet explained every aspect of acquisition. It would be premature, however, to be dismissive of the nativist argument altogether, since the question of why only humans develop language in this way remains unanswered.
options: why children learn second languages more slowly than adults
the history of recording children's speech
how Chomsky's universal grammar was finally proved by experiments
the differences between the grammars of different human languages
how two theories explain children's first-language learning and which one the author finds better supported
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how two theories explain children’s first-language learning and which one the author finds better supported’: metin doğuştancı görüş ile kullanıma dayalı görüşü karşılaştırır ve yazar sonunda ikincisini daha sağlam bulur. ‘second’ geçen şık konuyu ikinci dile kaydırır. ‘recording’ geçen şık bir yöntemi ana konu yapar. ‘proved’ geçen şık metinle çelişir. ‘differences’ geçen şık metnin konusu değildir.

They hold that children build their grammar gradually from the specific expressions they hear in everyday conversational exchanges, whether they grow up with one language or several, relying on general cognitive abilities such as pattern recognition and the capacity to understand what other people intend. Early utterances are seen not as applications of abstract rules but as fixed phrases, which are only later broken down and generalised.

The two positions differ most clearly on the question of evidence. Chomsky's argument is largely deductive: if a structure cannot be learned from the input, it must be innate. Usage-based researchers, by comparison, rely on detailed transcripts of children's speech, which suggest that early grammar is much less abstract than the innate view predicts. Critics of Chomsky also note that the proposed universal principles have been revised so often that they are hardly falsifiable, since it is difficult to say what evidence could disprove them.

On balance, the usage-based account appears to rest on more solid empirical ground, although it has not yet explained every aspect of acquisition. It would be premature, however, to be dismissive of the nativist argument altogether, since the question of why only humans develop language in this way remains unanswered.
options: firm support for universal grammar
a cautious preference for the usage-based account
a complete rejection of both theories
total indifference to the question
uncritical acceptance of every argument made by Chomsky's critics

exercises.question: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1982 the social scientists James Q. Wilson and George Kelling published an article in which they argued that visible signs of disorder, such as broken windows, graffiti and litter, encourage more serious crime. Their reasoning was that a neglected environment signals that nobody is in control, which encourages potential offenders and causes law-abiding residents to withdraw from public spaces. The theory was enthusiastically adopted by metropolitan police departments in the 1990s, most famously in New York, where officers were instructed to act firmly against minor offences such as fare evasion and public drinking.

Supporters pointed to the sharp fall in New York's crime rate during that decade as evidence that the strategy worked. Critics, however, observed that crime fell by similar amounts in many American cities which had not adopted the approach, and they attributed the decline to other factors, including changes in drug markets, demographic shifts and economic growth. The causal claim at the heart of the theory therefore remains difficult to verify, and the success stories may have been somewhat overstated.

A second line of criticism concerns fairness rather than effectiveness. Researchers in criminology have argued that aggressive enforcement against minor offences led to high rates of arrest and incarceration in poorer neighbourhoods, often for behaviour that would hardly be called deviance elsewhere. Some sociologists also questioned the underlying presumption that disorder is an objective condition, since what counts as disorder is often judged differently by heterogeneous social groups.

Interestingly, controlled field experiments have offered some corroboration for the original idea, showing that people are more likely to drop litter in places that are already dirty. The most defensible reading of the evidence seems to be that disorder influences behaviour to a modest extent, but that this effect does not justify the sweeping policing strategies which were built on it.
options: Broken windows policing was solely responsible for New York's falling crime rate.
Graffiti and litter have no effect at all on human behaviour.
Criminology rejects all field experiments as unreliable.
The broken windows theory has some support, but the evidence does not justify the aggressive policing it inspired.
Police departments abandoned the theory immediately after 1982.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The broken windows theory has some support, but the evidence does not justify the aggressive policing it inspired’: yazar kuramın kısmen desteklendiğini ama sert polislik stratejilerini haklı çıkarmadığını söyler. ‘solely’ geçen şık eleştirmenlerin sorguladığı iddiayı kesinleştirir. ‘Graffiti’ geçen şık saha deneyleriyle çelişir. ‘unreliable’ geçen şık metinde yoktur. ‘abandoned’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; kuram 1990’larda benimsenmiştir.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
According to the efficient market hypothesis, which was formulated most influentially by the economist Eugene Fama in the 1960s, the prices of shares quickly reflect all the information that is publicly available. If this is true, no investor can consistently earn higher returns than the market as a whole without taking greater risks, because any useful piece of news is incorporated into prices almost immediately. A corollary of the theory is that shares are rarely overvalued or undervalued for long, so ordinary savers would do better to buy funds which simply follow the whole market.

Behavioural economists have challenged this picture by drawing on findings from psychology. They argue that investors are often overconfident, follow the crowd and rely on simple heuristics, so that prices can drift far from any reasonable valuation for long periods. Speculation on internet companies in the late 1990s, when the shares of firms with little or no profitability were bought at extraordinary prices before a severe downturn, is frequently cited as an example of such collective error.

Defenders of the hypothesis reply that bubbles are easy to identify only after they have burst. They also point out that professional fund managers, who devote enormous resources to research, have mostly failed to beat the market over long periods, which is exactly what the theory predicts. In other words, markets may be wrong, but it is extremely difficult to make a profitable trade from knowing that they are wrong.

The disagreement is therefore narrower than it first appears. Both sides largely accept that beating the market is difficult; they differ on whether prices are rational. Perhaps the most balanced position is that markets are efficient enough to frustrate most investors but not so efficient that their volatility always reflects real changes in economic value. Fittingly, in 2013 Fama shared the Nobel Prize in economics with Robert Shiller, one of his best-known critics.
options: advise readers to buy shares in internet companies
compare two views of financial markets and suggest that their disagreement is narrower than it seems
prove that professional fund managers always beat the market
describe the life and career of Eugene Fama
argue that bubbles can easily be identified in advance

Speculation on internet companies in the late 1990s, when the shares of firms with little or no profitability were bought at extraordinary prices before a severe downturn, is frequently cited as an example of such collective error.

Defenders of the hypothesis reply that bubbles are easy to identify only after they have burst. They also point out that professional fund managers, who devote enormous resources to research, have mostly failed to beat the market over long periods, which is exactly what the theory predicts. In other words, markets may be wrong, but it is extremely difficult to make a profitable trade from knowing that they are wrong.

The disagreement is therefore narrower than it first appears. Both sides largely accept that beating the market is difficult; they differ on whether prices are rational. Perhaps the most balanced position is that markets are efficient enough to frustrate most investors but not so efficient that their volatility always reflects real changes in economic value. Fittingly, in 2013 Fama shared the Nobel Prize in economics with Robert Shiller, one of his best-known critics.
options: prices react slowly to new public information
bubbles are easy to identify before they burst
most investors are overconfident and follow the crowd
fund managers who do more research always earn more
investors cannot consistently beat the market without taking greater risks
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘investors cannot consistently beat the market without taking greater risks’: 1. paragraf bunu kuramın temel sonucu olarak verir. ‘slowly’ geçen şık kuramın tersidir; fiyatlar bilgiyi hızla yansıtır. ‘burst’ geçen şık savunucuların görüşüyle çelişir. ‘overconfident’ geçen şık davranışçı iktisatçıların görüşüdür. ‘research’ geçen şık 3. paragrafla çelişir.

options: As a result, most fund managers have become extremely wealthy by predicting bubbles.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Although the theory was widely adopted in the 1990s, its central claim has never been conclusively verified.’
options: Kuram 1990’larda geniş çapta benimsenmiş olsa da temel iddiası hiçbir zaman kesin olarak doğrulanmamıştır.
Kuram 1990’larda yaygın biçimde reddedildiği için temel iddiası hiçbir zaman doğrulanmamıştır.
Kuram 1990’larda geniş çapta benimsendi ve temel iddiası kesin olarak doğrulandı.
Kuramın temel iddiası 1990’larda doğrulanmış olsa da kuram hiçbir zaman benimsenmemiştir.
Kuram 1990’larda benimsenmiş olabilir, ancak bazı iddiaları ileride doğrulanacaktır.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Kuram 1990’larda geniş çapta benimsenmiş olsa da temel iddiası hiçbir zaman kesin olarak doğrulanmamıştır’: although = -sa da, widely adopted = geniş çapta benimsenmiş, has never been verified = hiçbir zaman doğrulanmamıştır. ‘reddedildiği’ geçen şık anlamı ve bağlacı değiştirir. ‘doğrulandı’ ile biten şık olumsuzluğu kaldırır. ‘benimsenmemiştir’ geçen şık iki bilgiyi yer değiştirir. ‘ileride’ geçen şık zamanı ve kesinliği değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Many economists believe that prices may drift away from their real value for long periods.’
options: Bütün ekonomistler fiyatların her zaman gerçek değerlerini yansıttığına inanmaktadır.
Birçok ekonomist fiyatların kısa sürede gerçek değerlerine döneceğini kanıtlamıştır.
Az sayıda ekonomist fiyatların uzun süre aynı kalacağına inanmıştı.
Birçok ekonomiste göre fiyatlar uzun süreler boyunca gerçek değerlerinden uzaklaşmamalıdır.
Birçok ekonomist fiyatların uzun süreler boyunca gerçek değerlerinden uzaklaşabileceğine inanmaktadır.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Çocukların dili nasıl edindiği, dilbilimin en çok tartışılan sorularından biri olmaya devam etmektedir.’
options: Why children acquire language was one of the least debated questions in linguistics.
How children acquire language remains one of the most debated questions in linguistics.
Children acquire language faster than linguistics had predicted.
How children acquire language will no longer be debated in linguistics.
Linguistics has stopped debating how adults acquire a second language.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘How children acquire language remains one of the most debated questions in linguistics’: nasıl = how, devam etmektedir = remains. ‘least’ geçen şık soruyu ve zamanı değiştirir. ‘faster’ geçen şık başka bir karşılaştırma kurar. ‘longer’ geçen şık geleceğe ve olumsuzluğa çevirir. ‘adults’ geçen şık özneyi ve konuyu değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Bazı araştırmacılara göre toplumsal düzensizlik suç üzerinde ılımlı bir etkiye sahip olabilir.’
options: According to all researchers, social disorder certainly causes most crime.
Some researchers argue that crime has a modest effect on social disorder.
According to some researchers, social disorder had no effect on crime.
According to some researchers, social disorder may have a modest effect on crime.
Researchers have proved that social disorder will have a strong effect on crime.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘According to some researchers, social disorder may have a modest effect on crime’: bazı = some, olabilir = may, ılımlı = modest. ‘certainly’ geçen şık niceleyiciyi ve kesinliği değiştirir. ‘argue’ geçen şık neden ile sonucu yer değiştirir. ‘had no effect’ geçen şık olumsuzluk ekler. ‘strong’ geçen şık etkinin derecesini ve kesinliği değiştirir.

exercises.question: Malthus expected rapid population growth to end in famine, ----.
options: whereas Boserup saw it as a pressure that encourages new farming methods
because Boserup agreed with him on every point
so food production always grew faster than population
unless he had published his essay in 1798
which is why famines never occurred in agrarian societies
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘whereas Boserup saw it as a pressure that encourages new farming methods’: whereas iki görüş arasındaki karşıtlığı doğru kurar. ‘agreed’ geçen şık metinle çelişir ve neden bağı anlamsızdır. ‘always’ geçen şık Malthus’un beklentisini tersine çevirir. ‘unless’ ile kurulan koşul anlamsızdır. ‘never’ geçen şık ana cümleyle çelişir.

exercises.question: ----, Piaget believed that teaching could not hurry a child through the stages of development.
options: Although he thought that children learn mainly from conversation
Since he saw development as an individual process with a fixed sequence
Unless children were taught by more capable partners
Because Vygotsky had proved that stages do not exist
Even though he regarded each stage as having its own logic
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Since he saw development as an individual process with a fixed sequence’: sabit sıralı evreler fikri, öğretimin çocuğu hızlandıramayacağı sonucunun nedenidir. ‘conversation’ geçen şık Vygotsky’nin görüşüdür. ‘partners’ geçen koşul cümlesi mantığı bozar. ‘proved’ geçen şık Piaget’nin evrelerini yok sayar. ‘Even though’ ile başlayan şık yanlış bağlaç kullanır; kendine özgü mantık bir karşıtlık değil, nedendir.

exercises.question: Ostrom did not deny that shared resources are sometimes overused, ----.
options: so she recommended privatisation in every case
because Hardin had never studied the problem
and therefore she rejected all forms of collective management
unless the users were unable to communicate
but she showed that collapse is not inevitable when users can make and enforce their own rules
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘but she showed that collapse is not inevitable when users can make and enforce their own rules’: but kabul ile itiraz arasındaki geçişi doğru kurar. ‘privatisation’ geçen şık Hardin’in çözümünü Ostrom’a yükler. ‘studied’ geçen şık ilgisiz bir neden verir. ‘rejected’ geçen şık Ostrom’un görüşüyle çelişir. ‘unable’ geçen koşul cümlesi yapıyı bozar.

exercises.question: Conservators examining the medieval tapestry under ultraviolet light found that its once vivid reds had ---- considerably, apparently because it had hung for centuries opposite a large window.

exercises.question: Because sea cucumbers ---- organic particles from the sediment as they feed, they play an important role in recycling nutrients on the seabed.
options: extract
abandon
reveal
imitate
dispose
exercises.explanation: Deniz hıyarları beslenirken tortudaki organik parçacıkları ayıklayıp alır; ‘extract … from’ (bir şeyden çıkarmak, ayırmak) kalıbı hem ‘from the sediment’ ile hem de besin döngüsü anlamıyla uyumludur. ‘abandon’ (terk etmek) ve ‘imitate’ (taklit etmek) beslenmeyle ilgisizdir; ‘reveal’ (ortaya çıkarmak) besinlerin geri dönüşümünü açıklamaz; ‘dispose’ ise ‘of’ edatı ister ve ‘atmak’ anlamı verir.

exercises.question: In many pastoral societies, livestock is not merely a source of food but also a ---- of wealth and social status, which is why animals are rarely slaughtered for everyday meals.
options: sacrifice
shortage
burden
remedy
measure
exercises.explanation: Hayvanlar yalnızca besin kaynağı değil, aynı zamanda zenginliğin ve toplumsal statünün ölçüsüdür; bu yüzden gündelik yemek için kesilmezler: ‘measure’ (ölçü, gösterge). ‘shortage’ (kıtlık) ve ‘burden’ (yük) zenginlikle çelişir; ‘remedy’ (çare) anlam kurmaz; ‘sacrifice’ (kurban) ise hayvanların nadiren kesildiği bilgisiyle çelişir.

exercises.question: The copper-alloy heads, ---- by artists in the West African city of Ife several centuries ago, are admired for their remarkably naturalistic portrayal of human faces.
options: casting
to be cast
cast
which casting
having cast
exercises.explanation: Cümlenin ana fiili ‘are admired’ dır; boşluk ‘The copper-alloy heads’ öznesini edilgen anlamla niteler (başlar sanatçılar tarafından dökülmüştür), bu yüzden geçmiş zaman ortacı ‘cast’ gerekir. ‘casting’ ve ‘having cast’ etken anlam verir, yani başları döken özne gibi gösterir; ‘to be cast’ gelecekte yapılacak bir işi anlatır; ‘which casting’ ise dil bilgisi açısından bozuk bir yapıdır.

exercises.question: By the time the first European ships reached the islands, local fishermen ---- a system of seasonal bans to protect their reef fisheries for generations.
options: have maintained
had maintained
will have maintained
are maintaining
maintain
exercises.explanation: ‘By the time … reached’ geçmişteki bir andan önce tamamlanmış ve süregelmiş bir durumu anlatır; ‘for generations’ ile birlikte past perfect gerekir: ‘had maintained’. ‘have maintained’ şimdiki zamana bağlanır; ‘will have maintained’ geleceği anlatır; ‘are maintaining’ ve ‘maintain’ ise geçmişteki bir olayla zaman uyumu kurmaz.

exercises.question: ---- the artist's signature is missing from the canvas, experts are fairly confident about who painted it because of the distinctive way the sky has been painted.
options: Because
Unless
Provided that
As long as
Even though
exercises.explanation: İmzanın olmaması ile uzmanların ressamın kim olduğundan emin olması arasında zıtlık vardır; bu zıtlığı ‘Even though’ (-diği hâlde) kurar. ‘Because’ neden bildirir ve anlamı bozar; ‘Unless’, ‘Provided that’ ve ‘As long as’ koşul bildirir, oysa imzanın eksik olması bir koşul değil, bilinen bir gerçektir.

exercises.question: Not until marine biologists began using remotely operated vehicles ---- how many species depend on the deep-sea sponge grounds of the North Atlantic.
options: did they realise
they realised
had realised
they had realised
realising
exercises.explanation: Cümle ‘Not until …’ ile başladığı için ana cümlede devrik yapı (yardımcı fiil + özne + fiil) gerekir: ‘did they realise’. ‘they realised’ ve ‘they had realised’ devrik değildir; ‘had realised’ öznesizdir; ‘realising’ ise çekimli bir yüklem olamaz.

exercises.question: Many anthropologists argue that naming a child after a dead grandparent helps to strengthen family ties, ---- it reinforces the idea that the dead remain part of the family line.
options: whereas
unless
so that
in that
even if
exercises.explanation: İkinci yan cümle, ad vermenin aile bağlarını nasıl güçlendirdiğini açıklar; ‘in that’ (-dığı için, şu bakımdan) bu açıklama ilişkisini kurar. ‘whereas’ zıtlık, ‘unless’ ve ‘even if’ koşul bildirir; ‘so that’ ise amaç bildirir, oysa ölülerin aileden sayılması fikrini pekiştirmek ad vermenin amacı olarak değil, nasıl işlediğinin açıklaması olarak verilmiştir.

exercises.passage: Among the Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest coast of North America, the potlatch was a ceremonial feast at which a host family gave away large quantities of goods, such as blankets, carved boxes and preserved food, to invited guests. To outsiders, the practice often seemed wasteful, since a host could (1)---- years of accumulated wealth in a single event. Anthropologists, however, came to see it as a central institution (2)---- rank was confirmed, names and rights were passed on, and marriages and deaths were publicly recognised. Guests were not merely receivers of gifts; by accepting them, they acted as witnesses (3)---- the claims made by the host. (4)----, giving goods away brought prestige rather than poverty, because a family's standing depended on what it could give, not on what it kept. In 1885, the Canadian government banned the ceremony, partly because officials believed it (5)---- their efforts to make Indigenous communities adopt European ideas of property. The ban was removed from the law in 1951, and potlatches are still held today.

spend
borrow
inherit
postpone

because few of them could speak the local languages fluently

exercises.passage: Ukiyo-e, the Japanese woodblock prints that flourished during the Edo period (1603–1868), are often admired today as the work of individual artists such as Hokusai and Hiroshige. Yet each print was in fact the product of a collaborative system in which no single person controlled the entire process. A publisher, who financed the project and judged what the public would buy, usually commissioned a design from an artist. The artist then produced a drawing in ink on thin paper, which was pasted face down onto a block of cherry wood and cut away by a skilled carver, so that the original drawing was destroyed in the process. Separate blocks were carved for each colour, and a printer applied the inks by hand, positioning each sheet carefully so that the colours lined up. Because hundreds or even thousands of copies could be made from one set of blocks, prints were relatively cheap, and they were bought by merchants and craftsmen as well as by wealthy collectors. Popular subjects included actors, famous beauties and, increasingly in the nineteenth century, landscapes and travel scenes. Ironically, the very features that made ukiyo-e commercial products in Japan helped to make them prized works of art abroad. After Japan opened its ports to Western trade in the 1850s, large numbers of prints reached Europe, where painters such as Van Gogh and Degas studied their flat areas of colour, bold outlines and unusual viewpoints. Some critics have argued that the European enthusiasm for these images, often called Japonisme, reveals as much about European tastes as about the prints themselves. Even so, few would deny that this exchange helped to reshape modern painting in the West.

exercises.passage: When a large whale dies in the open ocean, its body usually sinks to the seabed, where it may provide food for deep-sea organisms for decades. Such events, which are known as whale falls, were first studied in detail in the late 1980s, after researchers in a submersible came across a skeleton off the coast of California by chance. Since then, scientists have also sunk whale carcasses deliberately in order to observe how they are consumed over time. These studies suggest that a whale fall passes through several overlapping stages. In the first, which can last for months or even a few years, mobile scavengers such as sleeper sharks and hagfish remove most of the soft tissue. Next, smaller animals, including worms and crustaceans, colonise the bones and the surrounding sediment, which has been enriched by the remains. In the final stage, bacteria break down the fats stored inside the bones, releasing chemical compounds that support communities resembling those found around hydrothermal vents. One of the most unusual inhabitants of these sites is Osedax, a worm without a mouth or stomach, which relies on bacteria living inside its body to digest the bones. Some researchers have suggested that whale falls may act as stepping stones, allowing species that depend on chemical energy to spread across the ocean floor between widely separated vents. This hypothesis remains difficult to test, however, because natural whale falls are hard to locate in the vast, dark deep sea. Moreover, since commercial whaling greatly reduced whale numbers over the past two centuries, the number of carcasses reaching the seabed has presumably declined, with consequences for deep-sea life that are still poorly understood.
exercises.question: Which of the following could be the best title for the passage?

Balinaların neden battığı (‘Sink’) yalnızca ilk cümlede geçer; ticari avcılık (‘Whaling’) son cümledeki bir ayrıntıdır; hidrotermal bacalar (‘Vents’) yalnızca karşılaştırma için anılır; denizaltılar (‘Submersibles’) ise keşfin nasıl yapıldığını gösteren küçük bir bilgidir.

exercises.passage: When a large whale dies in the open ocean, its body usually sinks to the seabed, where it may provide food for deep-sea organisms for decades. Such events, which are known as whale falls, were first studied in detail in the late 1980s, after researchers in a submersible came across a skeleton off the coast of California by chance. Since then, scientists have also sunk whale carcasses deliberately in order to observe how they are consumed over time. These studies suggest that a whale fall passes through several overlapping stages. In the first, which can last for months or even a few years, mobile scavengers such as sleeper sharks and hagfish remove most of the soft tissue. Next, smaller animals, including worms and crustaceans, colonise the bones and the surrounding sediment, which has been enriched by the remains. In the final stage, bacteria break down the fats stored inside the bones, releasing chemical compounds that support communities resembling those found around hydrothermal vents. One of the most unusual inhabitants of these sites is Osedax, a worm without a mouth or stomach, which relies on bacteria living inside its body to digest the bones. Some researchers have suggested that whale falls may act as stepping stones, allowing species that depend on chemical energy to spread across the ocean floor between widely separated vents. This hypothesis remains difficult to test, however, because natural whale falls are hard to locate in the vast, dark deep sea. Moreover, since commercial whaling greatly reduced whale numbers over the past two centuries, the number of carcasses reaching the seabed has presumably declined, with consequences for deep-sea life that are still poorly understood.
exercises.question: The word "presumably" in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
options: probably
certainly
rarely
suddenly
gradually
exercises.explanation: ‘presumably’ kesin bilinmeyen ama akla yatkın görülen bir durumu anlatır; en yakın anlamlısı ‘probably’ (muhtemelen) dır. ‘certainly’ (kesinlikle) yazarın ihtiyatlı tutumuyla çelişir; ‘rarely’ (nadiren) sıklık, ‘suddenly’ (aniden) ve ‘gradually’ (yavaş yavaş) ise değişimin hızını anlatır, olasılık bildirmez.

exercises.passage:
Kerem: The power station on the coast had to shut down for two days last week because jellyfish blocked the pipes that bring in cooling water.
Laura: ----
Kerem: Partly, yes. With fewer fish around to eat young jellyfish or compete with them for plankton, their numbers can grow very quickly.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: How long does it usually take to repair a power station?
Do jellyfish actually sting people who swim near power stations?
Is that because overfishing has removed many of their natural competitors?
I didn't know that the station used sea water for cooling.
Couldn't they simply have used river water instead?
exercises.explanation: Kerem’in ‘Partly, yes’ yanıtı bir neden sorusuna verilmiştir ve ardından balıkların azalmasının denizanalarını çoğalttığını açıklar; bu yüzden boşluğa ‘Is that because overfishing has removed many of their natural competitors?’ gelmelidir. Onarım süresi (‘repair’), sokma (‘sting’) ve nehir suyu (‘river’) soruları Kerem’in balık açıklamasıyla bağlanmaz; ‘I didn’t know …’ ise bir soru olmadığı için ‘Partly, yes’ yanıtına uymaz.

exercises.passage:
Ayşe: Why are the lights in the textile gallery so dim? Visitors keep complaining that they can hardly see the patterns.
Tom: ----
Ayşe: I see. So the low light is a compromise between letting people see the textiles and keeping them for future generations.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: The gallery was redesigned by a well-known architect five years ago.
Most visitors prefer to look at the paintings upstairs anyway.
We are planning to add more labels explaining the history of each piece.
The museum's electricity bill has risen sharply this year.
Natural dyes fade quickly when exposed to strong light, and the damage cannot be reversed.
exercises.explanation: Ayşe’nin son sözü loş ışığı, kumaşları görmek ile onları gelecek kuşaklar için korumak arasında bir uzlaşma olarak açıklar; bu, ışığın doğal boyaları kalıcı olarak soldurduğunu söyleyen yanıttan çıkar: ‘Natural dyes fade quickly …’. Mimar (‘architect’), etiketler (‘labels’) ve elektrik faturası (‘electricity’) koruma gerekçesi vermez; ziyaretçilerin üst kattaki resimleri tercih etmesi (‘upstairs’) ise kumaşları korumakla ilgili değildir.

Supervisor: ----

options: Perhaps you should have recorded the interviews on video.
That's normal; trust usually takes a long time to build in fieldwork.
Family disputes are rarely studied by anthropologists.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Were it not for the careful notes kept by a nineteenth-century missionary, much of what we know about the island's funeral customs would have been lost.
options: Much of our knowledge about the island's funeral customs survives only because a nineteenth-century missionary kept careful notes.
A nineteenth-century missionary lost most of the notes he had kept about the island's funeral customs.
Although a nineteenth-century missionary kept careful notes, we know very little about the island's funeral customs.
The island's funeral customs were changed by a nineteenth-century missionary who kept careful notes about them.
If a nineteenth-century missionary keeps careful notes, the island's funeral customs will not be lost.
exercises.explanation: ‘Were it not for …’ (… olmasaydı) devrik koşul yapısıdır: misyonerin notları olmasaydı bilgilerimizin çoğu kaybolacaktı, yani bu bilgiler notlar sayesinde günümüze ulaşmıştır: ‘Much of our knowledge … survives only because …’. Notların kaybolduğu (‘lost most’) ve az şey bildiğimiz (‘very little’) seçenekleri anlamı tersine çevirir; misyonerin gelenekleri değiştirdiği (‘changed’) kaynakta yoktur; ‘keeps … will not be lost’ ise geçmişe ait gerçek dışı durumu geleceğe ait gerçek koşula çevirir.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Only when the varnish, which had darkened over the centuries, was removed did the painting's original colours become visible again.
options: The varnish was removed because the painting's original colours had darkened over the centuries.
Although the darkened varnish was removed, the painting's original colours did not become visible again.
Removing the varnish darkened the painting's original colours, which had been visible for centuries.
The painting's original colours could not be seen again until the varnish that had darkened over the centuries was removed.
Before the varnish darkened over the centuries, it had been removed to protect the painting's original colours.
exercises.explanation: ‘Only when … did …’ yapısı bir olayın ancak diğeri gerçekleştikten sonra olduğunu anlatır: renkler ancak kararmış vernik temizlenince yeniden göründü, yani ‘could not be seen again until the varnish … was removed’. Kararan şeyi renkler olarak gösteren (‘because’) seçenek özneyi değiştirir; ‘did not become visible’ anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘Removing the varnish darkened’ neden-sonucu bozar; ‘protect’ içeren seçenek ise olayların sırasını değiştirir.

exercises.passage: In 2001, the artist David Hockney proposed that some European painters from the fifteenth century onwards had used optical devices, such as lenses and curved mirrors, to project images onto their canvases. According to this view, the sudden increase in realistic detail in paintings of that period was not due to drawing skill alone. ---- Supporters of the theory, however, point out that using such devices would still have required great skill, so the claim does not reduce the painters' achievement.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Hockney himself is best known for his brightly coloured paintings of swimming pools in California.
As a result, every realistic painting of the period must have been produced with the help of mirrors.
Many art historians rejected the idea, arguing that it implied the great masters had in some sense cheated.
Similarly, the camera obscura was used by early astronomers to observe the sun safely.
Optical devices are also widely used by modern photographers and filmmakers.
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki cümle ‘however’ ile kuramın destekçilerinin bir itiraza yanıtını verir: bu aygıtları kullanmak da beceri gerektirdiğinden iddia ressamların başarısını küçültmez. Bu yanıtın karşılık verdiği itiraz, ustaların bir anlamda hile yaptığı eleştirisidir: ‘Many art historians rejected the idea, arguing that it implied the great masters had in some sense cheated.’ Hockney’nin yüzme havuzları (‘swimming pools’) ve fotoğrafçılar (‘photographers’) konuyu dağıtır; ‘every realistic painting’ kuramı abartır ve bir itiraz içermez; ‘Similarly … astronomers’ ise yanlış bağlaçla konuyu gökbilime kaydırır.

exercises.passage: It is estimated that a large proportion of the animals living in the open ocean below about 200 metres can produce their own light. This ability, known as bioluminescence, serves a variety of purposes. ---- Some fish, for example, have light-producing organs along their bellies that match the faint light coming from above, so that predators looking up cannot see their outline.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: However, very few animals in the deep ocean are able to produce any light at all.
The light is usually produced by a chemical reaction involving a compound called luciferin.
Deep-sea animals are often studied with the help of remotely operated vehicles.
Therefore, most fish living in shallow waters have gradually lost their eyes.
One of the most common, surprisingly, is helping an animal to avoid being seen.
exercises.explanation: Paragraf ışık üretmenin birçok amaca hizmet ettiğini söyler; boşluktan sonraki ‘for example’ cümlesi ise balıkların karınlarındaki ışıkla avcılardan saklanmasını örnek verir. Bu örneği hazırlayan, amaçlardan birinin görünmemek olduğunu söyleyen cümledir: ‘One of the most common, surprisingly, is helping an animal to avoid being seen.’ ‘very few’ içeren seçenek ilk cümleyle çelişir; ‘luciferin’ içeren seçenek amaçtan ışığın üretim biçimine kayar ve ‘for example’ ile bağlanmaz; araç (‘vehicles’) ve göz kaybı (‘eyes’) ise konudan sapar.

exercises.passage: (I) When the Terracotta Army was discovered near the city of Xi'an in 1974, its thousands of clay soldiers appeared to be a uniform grey-brown colour. (II) The figures had been buried near the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor to unify China, who died in 210 BC. (III) Close examination, however, revealed traces of bright pigments, showing that the soldiers had originally been painted in red, green, blue and purple. (IV) Unfortunately, once the figures were exposed to the dry air, the layer of lacquer beneath the paint began to curl and flake off within minutes. (V) For this reason, conservators have developed chemical treatments to hold the paint in place, and excavation has proceeded slowly.

exercises.passage: (I) Long before the compass reached the Pacific, Polynesian navigators sailed thousands of kilometres across the ocean without instruments. (II) They memorised the points on the horizon where particular stars rise and set, and used them to keep their canoes on course at night. (III) During the day, they could judge their direction from the pattern of ocean swells, which they sometimes felt through the movement of the hull rather than saw. (IV) The double-hulled canoes they sailed were built from wood and plant fibre and could carry families, animals and plants to new islands. (V) Signs such as the flight of seabirds returning to land at dusk also told them that an island lay nearby.

exercises.passage: (I) The oceans absorb roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide released by human activity each year, which slows the warming of the atmosphere. (II) This benefit comes at a cost, however, because the dissolved gas makes seawater more acidic. (III) Carbon dioxide is also released naturally by volcanoes, although in much smaller amounts than those produced by burning fossil fuels. (IV) In more acidic water, organisms such as oysters, mussels and tiny sea snails find it harder to build and maintain their shells. (V) Some shellfish farms on the Pacific coast of the United States have already reported losses of young oysters that have been linked to these changes.

options: I

exercises.passage: (I) Among many Aboriginal Australian peoples, knowledge of the land has traditionally been preserved in songlines, long cycles of songs that follow routes across the country. (II) Aboriginal Australians are thought to have lived on the continent for at least 50,000 years, which makes theirs one of the oldest continuous cultures in the world. (III) Each song describes features such as waterholes, hills and rock formations in the order in which a traveller would meet them. (IV) By singing the verses in sequence, a person could therefore find the way across hundreds of kilometres of unfamiliar land. (V) In this sense, songlines functioned not only as religious and cultural texts but also as a kind of spoken map.

units.title: Tarihsel anlatı
units.description: Tarih metinlerinde olayların sırasını ve nedenlerini izle: kurumlar, ticaret, teknoloji ve kentler
units.guide:
## Strateji

Tarihsel anlatı metinleri olayları zaman sırasıyla verir, ama sorular çoğu zaman sıranın kendisini değil, **olaylar arasındaki neden-sonuç bağını** sorar: "hangisi önce oldu?", "neden geriledi?", "bunun sonucu ne oldu?". Çeldiriciler metindeki tarihleri doğru verir ama olayları yanlış sıraya ya da yanlış nedene bağlar.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Okurken kenara mini bir zaman çizelgesi çıkar: *1837 broşür → 1840 pul → mektup sayısı ikiye katlandı*.

2. Zaman işaretlerini işaretle: *before, after, by then, within a decade, it was not until*.

3. Neden ifadelerini ayrı işaretle: *because, as a result, led to, partly in order to, a combination of factors*.

4. *partly, mainly, a combination of* tek bir neden olmadığını söyler; şıkta *only* ya da *solely* varsa dikkat et.

5. Tarih içeren her şıkkı zaman çizelgende kontrol et.

## Örnek

*Construction began in 1859. After forced labour was ended in the mid-1860s, the company relied on machines. The canal opened in 1869.* Sıra: başlangıç → zorla çalıştırmanın kaldırılması → makineler → açılış. Neden: makinelere geçişin nedeni işgücünün kaybıdır, makinelerin icadı değil.

## Sınav ipucu

*It was not until 1840 that…* yapısı "ancak 1840’ta" demektir; olay daha önce gerçekleşmemiştir. Bu yapıyı gördüğün soruda daha erken bir tarih veren şık yanlıştır.

nodes.title: Sosyal: Peni posta ve Hansa Birliği
nodes.description: Metin 1: Rowland Hill ve 1840 posta reformu. Metin 2: Hansa Birliği: kuzey Avrupa’nın tüccar ağı ve gerilemesi. ys9 kelimeleri: uniformity, procedural, documentation, adhesive, emigration, charitable, taxation, budgetary ve 15 kelime daha. ys7 kelimeleri: publish, label, complicate, informal, supporter ve 12 kelime daha.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
Before 1840, sending a letter in Britain was an expensive and complicated business. Charges were calculated according to the distance travelled and the number of sheets used, and many reformers regarded them as a form of hidden taxation. They were normally payable by the recipient rather than the sender, which meant that an unwanted letter could simply be refused at the door. Members of Parliament enjoyed the privilege of free postage, which was widely abused. Ordinary people, meanwhile, often relied on informal tricks, such as hidden marks on the outside of a letter, to pass on brief messages without paying.

In 1837 a former schoolteacher named Rowland Hill published a pamphlet in which he argued that the actual cost of carrying a letter was small. Most of the expense, he claimed, lay in the procedural burden of calculating and collecting charges. His proposal was radical in its simplicity: a uniform rate of one penny for letters up to a certain weight, paid in advance by the sender, regardless of distance. As documentation that the fee had been paid, he suggested a small printed label which could be attached to the envelope.

Despite opposition from officials of the Post Office, who doubted that such low charges could cover the costs, the reform was approved by Parliament, and the first adhesive stamp, later known as the Penny Black, came into use in May 1840. The number of letters sent rose dramatically, more than doubling within the first year, although the budgetary consequences were serious and postal revenue took many years to recover to its earlier level.

The longer-term consequences, which also included better connectivity between towns, were social as much as financial. Cheap postage gave literate working people a reason to write, made it easier for families separated by emigration to stay in touch with distant correspondents, and allowed charitable organisations to reach large numbers of supporters. Within a few decades, similar systems had been adopted by many other countries, and the uniformity of postal charges came to be taken for granted.
options: why Members of Parliament lost the privilege of free postage
the design and printing of the first adhesive stamp
how Rowland Hill's postal reform changed both the economics and the social role of letter writing
how the Post Office opposed every reform in the nineteenth century
the history of hidden marks used by ordinary people
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how Rowland Hill’s postal reform changed both the economics and the social role of letter writing’: metin reformdan önceki durumu, Hill’in önerisini, mali sonuçları ve toplumsal etkileri sırayla anlatır. ‘lost’ geçen şık metinde yoktur. ‘design’ geçen şık pulu ana konu yapar; pul yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır. ‘every’ geçen şık aşırı genellemedir. ‘hidden’ geçen şık 1. paragraftaki bir örneği ana konu yapar.

In 1837 a former schoolteacher named Rowland Hill published a pamphlet in which he argued that the actual cost of carrying a letter was small. Most of the expense, he claimed, lay in the procedural burden of calculating and collecting charges. His proposal was radical in its simplicity: a uniform rate of one penny for letters up to a certain weight, paid in advance by the sender, regardless of distance. As documentation that the fee had been paid, he suggested a small printed label which could be attached to the envelope.

Despite opposition from officials of the Post Office, who doubted that such low charges could cover the costs, the reform was approved by Parliament, and the first adhesive stamp, later known as the Penny Black, came into use in May 1840. The number of letters sent rose dramatically, more than doubling within the first year, although the budgetary consequences were serious and postal revenue took many years to recover to its earlier level.

The longer-term consequences, which also included better connectivity between towns, were social as much as financial. Cheap postage gave literate working people a reason to write, made it easier for families separated by emigration to stay in touch with distant correspondents, and allowed charitable organisations to reach large numbers of supporters. Within a few decades, similar systems had been adopted by many other countries, and the uniformity of postal charges came to be taken for granted.

Hidden marks, by contrast, were rarely used by ordinary people.
Nevertheless, letters continued to be paid for by the recipient after 1840.
Similarly, the railway network was expanding rapidly during the same decade.
Payment in advance, however, raised a practical problem: how could postal workers know whether a letter had been paid for?

exercises.passage:
The Hanseatic League, which dominated trade in northern Europe for several centuries, was neither a sovereign state nor a formal alliance in the modern sense, but something closer to a loose trading bloc. It began in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries as a series of agreements among German merchants who travelled together for protection, and it gradually developed into a decentralised association of trading towns led by Lübeck, each of which kept its allegiance to its own ruler. At its height in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, the network is estimated to have included between seventy and two hundred towns, depending on how membership is defined.

Grain, timber, furs and wax were shipped westwards from the Baltic, while cloth, salt and wine travelled in the opposite direction. Dried fish from Norway, which was in great demand in Catholic Europe, was another key part of this mercantile system. In major foreign cities such as London, Bruges, Bergen and Novgorod, the merchants maintained permanent trading posts, which enjoyed special legal privileges.

Because the league had no permanent army or central treasury, its main weapon was economic. When a ruler threatened its privileges, member towns could agree to stop trading with his territory, and such an embargo often proved remarkably effective. In 1370, after a war against Denmark, the league obtained a peace treaty that confirmed its hegemony in the Baltic, and some historians have compared its behaviour to that of a cartel.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
The department store, which seems such an ordinary feature of city life today, was a genuinely new institution when it emerged in the middle of the nineteenth century. Earlier retail trade had been dominated by small specialist shops, where prices were rarely displayed and were usually settled through bargaining between seller and customer. Shoppers were also expected to buy once they had entered, a convention which strongly discouraged casual browsing.

Several large stores in Paris, London and New York broke with these habits at roughly the same time, and historians disagree about which deserves to be called the first. The best-known example is Le Bon Marché in Paris, which was transformed from the 1850s onwards by Aristide Boucicaut and his wife Marguerite. Their store introduced fixed and clearly marked prices, allowed customers to enter freely without any obligation to purchase, and accepted the return of unwanted goods. Profitability depended on economies of scale and rapid turnover rather than on large margins for each item, and the business was later housed in a purpose-built building of iron and glass.

These innovations were made possible by wider changes in the economy. Factories were producing goods in large quantities thanks to growing standardisation, railways and horse-drawn buses brought shoppers from the suburbs into the centre of the metropolis, and the purchasing power of the bourgeoisie was rising steadily. Newspaper advertising and seasonal sales, which were organised to clear old stock, attracted further crowds.

The social consequences were significant. Department stores provided one of the few public spaces in which middle-class women could spend time unaccompanied, and they became major employers, with a workforce of young shop assistants, many of whom lived in rooms provided by the store. Critics, including the novelist Emile Zola, portrayed these businesses as engines of consumerism that destroyed the livelihood of small shopkeepers, a concern which continues to be raised about large retailers today.
options: Le Bon Marché was undoubtedly the first department store in the world.
Emile Zola's novels caused the decline of small shopkeepers.
Bargaining remained the normal method of setting prices in large stores.
Department stores were built mainly to provide housing for young workers.
The department store was a new kind of business whose methods depended on, and in turn changed, nineteenth-century society.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The department store was a new kind of business whose methods depended on, and in turn changed, nineteenth-century society’: metin yeni yöntemleri, onları mümkün kılan ekonomik değişimleri ve toplumsal sonuçları anlatır. ‘undoubtedly’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ilk mağaza tartışmalıdır. ‘novels’ geçen şık neden-sonucu çarpıtır; Zola yalnızca eleştirmişti. ‘Bargaining’ geçen şık yeni mağazaların terk ettiği yöntemi anlatır. ‘housing’ geçen şık bir ayrıntıyı amaç yapar.

exercises.question: The passage mainly discusses ----.
exercises.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, loading and unloading ships was one of the slowest and most expensive stages of international trade. Goods arrived at the docks in sacks, barrels and boxes of every size, and each item had to be lifted by a large workforce of port labourers, a process which could keep a vessel in port for a week or more. Theft was common, and the cost of handling cargo at both ends of a voyage sometimes exceeded the cost of the voyage itself.

The change that transformed this system is usually credited to Malcom McLean, an American trucking businessman. He reasoned that it would be more efficient to lift entire truck bodies onto ships than to unpack their contents. In April 1956 a converted oil tanker, the Ideal X, carried fifty-eight metal boxes from Newark, near New York, to Houston, and the age of the shipping container is commonly dated from this voyage. By one widely cited estimate, the cost of loading cargo fell to a small fraction of its previous level, a clear demonstration of economies of scale.

Widespread adoption, however, took more than a decade. Different companies initially used boxes of different sizes, so standardisation had to be agreed internationally in the late 1960s before containers could move smoothly between ships, trains and trucks. Ports also required an overhaul, with huge cranes, and the logistics of supplying the American military during the Vietnam War greatly increased the demand for containers.

The consequences extended well beyond shipping. Employment in the ports declined sharply, causing widespread redundancy and the loss of a traditional livelihood, and many old city-centre ports, including those of London and New York, lost their traffic to new terminals with more space and deeper water. Their abandoned docks were later redeveloped, often through gentrification. Lower transport costs encouraged manufacturers to move production offshore and to build a global supply chain, which has led some economists to argue that the humble metal box contributed as much to globalisation as many trade agreements did.
options: the life and business career of Malcom McLean
the causes of theft in twentieth-century ports
the role of the American military in the Vietnam War
the origins, spread and wider effects of container shipping
the reasons why trade agreements failed after 1956
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the origins, spread and wider effects of container shipping’: metin eski yükleme yöntemini, 1956 yolculuğunu, yavaş yayılmayı ve ekonomik sonuçları anlatır. ‘career’ geçen şık bir kişiyi ana konu yapar. ‘theft’ geçen şık bir ayrıntıdır. ‘Vietnam’ geçen şık konteynere talebi artıran bir etkeni ana konu yapar. ‘failed’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences, if added to the passage's second paragraph, would be irrelevant?
exercises.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, loading and unloading ships was one of the slowest and most expensive stages of international trade. Goods arrived at the docks in sacks, barrels and boxes of every size, and each item had to be lifted by a large workforce of port labourers, a process which could keep a vessel in port for a week or more. Theft was common, and the cost of handling cargo at both ends of a voyage sometimes exceeded the cost of the voyage itself.

The change that transformed this system is usually credited to Malcom McLean, an American trucking businessman. He reasoned that it would be more efficient to lift entire truck bodies onto ships than to unpack their contents. In April 1956 a converted oil tanker, the Ideal X, carried fifty-eight metal boxes from Newark, near New York, to Houston, and the age of the shipping container is commonly dated from this voyage. By one widely cited estimate, the cost of loading cargo fell to a small fraction of its previous level, a clear demonstration of economies of scale.

Widespread adoption, however, took more than a decade. Different companies initially used boxes of different sizes, so standardisation had to be agreed internationally in the late 1960s before containers could move smoothly between ships, trains and trucks. Ports also required an overhaul, with huge cranes, and the logistics of supplying the American military during the Vietnam War greatly increased the demand for containers.

The consequences extended well beyond shipping. Employment in the ports declined sharply, causing widespread redundancy and the loss of a traditional livelihood, and many old city-centre ports, including those of London and New York, lost their traffic to new terminals with more space and deeper water. Their abandoned docks were later redeveloped, often through gentrification. Lower transport costs encouraged manufacturers to move production offshore and to build a global supply chain, which has led some economists to argue that the humble metal box contributed as much to globalisation as many trade agreements did.
options: Unlike earlier experiments with large boxes, his approach treated the ship, the truck and the train as parts of a single transport system.
The boxes could be lifted directly from truck frames onto the ship, so their contents never had to be touched.
Today, containers are also converted into homes, offices and small shops in many cities.
According to a story he later told, McLean had first noticed how much time was lost while waiting at a port years earlier.
To finance the venture, he bought a shipping company, a step that was unusual for a trucking businessman.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1853 the emperor Napoleon III appointed Georges-Eugène Haussmann as prefect of the Seine, giving him responsibility for one of the most ambitious programmes of urban reconstruction ever attempted. At that time central Paris consisted largely of narrow, overcrowded medieval streets, where poor sanitation had contributed to serious outbreaks of cholera in earlier decades. Over the following seventeen years, large parts of the old city were demolished, and they were replaced by long, straight boulevards lined with apartment buildings of uniform height and style.

The works were not limited to what could be seen above ground. Haussmann and his engineers built a vast network of sewers and new channels for drinking water, which greatly improved the supply of clean water, and they created large public parks on the edges of the city. Railway stations were linked to one another by broad avenues, and new markets, schools and hospitals were constructed across the metropolis.

Historians have long debated the motives behind this transformation. Officially, the aims were hygiene, the easing of traffic and the beautification of the capital. Critics at the time, however, claimed that wide boulevards were intended to make it harder for rebels to build barricades and easier for troops to move quickly, since Paris had experienced several uprisings in previous decades. Most historians now regard this military motive as real but secondary, although it suited an authoritarian regime.

The costs of the project were considerable, both financial and social. Haussmann financed the works largely through borrowing, using methods which were attacked as irregular, so that the city became heavily indebted, and he was dismissed in 1870 shortly before the fall of the empire. Tens of thousands of working-class residents, who could no longer afford rents in the rebuilt centre, were pushed towards the outskirts, a process that some scholars describe as an early form of gentrification. Nevertheless, the plan shaped the appearance of modern Paris and influenced city planners in many other countries.
options: Rebuilding Paris: Motives, Methods and Costs of Haussmann's Plan
Napoleon III and the Fall of the Second Empire
Why Barricades Disappeared from European Cities
Cholera and Sewers in Nineteenth-Century London
The Parks and Gardens of Modern Paris
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Rebuilding Paris: Motives, Methods and Costs of Haussmann’s Plan’: metin projenin yapılış biçimini, tartışılan nedenlerini ve mali ve toplumsal bedelini anlatır. ‘Fall’ geçen başlık bir ayrıntıyı başlık yapar. ‘Barricades’ geçen başlık tartışmalı bir nedeni genelleştirir. ‘London’ geçen başlık kenti değiştirir. ‘Gardens’ geçen başlık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
Before the French Revolution, France had no single system of weights and measures. Historians have estimated that several hundred different units were in use. The same name could also refer to quite different quantities from one town to the next, which made trade between regions complicated and gave aristocratic landowners opportunities to cheat peasants when rents were collected in grain. Demands for uniformity and standardisation were frequently expressed in the lists of complaints that were drawn up across the country in 1789.

The revolutionaries saw the reform of measurement as part of a wider project, led by an increasingly centralised state, to replace inherited customs with rational and secular principles. In 1791 the Academy of Sciences recommended that the new unit of length, the metre, should be defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator, measured along the line passing through Paris. Two astronomers spent about seven years surveying the section of this line between Dunkirk and Barcelona, working with great precision and careful calibration of their instruments through a period of war and political violence, and the metric system was formally adopted in 1799.

Acceptance by ordinary people, however, proved much slower than its designers had expected. Many citizens continued to use familiar local units, which were tied to everyday practices and could be divided easily into halves, thirds and quarters. In 1812 Napoleon allowed a compromise system that mixed traditional names with metric values, and it was not until 1840 that the exclusive use of metric units was made compulsory in France, after an enactment of 1837.

From the middle of the nineteenth century the system spread rapidly abroad, helped by the growth of international trade and science, both of which depended on consistency of measurement. In 1875 seventeen countries signed the Metre Convention, which established an international bureau to maintain the standards. Today almost every country uses metric units officially, although older measures survive in everyday use in a few places, most notably the United States.
options: Napoleon invented the metric system in 1812 to replace revolutionary measures.
The metre was defined by measuring the whole distance from the pole to the equator directly.
The metric system, created during the Revolution for rational and practical reasons, was accepted only slowly before it spread worldwide.
Ordinary French people immediately adopted metric units in 1799.
The United States was the first country to make metric units compulsory.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The metric system, created during the Revolution for rational and practical reasons, was accepted only slowly before it spread worldwide’: metin sistemin doğuşunu, yavaş kabulünü ve yayılmasını anlatır. ‘invented’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; Napolyon yalnızca bir uzlaşma sistemine izin verdi. ‘whole’ geçen şık yanlıştır; yalnızca Dunkirk ile Barcelona arasındaki bölüm ölçüldü. ‘immediately’ geçen şık 3. paragrafla çelişir. ‘States’ geçen şık metnin tersidir.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
exercises.passage:
In 1602 the government of the Dutch Republic merged several competing trading companies into a single consortium, the United East India Company, usually known by its Dutch initials, VOC. The new company was granted a monopoly on Dutch trade with Asia for twenty-one years. It also received remarkable powers: it could build forts, maintain armed forces and sign treaties with local rulers as if it were a sovereign state. These powers reflected the mercantile ambitions of the republic and the fact that trade in spices such as pepper, nutmeg and cloves was highly profitable but also extremely risky, since a single voyage could take years and many ships never returned.

What made the VOC unusual was the way in which this risk was shared. Earlier ventures had typically been financed for a single voyage, after which the profits were divided and the partnership was dissolved. The VOC, by contrast, raised permanent capital from a broad public, and ownership was divided into shares which could be bought by anyone, from wealthy merchants to servants. Because investors could not easily withdraw their money, a market soon developed in Amsterdam in which shares were traded among investors. This early trade in securities, with all its volatility and speculation, is widely regarded as a forerunner of the modern stock exchange.

The company's commercial success was accompanied by considerable violence. In the 1620s, for example, its forces conquered the Banda Islands in present-day Indonesia, the main source of nutmeg, and much of the local population was killed or driven out. Such episodes, together with the annexation of territory elsewhere in Asia, have led modern historians to treat the company as an instrument of colonialism and imperialism as well as an innovation in finance.

The VOC remained powerful throughout the seventeenth century, but corruption, growing debts and competition from its English rival weakened it in the following century. Deeply indebted and close to bankruptcy, it was dissolved in 1799, after almost two hundred years of operation, and its possessions were taken over by the Dutch state.
options: the history of spices in medieval Europe
why the English company was more successful than the VOC from the start
the lives of servants who invested in the VOC
the geography of the Banda Islands
the VOC as both a financial innovation and an instrument of colonial power
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the VOC as both a financial innovation and an instrument of colonial power’: metin şirketin hisse sistemini ve şiddet içeren sömürgeci yönünü birlikte anlatır. ‘medieval’ geçen şık dönemi ve konuyu değiştirir. ‘start’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; şirket 17. yüzyıl boyunca güçlüydü. ‘lives’ geçen şık bir ayrıntıyı ana konu yapar. ‘geography’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.
