exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
The idea of linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea by a waterway was ancient, but it was realised only in the nineteenth century, largely through the persistent diplomacy of Ferdinand de Lesseps, a former French diplomat. In 1854 he obtained permission from the ruler of Egypt, Said Pasha, to form a company that would build and operate a canal across the narrow strip of land at Suez. Shares in this international consortium were sold mainly to French investors, while the Egyptian government took a large stake and supplied much of the labour, a burden which was later criticised severely.

Construction began in 1859 and lasted ten years. In the early stages tens of thousands of Egyptian labourers were recruited through a system of forced labour, and working conditions were harsh. After this practice was ended under international pressure in the mid-1860s, the company relied increasingly on steam-powered digging machines, which also eased the logistics of supplying workers in the desert. The canal, which was about 164 kilometres long when it opened in November 1869, required no locks, since the two seas lie at roughly the same level.

Its effect on trade was considerable. The sea route between Britain and India was shortened by several thousand kilometres, because ships no longer had to sail around Africa. Interestingly, the canal favoured steam propulsion over sail, as the winds in the Red Sea were unreliable, and it therefore accelerated the decline of large sailing vessels on routes to Asia.

Heavily indebted and close to insolvency, Egypt was eventually forced to sell its shares, which the British government bought in 1875. Britain occupied the country seven years later, partly in order to protect this route of great geopolitical value, and critics have treated the episode as a classic case of imperialism. The canal remained under foreign control until 1956, when the Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser announced its nationalisation, an action that led to an international crisis in which both superpowers pressed Britain and France to withdraw their troops.
options: The Life of Ferdinand de Lesseps
From Concession to Crisis: The Suez Canal and Its Consequences
Why Sailing Ships Were Faster Than Steamships
How Egypt Built the Canal Without Foreign Investment
The Locks of the Suez Canal
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘From Concession to Crisis: The Suez Canal and Its Consequences’: metin 1854 izninden 1956 krizine kadar kanalın yapımını ve sonuçlarını kronolojik olarak anlatır. ‘Life’ geçen başlık bir kişiyi ana konu yapar. ‘Faster’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir. ‘Without’ geçen başlık metnin tersidir; Fransız yatırımcılar hisse aldı. ‘Locks’ geçen başlık yanlıştır; kanalın havuzu yoktur.

units.title: Uzun cümle çevirisi
units.description: Fen, sağlık ve sosyal alan metinlerinde YÖKDİL tarzı uzun cümleler: önce çekirdeği, sonra niteleyicileri bul
units.guide:
## Strateji

YÖKDİL ve YDS çeviri sorularında cümleler 30–40 kelimeyi bulur: yan cümleler, ortaçlar ve edat öbekleri asıl iskeleti gizler. Uzun cümleyi baştan sona kelime kelime çevirmeye çalışırsan kaybolursun. Önce **çekirdeği** (özne + ana fiil + nesne) bul, sonra **niteleyicileri** tek tek bu iskeletin üzerine yerleştir. Türkçede niteleyiciler ismin önüne, İngilizcede çoğu zaman arkasına gelir; çeviride sıra tersine döner.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. **Ana fiili bul:** *which, that, who* ile başlayan yan cümlelerin ve virgül arası açıklamaların fiillerini ayıkla; geriye kalan çekimli fiil ana fiildir.

2. **Özneyi ve nesneyi bağla:** "Kim/ne, ne yaptı, neyi?" sorusuyla çekirdeği Türkçe kur.

3. **Niteleyicileri ekle:** yan cümleyi ismin önüne sıfat gibi koy (*the plates which had been chosen* → seçilmiş olan levhalar).

4. **Şıkları beş açıdan tara:** zaman, çatı (etken/edilgen), olumsuzluk, niceleyici (*most, all, some*) ve temkin (*may, about, roughly*).

## Örnek

*Surveys which were carried out before construction had shown that a layer of chalk ran beneath the Channel.*
Çekirdek: *Surveys had shown that…* → araştırmalar … göstermişti. Niteleyiciler: *which were carried out before construction* → inşaattan önce yapılan; *that a layer of chalk ran beneath the Channel* → bir tebeşir katmanının Manş’ın altında uzandığını.

## Sınav ipucu

Yanlış şıklar genellikle tek bir öğeyi bozar: *most* "hepsi" olur, *may* kesinliğe dönüşür ya da özne ile nesne yer değiştirir. Çekirdeği doğru kuran iki şık kalırsa niceleyiciye ve temkine bak; fark çoğu zaman oradadır.

nodes.title: Fen: Manş Tüneli ve gelgit santrali
nodes.description: Metin 1: Manş Tüneli’ni mümkün kılan jeoloji ve hassasiyet. Metin 2: Rance gelgit santrali ve çevresel bedeli. ys9 kelimeleri: calibration, precision, instrumentation, feasibility, margin of error, porous, brittle, durability ve 13 kelime daha. ys7 kelimeleri: struggle, channel, continent, route, kilometre ve 7 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
When the tunnel beneath the English Channel opened in 1994, it was described as one of the greatest engineering achievements of the twentieth century. The idea of linking Britain and France by land, however, had been discussed for almost two hundred years. Earlier attempts had been abandoned largely for political and financial reasons, since many British leaders feared that a fixed connection to the continent would weaken the country’s defence. When work finally began in 1988, the engineers faced a challenge of a different kind, because they had to dig about 38 kilometres beneath the sea, a longer stretch under the sea than any earlier tunnel.

The feasibility of the project depended largely on geology. Surveys which were carried out before construction had shown that a layer of chalk mixed with clay ran almost continuously beneath the Channel. This rock was soft enough to be cut quickly but firm and nearly waterproof, unlike the more porous and brittle chalk above it, which could have allowed sea water to flood the works. The route was therefore designed to follow this favourable layer, even though the tunnel then had to rise and fall with the rock rather than run in a straight line.

Eleven huge boring machines were used, working from both coasts at once and pushed forward by hydraulic arms. Their direction was controlled with laser guidance, and the calibration of this instrumentation was checked repeatedly, since even a small margin of error over such a distance could have left the two halves missing each other. When the teams finally met under the sea in December 1990, the tunnels were out of line by less than half a metre, a level of precision that was widely celebrated at the time. The durability of the concrete lining was another priority, given the risk of corrosion from salt water. The project nevertheless suffered serious delays and cost far more than had been estimated, and the operating company struggled with debt for many years after the opening.
options: The tunnel was delayed for two centuries because engineers could not dig beneath the sea.
The tunnel was completed on time and well within its original budget.
The Channel Tunnel succeeded largely because its route followed a suitable rock layer and its machines were guided with great precision.
Porous chalk is the best kind of rock for building tunnels under the sea.
British leaders supported a fixed connection to the continent for reasons of defence.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The Channel Tunnel succeeded largely because its route followed a suitable rock layer and its machines were guided with great precision.’: metin başarının jeolojiye ve yönlendirmedeki hassasiyete dayandığını anlatır. ‘engineers’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, eski girişimler siyasi ve mali nedenlerle bırakılmıştır; ‘budget’ geçen şık tersini söyler, proje gecikmiş ve çok pahalıya mal olmuştur; ‘Porous’ geçen şık tersini söyler, gözenekli tebeşir su sızdırabilirdi; ‘supported’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, liderler savunmanın zayıflayacağından korkmuştur.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Unlike wind turbines and photovoltaic panels, whose output can change from one hour to the next, the tides are governed by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun and can therefore be predicted many years in advance. This regularity has long attracted engineers. In 1966, the first large tidal power station was opened at the mouth of the river Rance in north-western France, where the difference between high and low water can exceed ten metres. The plant consists of a barrage, essentially a low dam across the river mouth, in which about two dozen turbines are installed.

As the tide rises, sea water flows through the turbines into a reservoir behind the barrage. When the tide falls, the stored water is released towards the sea again, so that electricity can be generated in both directions. Because the available energy is roughly proportional to the square of the tidal range, a site with twice the range offers about four times the power, which explains why only a small number of coastlines are considered suitable. With a capacity similar to that of a medium-sized hydroelectric plant, the station remained the largest of its kind for more than four decades.

The environmental consequences, however, have been the subject of considerable scrutiny. Construction closed the river mouth for about three years, and the reduced movement of water has led to the accumulation of mud and to noticeable changes in the populations of fish and plankton. Some studies suggest that the ecosystem has since reached a new balance, although it differs from the one that existed before. Proposals for much larger barrages, such as one across the Severn in Britain, have repeatedly failed the test of economic feasibility, partly because of their enormous cost and partly because of the damage they might cause to wetland habitats on which migratory birds depend.
options: Why Tidal Power Has Replaced Wind Turbines
Tidal Power: Predictable Energy with Environmental Costs
The Moon and the Origin of Ocean Tides
Migratory Birds of British Wetlands
How France Became the Largest Energy Producer in Europe
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Tidal Power: Predictable Energy with Environmental Costs’: metin gelgit enerjisinin öngörülebilirliğini, Rance santralinin işleyişini ve çevresel bedelini anlatır. ‘Replaced’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur, rüzgâr yalnızca karşılaştırma için anılır; ‘Origin’ geçen başlık ilk cümledeki bir ayrıntıyı ana konu yapar; ‘Birds’ geçen başlık son cümledeki bir örnektir; ‘Producer’ geçen başlık metinde desteklenmez.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
At the beginning of the twentieth century, waterborne diseases such as typhoid and cholera were still among the leading causes of death in many rapidly growing cities. Sand filters had already reduced the danger in some places, but the decisive step came in 1908, when Jersey City in the United States became one of the first cities to add chlorine to its public water supply on a continuous basis. The decision was largely the work of John Leal, a doctor who advised the private water company. He had to defend the method in court, where critics argued that adding a poison to drinking water could never be safe.

The results soon silenced most of these objections. Chlorine, in the small quantities which are needed for disinfection, kills most bacteria within minutes, and it leaves behind a residue that continues to protect the water as it travels through kilometres of pipes. Within a few decades the practice had spread to most cities in industrialised countries, and deaths from typhoid fell dramatically. One influential study estimated that clean water technologies, including filtration and chlorination, may account for roughly half of the fall in mortality in large American cities during that period. Their contribution to the decline in infant mortality, according to the same study, was even larger.

Chlorination is not, however, free of problems. In the 1970s, chemists discovered that chlorine reacts with natural organic matter in water to form by-products, some of which are considered possibly carcinogenic when consumed over many years. Regulators responded by setting limits on these contaminants rather than abandoning the method, since most public health experts agree that the risk from untreated water is far greater. A second limitation became evident in 1993, when an outbreak in Milwaukee made several hundred thousand people ill. The parasite responsible was resistant to chlorine, and investigators concluded that disinfection must be combined with careful filtration, good sanitation and regular monitoring of the sources from which water is taken.
options: describe how chlorination improved public health and what limitations it still has
argue that chlorine should be removed from drinking water
explain the chemistry of organic matter in rivers
compare the water systems of Jersey City and Milwaukee
praise John Leal for inventing the sand filter
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘describe how chlorination improved public health and what limitations it still has’: metin önce klorlamanın ölümleri nasıl azalttığını, sonra yan ürünler ve dirençli parazit gibi sınırlarını anlatır. ‘removed’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, düzenleyiciler yöntemi bırakmamıştır; ‘chemistry’ geçen şık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır; ‘compare’ geçen şık iki şehri karşılaştırmayan metni yanlış özetler; ‘inventing’ geçen şık yanlıştır, kum filtreleri zaten vardı.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
Every year, according to estimates by the World Health Organization, bites from venomous snakes kill somewhere between 80,000 and 140,000 people. Several hundred thousand others are left with permanent disabilities, most of them farmers and children in rural parts of Africa, Asia and Latin America. The only specific treatment is antivenom, a medicine whose basic method of production has changed surprisingly little since it was developed by the French scientist Albert Calmette in the 1890s. In this method, horses or sheep are injected with small but gradually increasing doses of venom, so that their immune response produces antibodies against the toxins without the animals becoming seriously ill.

Blood is then taken from the animals, and the antibodies, which are concentrated in the liquid part of the blood, are separated and purified before being given to patients through an intravenous line. Although the efficacy of this approach has saved countless lives, it suffers from several well-known limitations. Because the venom of each species has a different chemical composition, an antivenom made for the snakes of one region may be of little use against those of another, and products must therefore be matched carefully to local species. Furthermore, since the antibodies come from animals, a considerable proportion of patients develop allergic reactions, some of which can be life-threatening.

Practical obstacles add to these clinical problems. Many antivenoms need to be stored in refrigerators, which are often unavailable in the remote clinics where bites occur, and a full course of treatment can cost more than a farming family earns in several months. Partly for these reasons, the World Health Organization classified snakebite as a neglected tropical disease in 2017 and later launched a strategy to halve the deaths and the morbidity it causes by 2030. Researchers are now testing antibodies produced in the laboratory rather than in animals, as well as drugs that can be taken by mouth, which might allow clinicians to begin treatment before a patient reaches hospital. Whether their affordability will match their promise, however, remains uncertain.
options: Snakebites have become rare since the 1890s thanks to the method developed by Calmette.
Antibodies produced in laboratories have already replaced antivenoms made from animals.
Antivenom, made by an old method, saves many lives but has limitations that new research is trying to overcome.
Allergic reactions are now the main cause of death after snakebites.
Farmers in rural areas are no longer at risk because refrigerators are widely available.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Antivenom, made by an old method, saves many lives but has limitations that new research is trying to overcome.’: metin yöntemin eskiliğini, faydasını, sınırlılıklarını ve yeni araştırmaları anlatır. ‘rare’ geçen şık ilk cümledeki ölüm sayılarıyla çelişir; ‘replaced’ geçen şık fazla ileri gider, bu antikorlar hâlâ deneniyor; ‘Allergic’ geçen şık metinde ölüm nedeni olarak sunulmaz; ‘refrigerators’ geçen şık tersini söyler, buzdolapları çoğu zaman yoktur.

nodes.title: Sosyal: patent hukuku ve LiDAR
nodes.description: Metin 1: Venedik’ten bugüne patent hukuku. Metin 2: Lazer taramasıyla ormanın altındaki kentler. ys9 kelimeleri: aristocratic, monarch, parliamentary, lawmaker, enactment, profitable, antitrust, entrepreneurship ve 13 kelime daha. ys7 kelimeleri: publish, foundation, prompt, hinder, authority ve 18 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
The idea that an inventor should enjoy a temporary right to profit from a new device is now so familiar that it is easy to forget how recent and how contested it once was. Historians usually trace the first written patent law to a statute which was passed by the Republic of Venice in 1474. It granted anyone who built a new and ingenious machine in the city the exclusive right to use it for ten years. Anyone who copied such a device without permission could be fined, and the copy itself was to be destroyed, a provision suggesting that the authorities regarded innovation as a valuable public asset.

In England, by contrast, the power to grant exclusive rights was frequently abused by the monarch, who sold monopolies over ordinary goods such as salt and playing cards to aristocratic favourites. Parliamentary opposition grew, and in 1624 lawmakers passed the Statute of Monopolies, which abolished most of these privileges but expressly permitted patents for genuinely new inventions for a period of fourteen years. Legal historians often describe this enactment as the foundation of modern patent law, since it separated the reward of creativity from the arbitrary favours of the crown.

At the heart of the system lies a bargain between the inventor and society. In exchange for a monopoly of limited duration, the inventor must publish a description detailed enough for others to reproduce the invention once the protection expires. Whether this bargain actually encourages entrepreneurship, however, remains a matter of debate among economists. Some studies suggest that patents matter greatly in sectors such as medicines, where copying a finished product is cheap but development is extremely costly, whereas many startups appear to rely more on secrecy and on being first to the market. Critics also argue that excessively broad patents can hinder later inventors and make medicines less affordable, while they remain highly profitable for their owners. Such concerns have prompted courts and antitrust regulators to examine broad patents closely.
options: How Venice Became the Richest City in Europe
Patent Law: Its Origins and a Continuing Debate
The English Monarchy and the Salt Trade
Why Startups No Longer Need Secrecy
The Life of the First Venetian Inventor
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Patent Law: Its Origins and a Continuing Debate’: metin Venedik ve İngiltere’deki kökenleri anlatır, sonra patentlerin yeniliği gerçekten teşvik edip etmediği tartışmasına geçer. ‘Richest’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur; ‘Salt’ geçen başlık tek bir örneği ana konu yapar; ‘Secrecy’ geçen başlık tersini söyler, birçok girişim gizliliğe dayanır; ‘Life’ geçen başlık metinde hiç anılmayan bir kişiden söz eder.

The idea that an inventor should enjoy a temporary right to profit from a new device is now so familiar that it is easy to forget how recent and how contested it once was. Historians usually trace the first written patent law to a statute which was passed by the Republic of Venice in 1474. It granted anyone who built a new and ingenious machine in the city the exclusive right to use it for ten years. Anyone who copied such a device without permission could be fined, and the copy itself was to be destroyed, a provision suggesting that the authorities regarded innovation as a valuable public asset.

In England, by contrast, the power to grant exclusive rights was frequently abused by the monarch, who sold monopolies over ordinary goods such as salt and playing cards to aristocratic favourites. Parliamentary opposition grew, and in 1624 lawmakers passed the Statute of Monopolies, which abolished most of these privileges but expressly permitted patents for genuinely new inventions for a period of fourteen years. Legal historians often describe this enactment as the foundation of modern patent law, since it separated the reward of creativity from the arbitrary favours of the crown.

At the heart of the system lies a bargain between the inventor and society. In exchange for a monopoly of limited duration, the inventor must publish a description detailed enough for others to reproduce the invention once the protection expires. Whether this bargain actually encourages entrepreneurship, however, remains a matter of debate among economists. Some studies suggest that patents matter greatly in sectors such as medicines, where copying a finished product is cheap but development is extremely costly, whereas many startups appear to rely more on secrecy and on being first to the market. Critics also argue that excessively broad patents can hinder later inventors and make medicines less affordable, while they remain highly profitable for their owners. Such concerns have prompted courts and antitrust regulators to examine broad patents closely.
options: In contrast, economists agree that patents have no effect at all on the price of medicines.
For example, the English monarch sold monopolies over playing cards to his favourites.
Thus, more than five centuries after the Venetian statute, the right balance between rewarding inventors and serving the public is still being negotiated.
As a result, all patents were abolished in Europe at the end of the twentieth century.
Moreover, the Venetian authorities destroyed every machine that had received a patent.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Thus, more than five centuries after the Venetian statute, the right balance between rewarding inventors and serving the public is still being negotiated.’: eleştiriler ve incelemelerden sonra tartışmanın sürdüğünü söyleyerek metni toparlar. ‘agree’ geçen cümle ‘remains a matter of debate’ ve ilaç fiyatı eleştirisiyle çelişir; ‘playing’ geçen cümle ikinci paragrafa geri sıçrar; ‘abolished’ geçen cümle yanlış bir sonuç bağlar; ‘destroyed’ geçen cümle tersini söyler, yok edilen şey izinsiz kopyalardır.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
For more than a century, archaeologists working in rainforests faced a frustrating problem, since the dense vegetation that covers many ancient sites can hide even large buildings from someone standing only a few metres away. Since the early 2010s, however, this situation has been transformed by airborne laser scanning, a technique usually known as LiDAR, in which a scanner mounted on an aircraft sends hundreds of thousands of laser pulses towards the ground every second. Although most of the pulses are reflected by leaves and branches, a small fraction passes through gaps in the trees, and by measuring the time each pulse takes to return, specialists can reconstruct the shape of the land surface beneath them.

The results have been remarkable. A survey which was carried out in northern Guatemala in 2016 covered more than 2,000 square kilometres and revealed tens of thousands of previously unknown structures, including houses, raised roads and defensive walls. Similar work around Angkor in Cambodia showed that the famous temples had been surrounded by extensive urban districts whose traces were barely detectable on the ground. Such findings have prompted researchers to revise their estimates of the size of these societies, and some anthropologists now argue that the regions were considerably more populous than earlier fieldwork had suggested.

Nevertheless, the method has important limitations that its enthusiastic users sometimes overlook. A LiDAR image shows only the shape of the surface, so it cannot establish the chronological order in which features were built, and a mound that looks like a house may turn out to be a natural formation. For this reason, every interpretation must be checked through excavation or visits to the site, a process that is slow and expensive. Some archaeologists have also expressed concern that detailed maps, if they are published carelessly, could guide thieves directly to undisturbed tombs. The technology, in short, has not replaced traditional fieldwork but has changed the questions that fieldwork is expected to answer.
options: LiDAR has transformed archaeology in forests, although its results still need to be checked on the ground.
LiDAR can show exactly when ancient buildings were constructed.
Excavation is no longer necessary because aircraft can map every site.
The temples of Angkor were built by the same people who lived in Guatemala.
Archaeologists have stopped working in rainforests because of the dense vegetation.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘LiDAR has transformed archaeology in forests, although its results still need to be checked on the ground.’: metin yöntemin büyük keşiflerini ve sahada doğrulama gerektiren sınırlılıklarını anlatır. ‘exactly’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, LiDAR yapım sırasını belirleyemez; ‘Excavation’ geçen şık son paragrafa ters düşer; ‘Angkor’ geçen şık iki ayrı örneği birbirine bağlar; ‘stopped’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
exercises.passage:
In many villages of China and India, a small brick or concrete tank buried near the house provides families with gas for cooking, produced from biomass such as animal manure, kitchen waste and plant remains mixed with water. Inside the tank, which is known as a digester, microorganisms break down the organic material in the absence of oxygen. This process releases a flammable mixture consisting mainly of methane and carbon dioxide. The methane can be burned directly on a stove, and because the material is broken down rather than burned, the remaining liquid keeps most of its nitrogen and can be spread on fields as fertiliser.

Supporters of the technology emphasise that it addresses several problems at once. Cooking over wood or dung fires fills homes with smoke, and the inhalation of this smoke is a major cause of respiratory illness, especially among women and children, who spend the most time near the fire. Collecting firewood can also take hours each day. Manure that is left in open heaps, moreover, releases methane directly into the atmosphere, where it is a far more powerful greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide over a period of decades. Capturing that gas and using it for clean combustion therefore reduces indoor pollution and the climate impact of farming, while also improving sanitation by removing contaminants from around the house.

Experience has shown, however, that the benefits depend heavily on maintenance. Surveys in several countries have found that a considerable proportion of household digesters stop working within a few years, often because of cracks, blocked pipes or a lack of manure when families sell their animals. Microbial activity also slows sharply in cold weather, which limits gas production in mountainous regions during winter. In many villages of China and India, a small brick or concrete tank buried near the house provides families with gas for cooking, produced from biomass such as animal manure, kitchen waste and plant remains mixed with water. Experience has shown, however, that the benefits depend heavily on maintenance. Surveys in several countries have found that a considerable proportion of household digesters stop working within a few years, often because of cracks, blocked pipes or a lack of manure when families sell their animals. Microbial activity also slows sharply in cold weather, which limits gas production in mountainous regions during winter. In addition, a digester that leaks may release more methane than the untreated manure would have done, so a poorly built system can be worse for the climate than none at all. For these reasons, recent programmes have placed greater emphasis on training local technicians than on simply building as many units as possible.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Cataract, a gradual clouding of the lens inside the eye, is the leading cause of blindness in the world. It becomes increasingly common with age, although exposure to ultraviolet light, smoking and diabetes also appear to raise the risk. For more than two thousand years, the only treatment available was a procedure known as couching, in which a sharp instrument was used to push the cloudy lens out of the line of sight. The operation, which was described in ancient Indian medical texts, could restore some vision, but it was performed without anaesthesia and frequently ended in infection or permanent blindness.

A more reliable approach appeared in the eighteenth century, when the French surgeon Jacques Daviel began removing the lens entirely through an incision in the front of the eye. Patients who recovered could see again, but only with very thick glasses, since the eye no longer possessed a lens to focus light. The next breakthrough came from an unexpected observation. During the Second World War, the British eye surgeon Harold Ridley noticed that pilots whose eyes had been hit by fragments of plastic from aircraft windows often showed surprisingly little inflammatory reaction. In 1949 he used the same material to make the first prosthetic lens, which was implanted in place of the natural one.

Ridley’s idea was resisted by many colleagues for years, but the implantation of artificial lenses eventually became standard practice. In the late 1960s the American surgeon Charles Kelman introduced a technique in which ultrasound breaks the cloudy lens into tiny pieces that can be removed through a cut only a few millimetres wide, so that sutures are rarely needed. Today the operation usually takes less than half an hour and is performed on outpatients who remain awake throughout. Nevertheless, millions of people in low-income countries remain blind because of cataract, largely because there are too few trained surgeons. This suggests that the main obstacle is no longer medical knowledge but access to care.
options: argue that couching is still the safest treatment for cataract
explain how ultraviolet light damages the eye
describe the career of a wartime pilot
compare medical education in different countries
trace how the treatment of cataract developed and point out a problem that remains
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘trace how the treatment of cataract developed and point out a problem that remains’: metin şişlemeden yapay merceğe ve ultrasona uzanan gelişimi anlatır, sonunda cerrah eksikliği sorununu vurgular. ‘safest’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, şişleme çoğu zaman körlükle biterdi; ‘ultraviolet’ geçen şık yalnızca bir risk etkenidir; ‘pilot’ geçen şık bir gözlemi ana konu yapar; ‘education’ geçen şık metinde karşılaştırılmaz.

exercises.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, the lighthouse was the favourite example that economists used to illustrate a public good. A lighthouse, the argument went, sends its light to every passing ship, and it is impossible to prevent a vessel that has not paid from using the signal to avoid the rocks. Since no shipowner would voluntarily pay for something that he could enjoy for free, private firms would never build lighthouses, and the state would have to provide them out of general taxation. Paul Samuelson, whose textbook was read by generations of students, presented the case in almost exactly these terms.

In 1974, however, Ronald Coase published an article which asked whether economists had ever looked at how lighthouses were actually financed. Studying British records, he found that in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries many lighthouses had been built and operated by private individuals. These owners obtained permission from the Crown to collect "light dues", a charge that was paid by ships when they arrived at nearby ports. Because a vessel could not easily avoid entering a port, the free-rider problem was largely solved, and some lighthouse owners earned considerable profits.

Coase's study was widely cited as evidence that markets could supply even the most typical public goods. Later historians, though, have offered a more cautious reading. They point out that the right to collect dues was granted and enforced by the government, and that ports refusing to cooperate could be punished by law. In this view, the British system was neither purely private nor purely public, but a partnership in which the state made private provision possible. The debate has therefore shifted from the simple question of whether the market or the state should provide a good to the more practical question of which combination of the two works best.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why lighthouses are no longer needed by modern ships
the methods that British ports used to punish ships which refused to pay
a textbook that changed the way economics was taught to students
the profits that private lighthouse owners earned in the eighteenth century
how a classic example of a public good has been re-examined using historical evidence
exercises.explanation: Metin, deniz fenerinin kamusal malın klasik örneği olarak nasıl kullanıldığını, Coase’un tarihsel kayıtlarla bu örneği nasıl sorguladığını ve sonraki tartışmayı anlatır: ‘how a classic example of a public good has been re-examined using historical evidence’. Modern gemilerin fenere ihtiyacı (‘modern ships’) hiç ele alınmaz; limanların cezalandırılması (‘punish’) ve fener sahiplerinin kârları (‘profits’) yalnızca ayrıntıdır; Samuelson’ın ders kitabı (‘textbook’) ise sadece örneğin kaynağı olarak anılır.

A lighthouse, the argument went, sends its light to every passing ship, and it is impossible to prevent a vessel that has not paid from using the signal to avoid the rocks. Paul Samuelson, whose textbook was read by generations of students, presented the case in almost exactly these terms.

In 1974, however, Ronald Coase published an article which asked whether economists had ever looked at how lighthouses were actually financed. Studying British records, he found that in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries many lighthouses had been built and operated by private individuals. These owners obtained permission from the Crown to collect "light dues", a charge that was paid by ships when they arrived at nearby ports. Because a vessel could not easily avoid entering a port, the free-rider problem was largely solved, and some lighthouse owners earned considerable profits.

Coase's study was widely cited as evidence that markets could supply even the most typical public goods. Later historians, though, have offered a more cautious reading. They point out that the right to collect dues was granted and enforced by the government, and that ports refusing to cooperate could be punished by law. In this view, the British system was neither purely private nor purely public, but a partnership in which the state made private provision possible. The debate has therefore shifted from the simple question of whether the market or the state should provide a good to the more practical question of which combination of the two works best.

considered Coase's conclusion about markets to be somewhat overstated

exercises.passage:
Every day, at almost exactly the same moments, weather balloons are released from several hundred stations around the world. Each balloon, which is usually filled with hydrogen or helium, carries a small, lightweight instrument package known as a radiosonde. As the balloon rises at roughly five metres per second, the radiosonde measures temperature, humidity and air pressure, while its changing position, tracked by satellite navigation, reveals the speed and direction of the wind. After about two hours, when it has climbed to a height of more than twenty kilometres, the balloon has expanded so much in the thin air that it bursts, and the instrument falls back to the ground, often under a small parachute.

Releases are coordinated internationally so that measurements taken at midnight and midday Greenwich time can be compared directly. The resulting profiles of the atmosphere are fed into the computer models on which modern forecasts depend. Satellites now provide far more observations than balloons do, yet they mainly measure radiation coming from thick layers of air and cannot describe conditions at a particular height with the same precision. For this reason, studies in which forecasters deliberately removed balloon data from their models have generally found that forecast quality declines, particularly in regions where other observations are scarce.

The network is nevertheless under pressure. Each launch requires a new instrument, most of which are never recovered, and stations in remote areas are expensive to staff and supply. In recent decades, a number of stations, especially in Africa, have reduced their launches or stopped altogether, leaving gaps that meteorologists regard as a serious weakness. Some agencies have experimented with automatic launchers, which fill and release balloons without a human operator, as one way of keeping the network alive.

Designing Parachutes for Falling Scientific Instruments

exercises.passage: (I) When moist air from the ocean meets a mountain range, it is forced to rise and cools as it climbs. (IV) By the time the air descends on the far side, it has lost most of its moisture, and it warms up as it sinks. (V) As a result, the land beyond the mountains, known as a rain shadow, is often much drier, as in the dry plains east of the Andes in Patagonia.

units.guide:
## Strateji

YÖKDİL ve YDS’de okuma bölümü zamanla yarıştır: metin başına yaklaşık **10 dakikan** var ve alanlar art arda değişir. Bir fen metninden sonra sağlık, ardından hukuk ya da tarih gelebilir. Süreyi korumanın yolu her metni aynı düzenle okumaktır: önce soru köklerine bak, sonra metni amaçlı oku, en son şıkları metinle eşleştir. Alan değişince terimler değişir, ama metnin iskeleti (iddia, açıklama, sınır) çoğu zaman aynıdır.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. **1 dk:** dört soru kökünü oku; hangisinin ayrıntı, hangisinin çıkarım ya da paragraf sorusu olduğunu işaretle.

2. **4 dk:** metni oku; her paragrafın kenarına tek kelimelik rol yaz: "keşif", "neden", "sınır", "tartışma".

3. **4 dk:** soruları çöz. Paragraf tamamlama ve aykırı cümle sorularında bağlaca ve paragrafın odağına bak.

4. **1 dk:** emin olmadığın soruyu işaretle ve sıradaki metne geç.

## Örnek

*Ridley’s idea was resisted for years. Today, however, artificial lenses are standard practice.* Roller: "direnç → kabul". Soru bugünkü durumu sorarsa cevabı *however*’dan sonra ararsın; eski tartışmayı soran şıklar tuzaktır.

## Sınav ipucu

Bilmediğin terimlerle (khipu, caisson, chemosynthesis) vakit kaybetme; metin bu kelimeleri genellikle hemen ardından açıklar. Bir metinde 10 dakikayı aşarsan en olası şıkkı işaretle ve geç: geride kalan bir soru, okunmamış bir metnin dört sorusundan değerli değildir.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1977, scientists using a small deep-diving vehicle to explore a volcanic ridge near the Galápagos Islands made a discovery that forced biologists to reconsider their assumptions about where life can exist. At a depth of about 2,500 metres, where sunlight never reaches, they found openings in the seabed from which warm, mineral-rich water was flowing. Around these openings lived dense communities of invertebrates, including clams, crabs and tube worms more than a metre long. Until then, it had been widely accepted that almost all life on Earth depends ultimately on photosynthesis, the process by which plants and algae capture energy from the Sun.

The energy which sustains these vent communities comes instead from chemistry. Sea water that sinks into cracks in the ocean floor is heated by hot rock below and returns loaded with dissolved sulphur compounds, which are toxic to most animals. Certain microbial species, however, are able to extract energy by oxidising these inorganic substances and use it to build organic matter, a process known as chemosynthesis. The giant tube worms, which have neither a mouth nor a digestive tract as adults, house billions of these bacteria inside their bodies, a remarkable example of symbiosis in which the animal supplies chemicals and its partners supply food.

The discovery has had consequences well beyond marine biology. Because the conditions at vents resemble those that probably existed on the young Earth, some researchers have proposed that life itself may have originated in such environments, although this hypothesis remains far from conclusive. The vents have also attracted the attention of space scientists, since moons such as Europa and Enceladus are believed to contain liquid oceans beneath their icy surfaces. More recently, the metal deposits that accumulate around vents have been examined by mining companies. This development worries ecologists, who point out that many vent species are found nowhere else and that their capacity to regenerate after disturbance is poorly understood.
options: Tube worms are the largest animals ever found in the deep ocean.
Life on Earth certainly began around openings in the seabed.
Life around deep-sea vents showed that whole communities can depend on chemical energy rather than sunlight.
Mining companies have already destroyed most vent communities.
Photosynthesis is more efficient than chemosynthesis in warm water.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Life around deep-sea vents showed that whole communities can depend on chemical energy rather than sunlight.’: metin keşfin, yaşamın fotosenteze bağlı olduğu varsayımını nasıl değiştirdiğini anlatır. ‘largest’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘certainly’ geçen şık fazla kesindir, bu hipotez ‘far from conclusive’ olarak sunulur; ‘destroyed’ geçen şık abartılıdır, şirketler yalnızca yatakları incelemiştir; ‘efficient’ geçen şık metinde karşılaştırılmaz.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Long before electric air conditioning was invented, builders in the hot, dry regions of Iran and the Persian Gulf developed an ingenious way of cooling houses that required no fuel at all. The windcatcher is a tall vertical tower rising above the roof with openings near the top. It captures the wind, which blows more strongly at height, and directs it down a narrow passage into the rooms below. In the Iranian city of Yazd, where summer temperatures regularly exceed 40 degrees, hundreds of these towers still stand, and the durability of some has allowed them to remain in use for several centuries.

The physics behind the design is more sophisticated than it first appears. When the wind blows, air is pushed down the side of the tower that faces it, while lower pressure on the opposite side draws warm air out of the building. In this way, the kinetic energy of the wind does work that would otherwise require mechanical fans. Even on still days, the tower continues to function through convection, since hot air inside the house rises and escapes through the top, pulling cooler air in at ground level. In some houses the incoming air was passed over a pool or an underground channel, and the evaporation of this water lowered its temperature further, a technique which works best where the air is dry.

Engineers who have measured traditional towers report that they can reduce indoor temperatures by several degrees, which is modest compared with modern machines but achieved without any electricity or photovoltaic panels. Thick walls of porous clay, which act as insulators, add to the thermal comfort of the rooms, and the basic thermodynamics of the system is now well understood. Interest in the principle has therefore revived among architects who wish to cut the energy demand of buildings, and modern versions with filters have been installed in schools and offices in several countries. Nevertheless, the feasibility of copying windcatchers depends on local conditions, because in humid climates the cooling effect of evaporation is much weaker.
options: Why Air Conditioning Was Invented in Iran
Windcatchers: An Old Way of Cooling Without Fuel
The History of the City of Yazd
How Humid Climates Improve Evaporative Cooling
Modern Fans and Their Electricity Costs
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Windcatchers: An Old Way of Cooling Without Fuel’: metin rüzgâr kulelerinin nasıl çalıştığını, ne kadar serinlettiğini ve bugünkü uygulanabilirliğini anlatır. ‘Invented’ geçen başlık yanlıştır, kuleler klimadan çok önce vardı; ‘History’ geçen başlık Yezd’i yalnızca örnek olarak anar; ‘Humid’ geçen başlık tersini söyler, nemli iklimde etki zayıftır; ‘Fans’ geçen başlık metnin konusu değildir.

Metin 2: Glisemik indeksin değeri ve sınırları. ys9 kelimeleri: detectable, physiology, compression, asymptomatic, ultrasound, ailment, clinician, therapeutic ve 13 kelime daha. ys7 kelimeleri: publish, foundation, gradual, aircraft, joint ve 12 kelime daha.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
In the second half of the nineteenth century, engineers who were building the foundations of large bridges began to use caissons. These were enormous boxes, open at the bottom, that were sunk into riverbeds and filled with compressed air to keep water and mud out. The men who dug inside them worked without difficulty. After returning to the surface, however, many of them developed severe pain in their joints, dizziness and sometimes paralysis. During the construction of the Brooklyn Bridge in New York, several workers died of this unexplained ailment, and the chief engineer, Washington Roebling, was left partially disabled for the rest of his life.

The cause was explained by the French scientist Paul Bert, a pioneer of physiology, who demonstrated in 1878 that the illness resulted from bubbles of nitrogen forming in the blood and tissues. During compression, more of this gas dissolves in the body, and if the pressure is reduced too quickly, the gas comes out of solution in much the same way that bubbles appear when a bottle of fizzy drink is opened. Bert also observed that the symptoms could be relieved by returning the patient to high pressure, an insight which later led to the therapeutic use of special pressure chambers.

Practical guidance arrived in 1908, when the Scottish scientist John Scott Haldane published tables for the Royal Navy based on experiments with goats. His tables recommended bringing divers up in stages, with pauses that allowed nitrogen to leave the body gradually. Modified versions of these schedules are still used by divers today, and decompression sickness, as the condition is now called, has become relatively uncommon among those who follow them. The risk has not disappeared, however. Ultrasound scans show that bubbles are often detectable even in divers who remain asymptomatic, and clinicians still debate why some develop neurological damage while others do not. Some studies suggest, for example, that flying soon after a dive increases the danger, because the air pressure in an aircraft cabin is lower than at sea level.
options: explain the cause of decompression sickness and how its risk came to be reduced
describe the construction of the Brooklyn Bridge in detail
argue that divers should never travel by air
compare French and Scottish medicine in the nineteenth century
prove that goats are more sensitive to pressure than humans
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain the cause of decompression sickness and how its risk came to be reduced’: metin hastalığın ortaya çıkışını, Bert’in açıklamasını, Haldane’in tablolarını ve süren riski anlatır. ‘Brooklyn’ geçen şık yalnızca bir örnektir; ‘never’ geçen şık metindeki temkinli bulguyu abartır; ‘compare’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘goats’ geçen şık deneyin ayrıntısını yanlış yorumlar.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, experts classified dietary carbohydrates simply as either simple sugars, which were thought to raise blood sugar quickly, or complex starches, which were assumed to be digested slowly. In 1981, however, a team led by the Canadian researcher David Jenkins showed that this distinction was misleading, because some starchy foods, such as white bread and potatoes, raised blood glucose almost as fast as pure sugar. To compare foods more precisely, the team proposed the glycaemic index. On this scale, the effect of a food containing a fixed amount of carbohydrate is measured against that of pure glucose, which is given a value of 100.

The index revealed that the way in which a food is processed and prepared matters a great deal. Foods that are rich in fibre, fat or protein tend to be digested more slowly, while grinding grain into fine flour or cooking pasta for too long increases the speed at which glucose enters the blood. Critics soon pointed out, though, that the index ignores the quantity of food that people actually eat. Watermelon, for example, has a high index, yet a normal portion contains so little carbohydrate that its effect is small, which is why researchers later introduced a related indicator known as glycaemic load.

The practical value of the index for nutritional advice remains a matter of discussion. Several trials have suggested that diets based on low-index foods can modestly improve the control of blood sugar in diabetic patients, some of whom may thereby reduce their need for insulin. The benefits for healthy individuals, however, are less clear. Moreover, a study published in 2015 found that different people responded to identical meals in strikingly different ways, a variability which the authors linked partly to differences in the microbiome of the gut. Such findings suggest that a single number printed on a package of sugary cereal may be a less reliable guide than its popularity implies, and that personalised advice might eventually prove more useful.
options: Simple sugars always raise blood sugar faster than starches.
The glycaemic index has been shown to prevent diabetes in healthy people.
The glycaemic index improved on older ideas about carbohydrates, but its practical value has limits.
Watermelon should be avoided by people with diabetes.
Personalised advice has already replaced the glycaemic index.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The glycaemic index improved on older ideas about carbohydrates, but its practical value has limits.’: metin indeksin eski sınıflandırmayı nasıl düzelttiğini, sonra eleştirilerini ve sınırlarını anlatır. ‘always’ geçen şık Jenkins’in çürüttüğü eski görüştür; ‘prevent’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, sağlıklı kişilerdeki fayda belirsizdir; ‘Watermelon’ geçen şık örneği tersine yorumlar; ‘replaced’ geçen şık fazla kesindir, metin ‘might eventually’ der.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
The Inca state, which at its height in the early sixteenth century stretched for more than 4,000 kilometres along the Andes, governed millions of people without an alphabet or any other known system of writing. Instead, its officials relied on khipus, bundles of coloured cotton or wool strings on which numeric information was recorded by means of knots. Spanish observers who arrived in the 1530s reported with some surprise that trained specialists could describe population figures and stored goods in great detail. They did so simply by running their fingers along the strings, much as a literate official might read a written list.

How these records worked was largely explained in 1912, when the American scholar Leland Locke demonstrated that they used a decimal system. In this system, the position of a knot on a string indicated units, tens, hundreds and so on, and different types of knot distinguished the units from the higher values. Smaller strings attached to a main string could record partial totals that added up to the figure above. This arrangement, which resembles a modern spreadsheet in some respects, allowed the aggregation of census data from many villages and kept a reliable tally of the contents of state storehouses.

A more controversial question is whether the strings also recorded language, such as names, laws or historical narratives. Several colonial writers claimed that they did, yet scholars have not succeeded in decoding any such content. One reason is that only around a thousand examples survive, and very few of them are accompanied by written translations in archival documents. Many others were destroyed after church authorities in the 1580s condemned them as connected with traditional religion. Some recent studies of khipus kept by villages in the Peruvian highlands have suggested that colour and fibre type may have carried phonetic information, as a kind of cipher. The evidence, however, remains limited, and most specialists treat such claims with caution until larger samples have been analysed.
options: The Incas used an alphabet that was later destroyed by the Spanish.
Khipus were an effective way of keeping records, but whether they also recorded language is still uncertain.
Locke proved that khipus recorded historical narratives.
Khipus were invented by Spanish officials in the 1530s.
Most khipus survive today together with written translations.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Khipus were an effective way of keeping records, but whether they also recorded language is still uncertain.’: metin sayısal sistemi açıklar, sonra dil kaydı tartışmasının sürdüğünü söyler. ‘alphabet’ geçen şık ilk cümleyle çelişir; ‘narratives’ geçen şık yanlıştır, Locke sayı sistemini açıklamıştır; ‘invented’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, İspanyollar khipuları buldukları biçimde görmüştür; ‘translations’ geçen şık tersini söyler, çok azı çeviriyle birlikte kalmıştır.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
For several centuries, the dominant principle governing the oceans was the freedom of the seas. This idea was famously defended in 1609 by the Dutch lawyer Hugo Grotius, who argued that the sea, unlike land, could not be owned by any sovereign state. In practice, coastal states were permitted to control only a narrow belt of water, often set at about five kilometres, a distance which was traditionally associated with the range of a gun fired from the shore. Beyond that line, ships of every nation could sail, fish and trade as they wished, an arrangement that suited colonial powers whose large fleets supported their naval hegemony.

This arrangement began to break down after the Second World War, when advances in technology made it possible to take oil from the seabed and to fish far from home on an industrial scale. In 1945 the United States declared that the resources of the sea floor next to its coast belonged to it. A few years later, several South American countries claimed rights over waters extending about 370 kilometres from their shores. Such unilateral claims, together with a growing number of bilateral disputes, threatened to produce chaos. After nearly a decade of multilateral negotiations and intense diplomatic effort, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea was finally signed in 1982.

The convention, which came into effect in 1994, established a territorial sea of about 22 kilometres and an exclusive economic zone that extends roughly 370 kilometres from the coast. Within this zone a coastal state controls fishing and the removal of minerals, while foreign ships retain the right to pass. Despite broad ratification by more than 160 states, the treaty has not been accepted by every superpower, and disputes over the status of small islands continue to create geopolitical tension in several regions. Moreover, the convention left the high seas largely unprotected, a gap that a separate agreement adopted in 2023 attempts to close in order to strengthen the rule of law beyond national control.
options: From Freedom of the Seas to Zones of National Control
Hugo Grotius and the Dutch Navy
How Fishing Fleets Protect the High Seas
Why the United States Wrote the Convention
The Range of Guns in the Age of Sail
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘From Freedom of the Seas to Zones of National Control’: metin denizlerin serbestliği ilkesinden kıyı devletlerinin denetlediği bölgelere geçişi anlatır. ‘Navy’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur; ‘Fishing’ geçen başlık tersini söyler, açık denizler büyük ölçüde korumasız kalmıştır; ‘Wrote’ geçen başlık yanlıştır, ABD sözleşmeyi onaylamamıştır; ‘Guns’ geçen başlık tek bir ayrıntıyı ana konu yapar.

exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that the principle of the freedom of the seas ----.
exercises.passage:
For several centuries, the dominant principle governing the oceans was the freedom of the seas. This idea was famously defended in 1609 by the Dutch lawyer Hugo Grotius, who argued that the sea, unlike land, could not be owned by any sovereign state. In practice, coastal states were permitted to control only a narrow belt of water, often set at about five kilometres, a distance which was traditionally associated with the range of a gun fired from the shore. Beyond that line, ships of every nation could sail, fish and trade as they wished, an arrangement that suited colonial powers whose large fleets supported their naval hegemony.

This arrangement began to break down after the Second World War, when advances in technology made it possible to take oil from the seabed and to fish far from home on an industrial scale. In 1945 the United States declared that the resources of the sea floor next to its coast belonged to it. A few years later, several South American countries claimed rights over waters extending about 370 kilometres from their shores. Such unilateral claims, together with a growing number of bilateral disputes, threatened to produce chaos. After nearly a decade of multilateral negotiations and intense diplomatic effort, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea was finally signed in 1982.

The convention, which came into effect in 1994, established a territorial sea of about 22 kilometres and an exclusive economic zone that extends roughly 370 kilometres from the coast. Within this zone a coastal state controls fishing and the removal of minerals, while foreign ships retain the right to pass. Despite broad ratification by more than 160 states, the treaty has not been accepted by every superpower, and disputes over the status of small islands continue to create geopolitical tension in several regions. Moreover, the convention left the high seas largely unprotected, a gap that a separate agreement adopted in 2023 attempts to close in order to strengthen the rule of law beyond national control.
options: was first proposed by the United Nations in 1982
was strengthened by the claims of South American countries
is still the only principle governing the oceans
benefited states with large fleets more than other states
was abandoned because guns could no longer reach the shore
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘benefited states with large fleets more than other states’: metin bu düzenin büyük filolara sahip sömürgeci güçlere uygun düştüğünü söyler. ‘United’ geçen şık yanlıştır, ilke 1609’da Grotius tarafından savunulmuştur; ‘strengthened’ geçen şık tersini söyler, bu iddialar ilkeyi zayıflatmıştır; ‘only’ geçen şık sözleşmeyle çelişir; ‘abandoned’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir neden öne sürer.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
Less than twenty years after his conquest of England in 1066, William the Conqueror ordered one of the most ambitious administrative projects of medieval Europe. At a meeting held at Christmas in 1085, the monarch decided to send officials into almost every county to find out who held each piece of land. They were also asked to record how many tenants lived on it, how many mills and animals it contained, and what it was worth. The survey which resulted was completed with remarkable speed during 1086, and its findings were written down in Latin in two large volumes that are still preserved, among other archival treasures, in London.

The purpose of the survey has long been debated by historians. One view holds that it was mainly a fiscal exercise, intended to give the king an appraisal of the taxable wealth of each landowner at a time when he feared an invasion from Scandinavia. Others emphasise its legal function, pointing out that the conquest had transferred vast estates from English to French aristocratic families. This transfer had generated countless disputes over ownership, which a written record could help to settle. The two interpretations are not mutually exclusive, and most scholars now accept that the work served several aims at once, including taxation and the defence of the realm.

The name Domesday Book, by which the volumes are known, was not given to them until about a century later. People had begun comparing them with the Last Judgement, after which, according to Christian belief, no appeal would be possible. Their authority in court lasted surprisingly long, and they were consulted in property cases well into the modern period. For modern researchers, however, their value lies elsewhere, since this vast ledger offers an almost unique statistical portrait of an early medieval society. It records everything from the valuation of individual farms to the size of the rural populace, although historians caution that several northern areas are missing and that population estimates derived from it rest on uncertain assumptions.
options: a medieval survey, the debate about its purpose and its value today
the military defeat of England in 1066
the Christian idea of the Last Judgement
the tax system of modern Britain
an invasion of England from Scandinavia
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a medieval survey, the debate about its purpose and its value today’: metin araştırmanın yapılışını, amacına ilişkin görüşleri ve bugünkü değerini anlatır. ‘defeat’ geçen şık yalnızca arka plandır; ‘Judgement’ geçen şık adın kökenini ana konu yapar; ‘modern’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘invasion’ geçen şık yalnızca kralın korkusudur ve gerçekleştiği söylenmez.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Engineers who design concrete dams must solve a fundamental problem. The water held back by the structure exerts an enormous horizontal force, which increases sharply with depth and must be transferred safely into the ground. The traditional answer is the gravity dam, a massive wall whose sheer weight prevents it from being pushed over or sliding along its foundation. Such dams can be built on almost any solid rock, but they require vast quantities of concrete, and the heat which is released as the concrete hardens becomes a serious difficulty in very large hydroelectric projects.

An arch dam relies on a different principle. Curved so that its outer face points towards the reservoir, it transfers much of the water pressure sideways into the walls of the valley, in much the same way that a stone arch carries the load of a bridge to its supports. Concrete is brittle and has little tensile strength, but it resists compression very well. The curved shape therefore allows an arch dam to be remarkably thin, sometimes using only a fraction of the material that an equivalent gravity dam would need. The price of this efficiency, however, is that the design is suitable only for narrow valleys whose rock walls are strong enough to bear the load.

The importance of that condition was demonstrated tragically in 1959, when the Malpasset Dam in southern France failed only a few years after its completion. The flood that followed killed more than four hundred people. Subsequent investigations concluded that the concrete had not been at fault. Instead, hydraulic pressure from water trapped in porous and fractured rock beneath one end of the dam had caused the foundation to move. The disaster led to far closer scrutiny of the ground before construction, and it is now widely accepted that the durability of any dam depends as much on the rock beneath it as on the structure itself, whether its turbines produce power or it simply stores water.
options: explain how hydroelectric turbines produce electricity
compare two types of concrete dam and show why the ground beneath them matters
argue that arch dams should no longer be built
describe the history of southern France
prove that concrete is stronger in tension than in compression

The importance of that condition was demonstrated tragically in 1959, when the Malpasset Dam in southern France failed only a few years after its completion. The flood that followed killed more than four hundred people. Subsequent investigations concluded that the concrete had not been at fault. Instead, hydraulic pressure from water trapped in porous and fractured rock beneath one end of the dam had caused the foundation to move. The disaster led to far closer scrutiny of the ground before construction, and it is now widely accepted that the durability of any dam depends as much on the rock beneath it as on the structure itself, whether its turbines produce power or it simply stores water.
options: it is built only in very wide valleys
its weight alone holds back the water
the concrete it uses has great tensile strength
it releases less heat as the concrete hardens
its curve sends the load into the valley walls and keeps the concrete under compression
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘its curve sends the load into the valley walls and keeps the concrete under compression’: kemer, yükü yanlara aktarır ve beton iyi dayandığı sıkışma altında kalır. ‘wide’ geçen şık tersini söyler, dar vadiler gerekir; ‘weight’ geçen şık ağırlık barajını anlatır; ‘tensile’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘heat’ geçen şık ağırlık barajlarının sorunuyla ilgili bir ayrıntıyı karıştırır.

exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that the Malpasset disaster ----.
exercises.passage:
Engineers who design concrete dams must solve a fundamental problem. The water held back by the structure exerts an enormous horizontal force, which increases sharply with depth and must be transferred safely into the ground. The traditional answer is the gravity dam, a massive wall whose sheer weight prevents it from being pushed over or sliding along its foundation. Such dams can be built on almost any solid rock, but they require vast quantities of concrete, and the heat which is released as the concrete hardens becomes a serious difficulty in very large hydroelectric projects.

An arch dam relies on a different principle. Curved so that its outer face points towards the reservoir, it transfers much of the water pressure sideways into the walls of the valley, in much the same way that a stone arch carries the load of a bridge to its supports. Concrete is brittle and has little tensile strength, but it resists compression very well. The curved shape therefore allows an arch dam to be remarkably thin, sometimes using only a fraction of the material that an equivalent gravity dam would need. The price of this efficiency, however, is that the design is suitable only for narrow valleys whose rock walls are strong enough to bear the load.

The importance of that condition was demonstrated tragically in 1959, when the Malpasset Dam in southern France failed only a few years after its completion. The flood that followed killed more than four hundred people. Subsequent investigations concluded that the concrete had not been at fault. Instead, hydraulic pressure from water trapped in porous and fractured rock beneath one end of the dam had caused the foundation to move. The disaster led to far closer scrutiny of the ground before construction, and it is now widely accepted that the durability of any dam depends as much on the rock beneath it as on the structure itself, whether its turbines produce power or it simply stores water.
options: showed that a well-built dam can still fail if the rock beneath it is weak
was caused by concrete of poor quality
led engineers to abandon arch dams completely
happened because the valley was too wide
had no influence on later construction practice
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘showed that a well-built dam can still fail if the rock beneath it is weak’: soruşturmalar betonu suçlamamış, kayadaki zayıflığı neden olarak göstermiştir. ‘quality’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘abandon’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘wide’ geçen şık metinde desteklenmez; ‘influence’ geçen şık tersini söyler, felaket daha sıkı zemin incelemelerine yol açmıştır.

exercises.question: Which of the following sentences, if added to the passage’s second paragraph, would be irrelevant?
exercises.passage:

An arch dam relies on a different principle. Curved so that its outer face points towards the reservoir, it transfers much of the water pressure sideways into the walls of the valley, in much the same way that a stone arch carries the load of a bridge to its supports. Concrete is brittle and has little tensile strength, but it resists compression very well. The curved shape therefore allows an arch dam to be remarkably thin, sometimes using only a fraction of the material that an equivalent gravity dam would need. The price of this efficiency, however, is that the design is suitable only for narrow valleys whose rock walls are strong enough to bear the load.

The importance of that condition was demonstrated tragically in 1959, when the Malpasset Dam in southern France failed only a few years after its completion. The flood that followed killed more than four hundred people. Subsequent investigations concluded that the concrete had not been at fault. Instead, hydraulic pressure from water trapped in porous and fractured rock beneath one end of the dam had caused the foundation to move. options: Some of the thinnest arch dams are only a few metres thick at the top, even though they hold back very deep water.
This is why arch dams are most often found in steep, rocky mountain valleys.
Engineers therefore study the shape of the valley carefully before choosing the curve of the dam.
In wider valleys, engineers often combine the two principles in a dam that is both curved and heavy.
The reservoirs behind large dams have also become popular places for sailing and fishing.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The reservoirs behind large dams have also become popular places for sailing and fishing.’: ikinci paragraf kemer barajın yapısal ilkesini ve uygun vadi koşullarını anlatır; baraj göllerinin eğlence amaçlı kullanımı aynı konunun farklı bir yönüdür. ‘thinnest’ geçen cümle incelik bilgisini somutlaştırır; ‘rocky’ geçen cümle dar vadi koşulunu sürdürür; ‘curve’ geçen cümle vadi biçimiyle tasarımı bağlar; ‘combine’ geçen cümle geniş vadiler için çözümü verir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘The bacteria that live inside the tube worms extract energy from chemicals which would be toxic to most other animals.’
options: Tüp solucanları, içlerinde yaşayan bakteriler için zehirli olan kimyasallardan enerji elde eder.
Tüp solucanlarının içinde yaşayan bakteriler, bütün hayvanlar için zararsız olan kimyasallardan enerji elde eder.
Tüp solucanlarının içinde yaşayan bakteriler, diğer hayvanların çoğu için zehirli olacak kimyasallardan enerji elde eder.
Tüp solucanlarının içinde yaşayan bakteriler, diğer hayvanların çoğu için zehirli olan kimyasallardan enerji elde edemez.
Tüp solucanlarının içinde yaşayan bakteriler, ileride diğer hayvanlar için zehirli kimyasallar üretecektir.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Tüp solucanlarının içinde yaşayan bakteriler, diğer hayvanların çoğu için zehirli olacak kimyasallardan enerji elde eder.’ Çekirdek: ‘The bacteria … extract energy from chemicals’; ‘that live…’ ve ‘which would be…’ iki yan cümledir. ‘içlerinde’ geçen şık özneyi değiştirir; ‘zararsız’ geçen şık niceleyiciyi ve anlamı değiştirir; ‘edemez’ geçen şık olumsuzluk ekler; ‘üretecektir’ geçen şık fiili ve zamanı değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Investigators concluded that the dam had failed not because of its concrete but because of weaknesses in the rock beneath it.’
options: Araştırmacılar, barajın betonu yüzünden değil, altındaki kayadaki zayıflıklar yüzünden çöktüğü sonucuna vardı.
Araştırmacılar, barajın altındaki kaya yüzünden değil, betonundaki zayıflıklar yüzünden çöktüğü sonucuna vardı.
Araştırmacılar, barajın hem betonu hem de altındaki kaya yüzünden çöktüğü sonucuna vardı.
Araştırmacılar, barajın altındaki kayadaki zayıflıklar yüzünden çökebileceği konusunda uyardı.
Araştırmacılar, barajın neden çöktüğüne dair hiçbir sonuca varamadı.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Araştırmacılar, barajın betonu yüzünden değil, altındaki kayadaki zayıflıklar yüzünden çöktüğü sonucuna vardı.’ ‘not because of … but because of …’ yapısı ‘… yüzünden değil, … yüzünden’ olarak çevrilir. ‘betonundaki’ geçen şık nedenleri yer değiştirir; ‘hem’ geçen şık iki nedeni birleştirir; ‘uyardı’ geçen şık fiili ve zamanı değiştirip olayı olasılığa çevirir; ‘varamadı’ geçen şık olumsuzluk ekler.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Bazı çalışmalar, dalıştan kısa süre sonra uçmanın riski artırabileceğini ileri sürmektedir.’
options: All studies prove that flying soon after a dive increases the risk.
Some studies suggest that diving soon after a flight may reduce the risk.
Some studies suggested that flying long after a dive had no effect on the risk.
Some studies suggest that flying soon after a dive may increase the risk.
No study has suggested that flying after a dive is risky.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Some studies suggest that flying soon after a dive may increase the risk.’ ‘Bazı’ → ‘Some’, ‘ileri sürmektedir’ → ‘suggest’, ‘-abileceğini’ → ‘may’. ‘prove’ geçen şık niceleyiciyi ‘All’ yapar ve temkini kaldırır; ‘reduce’ geçen şık sırayı ve fiili tersine çevirir; ‘long’ geçen şık zamanı ve anlamı değiştirir; ‘No study’ ile başlayan şık olumsuzluk ekler.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Antlaşma, kıyı devletlerinin balıkçılığı denetlediği ancak yabancı gemilerin geçiş hakkını koruduğu bir bölge oluşturdu.’
options: The treaty created a zone in which foreign ships control fishing but coastal states keep the right to pass.
The treaty created a zone in which coastal states control fishing but foreign ships keep the right to pass.
The treaty abolished the zone in which coastal states had controlled fishing.
The treaty will create a zone in which coastal states may control fishing and foreign ships may not pass.
The treaty created a zone in which no state controls fishing and all ships keep the right to pass.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The treaty created a zone in which coastal states control fishing but foreign ships keep the right to pass.’ Türkçede bölgeyi niteleyen ‘…denetlediği ancak … koruduğu’ öbeği İngilizcede ‘a zone in which…’ yan cümlesi olur. ‘foreign ships control’ diyen şık özneleri yer değiştirir; ‘abolished’ geçen şık fiili tersine çevirir; ‘will’ geçen şık zamanı değiştirip geçişi yasaklar; ‘no state’ diyen şık niceleyiciyi ve olumsuzluğu değiştirir.

exercises.question: Unlike plants, which depend on sunlight, ----.
options: the bacteria around deep-sea vents obtain energy from chemical compounds
because sunlight never reaches the ocean floor
which were discovered near the Galápagos Islands in 1977
although tube worms have neither a mouth nor a gut
photosynthesis takes place only in shallow water
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the bacteria around deep-sea vents obtain energy from chemical compounds’: ‘Unlike plants’ bitkilerle karşılaştırılabilecek bir özne ve ana cümle ister. ‘because’ ile başlayan şık ana cümle kurmaz; ‘which’ ile başlayan şık ana cümle değildir; ‘although’ ile başlayan şık yan cümle olduğu için cümleyi tamamlamaz; ‘shallow’ geçen şıkta özne (fotosentez) bitkilerle karşılaştırılabilecek bir canlı değildir.

exercises.question: The glycaemic index of a food can change ----.
options: unless it contains any carbohydrate at all
depending on how the food has been processed and cooked
which was proposed by David Jenkins in 1981
so that it contains no fibre at all
since glucose is given a value of 100
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘depending on how the food has been processed and cooked’: metne göre işleme ve pişirme yöntemi indeksi değiştirir. ‘unless’ ile başlayan şık anlamsız bir koşul kurar; ‘which’ ile başlayan şık yanlış ismi niteler; ‘fibre’ geçen şık amaç bildirir ve anlamsızdır; ‘since’ ile başlayan şık değişmenin nedenini açıklamaz, yalnızca ölçeğin tanımıdır.

exercises.question: ----, William ordered a survey of almost every county in his kingdom.
options: Although he had never visited England
Unless the survey had already been completed
Whose findings were later called the Domesday Book
Less than twenty years after he had conquered England
So that historians could compare it with the Last Judgement
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Less than twenty years after he had conquered England’: zaman öbeği cümleyi doğru ve metinle uyumlu biçimde tamamlar. ‘Although’ ile başlayan şık hem metinle çelişir hem zıtlık kuramaz; ‘Unless’ ile başlayan şık anlamsız bir koşuldur; ‘Whose’ ile başlayan şık niteleyecek isim bulamaz; ‘historians’ geçen şık metinde olmayan, mantıksız bir amaç bildirir.
